area: CLAUDE.md, memory, rule files, path scoping, imports, /doctor, /init, managed CLAUDE.md, auto-memory

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced config
facts.behavior: Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead. CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt itself; there's no guarantee of strict compliance, especially for vague or conflicting instructions.
facts.limits: No enforcement. Instructions that must run at a specific point (before every commit, after each edit) should be hooks. For system-prompt-level instructions use --append-system-prompt (suited to scripts, not interactive use).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (CLAUDE.md vs auto memory; Troubleshoot: Claude isn't following my CLAUDE.md)

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md file locations and load order
facts.behavior: Listed broadest to most specific so a project instruction appears in context after a user instruction: Managed policy (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md; Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md; Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md), User (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), Project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), Local (./CLAUDE.local.md, add to .gitignore).
facts.limits: CLAUDE.local.md is personal and not committed unless you commit it; gitignored CLAUDE.local.md only exists in the worktree where it was created.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Choose where to put CLAUDE.md files)

facts.behavior: Loads CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md from the current working directory and every directory above it. All discovered files are concatenated rather than overriding; ordered from filesystem root down to working directory, so closer files are read last. Within a directory CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: No override semantics: conflicting instructions across files, Claude may pick one arbitrarily.

facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md in subdirectories under the working directory are not loaded at launch; each loads once Claude reads, writes, or edits another file in that subdirectory. Reading includes a Bash command that counts as a read (cat or head on a single file). A 'Loaded' line with its path appears in the terminal. They do not appear under Memory files in /context.
facts.limits: Not loaded at launch. Doc defers to the worktrees page for files inside a worktree under .claude/worktrees/ (not fetched here, so that behavior is unverified). To test a new nested file, create it from the shell rather than asking Claude to write it.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (How CLAUDE.md files load; Claude isn't following my CLAUDE.md)

facts.behavior: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file; longer files consume more context and reduce adherence. Claude Code loads a CLAUDE.md file of up to 4 MiB in full and skips a larger file. If an instruction file is over the recommended length you see a warning at startup and when you run /status; also a warning when files each within the length add up past a combined limit at session start. Each CLAUDE.md, rules file, and @path import counts as a separate file.
facts.limits: 200 lines is a recommendation (warning only); 4 MiB is a hard skip. The 200-line/25KB truncation applies only to auto-memory MEMORY.md, not CLAUDE.md. Exact combined-limit number not stated.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Write effective instructions; How it works; My CLAUDE.md is too large)

facts.behavior: Write concrete verifiable instructions ('Use 2-space indentation'); group under markdown headers and bullets; review CLAUDE.md, nested CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules periodically to remove outdated or conflicting instructions. Add to CLAUDE.md when Claude repeats a mistake, review catches something, same correction typed again, or a new teammate would need it. Multi-step procedures or single-area entries belong in a skill or path-scoped rule.
facts.limits: Guidance only.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (When to add to CLAUDE.md; Write effective instructions)

facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md files can import files with @path/to/import; imports are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the importing file. Relative and absolute paths allowed; relative paths resolve relative to the containing file. Recursive imports to a maximum depth of four hops. Spaces in paths need a backslash before each space; quoted paths are not imported. Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks (wrap `@README` in backticks to keep it literal).
facts.limits: Imports organize but do not reduce context cost, since imported files also load at launch. Max depth four hops.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Import additional files; Write effective instructions)

facts.behavior: An import in a project-level memory file is external when its path resolves outside the working directory (for example @~/...). First time Claude Code encounters external imports in a project it shows an approval dialog listing the files; if declined, imports stay disabled and the dialog doesn't appear again. User-scope files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/rules/) load imports without the dialog, except in Cowork desktop sessions, where imports resolving outside the working directory are skipped and a symlinked ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is skipped.
facts.limits: Applies to project-level files; user-scope files are trusted.

facts.behavior: Block-level HTML comments (<!-- maintainer notes -->) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before content is injected into Claude's context. Comments inside code blocks are preserved. When opened directly with the Read tool, comments remain visible.
facts.limits: Block-level only; not stripped in code blocks.

facts.behavior: By default, CLAUDE.md files from --add-dir directories are not loaded. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 loads CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, and CLAUDE.local.md from them (CLAUDE.local.md skipped if local excluded from --setting-sources).
facts.limits: Off by default; AGENTS.md in added directories does not load even with the variable set.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Load from additional directories; Where AGENTS.md differs)

facts.behavior: Place markdown files in .claude/rules/, one topic per file. All .md files are discovered recursively (subdirectories allowed). Rules without paths frontmatter load at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md. Rules load into context every session or when matching files are opened.
facts.limits: Project rules are skipped if 'project' is excluded from --setting-sources (before v2.1.211 on-demand rules still loaded). For task-specific instructions not needed always, use skills.

facts.behavior: YAML frontmatter 'paths' field scopes a rule to glob patterns. A path-scoped rule loads when Claude uses Read, Write, or Edit on a matching file, or views a matching file with a Bash command that counts as a read (cat or head on a single file). Works through symlinked paths to the project dir. Accepts a YAML list or comma-separated string. Brace expansion supported; a rule's paths list shares a budget of 1,000 expanded patterns and 4 MiB, over-budget patterns used unexpanded (literal braces match nothing). Invalid bracket patterns match nothing while other patterns keep working.
facts.limits: Triggered by file access, not at launch; a path-scoped rule that hasn't matched a file since compaction is not present. 'paths' is the only frontmatter field Claude Code reads from a rule; other fields are ignored without error. Frontmatter is removed before loading. Unparseable YAML: frontmatter ignored and rule loads as if unscoped (see claude --debug). Unscoped rules apply to all files.

facts.behavior: The .claude/rules/ directory supports symlinks; circular symlinks are detected and handled. A symlink whose target is outside the working directory is treated like an external import: linked rules don't load until the project's external imports are approved, and then only those without a paths field load. Network-path symlinks (UNC, /net, /Network) are not followed.
facts.limits: Path-scoped rules via external symlinks do not load even after approval. Shared rules in ~/.claude/rules/ avoid the approval.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Share rules across projects with symlinks)

facts.behavior: Personal rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on the machine. Loaded before project rules, so a project rule appears later in context. Neither set overrides the other; on conflict Claude may follow either.
facts.limits: No precedence guarantee.

facts.behavior: Deployed at the managed policy path (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md, Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md) and applies to all users on a machine, every session in every repository. Cannot be excluded by individual settings or claudeMdExcludes. Loads before user and project CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: Behavioral guidance, not a hard enforcement layer; technical enforcement belongs in managed settings (permissions.deny, sandbox.enabled, env, forceLoginMethod). Repo-specific guidance should be a committed project CLAUDE.md.

facts.behavior: The claudeMd key puts managed CLAUDE.md content directly inside managed-settings.json instead of a separate file. Same precedence as a managed CLAUDE.md file.
facts.limits: Honored in managed and policy settings only; in user, project, or local settings it has no effect.

facts.behavior: Skips specific CLAUDE.md or rules files by absolute-path glob. Configurable at any settings layer (user, project, local, managed); arrays merge across layers. For symlinked rules files a pattern matching either the .claude/rules path or the link target excludes it (v2.1.239+).
facts.limits: Managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded.

facts.feature: AGENTS.md reading and Project instructions setting
facts.behavior: Claude reads AGENTS.md by default only when there is no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above (v2.1.277+). ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, managed CLAUDE.md, and .claude/rules/ do not count. /config 'Project instructions' values: claude-md-or-agents-md (default), claude-md-and-agents-md, claude-md, managed-only. managed-only loads only managed CLAUDE.md and auto memory at launch (user/project/local CLAUDE.md, rules, AGENTS.md left out; subdirectory CLAUDE.md, rules and path-scoped rules still load on demand). Set via pluginConfigs cc-plugin-agents-md@builtin (read from ~/.claude/settings.json, --settings, or managed settings; ignored in project/local).
facts.limits: Not read: AGENTS.local.md, AGENTS.override.md, anything under .agents/. AGENTS.md read via the setting does not fire InstructionsLoaded hooks and its external @imports load without prompt if previously approved. Unavailable on versions before v2.1.277, if built-in plugin disabled, or sometimes first session after upgrade. Adding CLAUDE.local.md stops AGENTS.md being read by default.

facts.behavior: Put @AGENTS.md in a CLAUDE.md, with Claude-specific instructions below; or ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md. Importing never makes Claude read AGENTS.md twice.
facts.limits: Edit and Write tools refuse to write through a symlink (directed to edit the target). On Windows use the import, since symlinks need privileges and Git may check out a one-line text file.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Share one file with other coding tools; Remove an earlier AGENTS.md workaround)

facts.behavior: Generates a starting CLAUDE.md: Claude analyzes the codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions. If a CLAUDE.md exists, /init suggests improvements rather than overwriting. Reads Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/, .cursorrules) and Copilot rules (.github/copilot-instructions.md) and incorporates relevant parts. With CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1: interactive multi-phase flow asking which artifacts to set up (CLAUDE.md files, skills, hooks), explores with a subagent, presents a reviewable proposal before writing, also reads AGENTS.md, .devin/rules/, .windsurf/rules/ or .windsurfrules, .clinerules; choosing the personal option adds CLAUDE.local.md to .gitignore.
facts.limits: Generated file is a starting point to refine with instructions Claude wouldn't discover on its own.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Set up a project CLAUDE.md; Migrate instructions from other tools)

facts.behavior: Brings a supported coding agent's configuration into Claude Code: appends a one-time copy of instruction files such as AGENTS.md to the matching CLAUDE.md and carries over MCP servers, commands, subagents, and skills.
facts.limits: One-time copy, not a live link.

facts.behavior: Run '/doctor prompt-audit' to have Claude check instruction files for outdated or conflicting content: instructions written for older models, references to files or commands that don't exist, and files that contradict each other. Reports findings with proposed edits; nothing changes until you ask Claude to apply them. Default scope: CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md, plus rules, skills, commands, subagents, output styles under .claude/ and ~/.claude/; pass a path to audit one file or directory.
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.283+. Runs through the bundled /claude-api skill; unavailable if that skill is turned off in skillOverrides or disableBundledSkills. On-demand, not automatic.

facts.behavior: The /doctor checkup proposes trims for a checked-in CLAUDE.md: it cuts content Claude can derive from the codebase (directory layouts, dependency lists, architecture overviews) and keeps pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from tool defaults.
facts.limits: Proposes only, for a checked-in CLAUDE.md; scope beyond that not stated.

facts.behavior: Lists CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and other memory file locations across user and project scopes (including entries for files that don't exist yet; selecting one creates it), toggles auto memory, and opens the auto memory folder. Lists AGENTS.md Claude read (v2.1.280+). GUI editors open in a separate window.
facts.limits: Does not by itself show launch-loaded rules; use /context for that.

facts.behavior: /context lists loaded CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md under 'Memory files' to confirm a file loaded at launch. If a file is missing, Claude can't see it. An 'Instruction file not loaded' notice may appear (see errors docs). /status shows the over-length warning.
facts.limits: Nested subdirectory CLAUDE.md files do not appear there until loaded.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Set up a project CLAUDE.md; Troubleshoot)

facts.behavior: Logs which CLAUDE.md and rules files are loaded, when, and why; useful for debugging path-specific rules and lazy-loaded subdirectory files.
facts.limits: Does not fire for AGENTS.md read through the Project instructions setting (fires for one a CLAUDE.md imports or symlinks to).

facts.behavior: Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it. Nested CLAUDE.md files and rules with paths frontmatter load again on demand.
facts.limits: Instructions given only in conversation, in a nested CLAUDE.md not yet reloaded, or in a path-scoped rule not matched since are lost.

facts.feature: Auto memory: what it is and what it saves
facts.behavior: Notes Claude writes itself across sessions. Four kinds recorded in a type frontmatter field: user, feedback, project, reference. Claude skips anything derivable from the codebase and anything CLAUDE.md files already say, and doesn't save every session; it decides based on future usefulness.
facts.limits: Judgment of Claude; nothing forces a save. Auto memory is context, not enforced.

facts.behavior: On by default in local sessions. Toggle in /memory (saves autoMemoryEnabled to ~/.claude/settings.json); per-project via autoMemoryEnabled in project settings; or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1.
facts.limits: Self-hosted environment sessions default off. In background sessions and sessions started by another Claude Code session the toggle can turn it off but not back on.

facts.feature: Auto memory storage location and sharing
facts.behavior: Per-project directory ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, where <project> is derived from the git repository so all worktrees and subdirectories of the same repo share one directory (outside git, project root). CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME (v2.1.234+) overrides the name. autoMemoryDirectory setting (absolute or ~/ path, any settings scope) relocates it. Contains MEMORY.md index plus one topic file per memory.
facts.limits: Machine-local; not shared across machines or cloud environments. With permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories on, no auto memory is loaded from or saved to a directory chosen by a repository-supplied settings file. Project-settings autoMemoryDirectory is honored under the workspace trust rule.

facts.behavior: The first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that is not loaded at session start. Claude keeps MEMORY.md concise by moving detail into topic files.
facts.limits: Applies only to MEMORY.md, not CLAUDE.md. Topic files (e.g. user_role.md) are not loaded at startup; Claude reads them on demand with standard file tools.

facts.behavior: After Claude writes to MEMORY.md, Claude Code measures it against the 200-line and 25KB limits. Near a limit: reminds Claude to shorten it (one line per entry, move detail into topic files, merge or drop stale entries). Over a limit: the write still succeeds but Claude Code returns an error telling Claude to rewrite the index, because everything past the limit is dropped on next load.
facts.limits: Triggered by Claude's own writes to MEMORY.md; does not block the write; edits made by hand are not described as triggering it.

facts.feature: Auto memory retention and modified timestamp
facts.behavior: Memory files are excluded from the cleanupPeriodDays transcript retention sweep; they stay until you or Claude edit or delete them. When Claude writes a memory file beginning with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records write time in a 'modified' frontmatter field (ISO 8601).
facts.limits: The modified stamp is added only for files that begin with YAML frontmatter.

facts.behavior: Main conversation's auto memory isn't loaded into subagents, except a fork, which inherits the parent conversation and system prompt. A subagent's own auto memory (enabled via the subagent memory field) is a separate directory.
facts.limits: Subagents do not see the parent's MEMORY.md by default.

facts.feature: Asking Claude to remember vs adding to CLAUDE.md
facts.behavior: Asking Claude to remember something ('always use pnpm') saves it to auto memory. To add to CLAUDE.md, ask 'add this to CLAUDE.md' or edit via /memory. 'Saved N memories' / 'Recalled N memories' messages appear when Claude writes/reads the memory directory. Files are plain markdown to edit or delete.
facts.limits: Default destination for 'remember' is auto memory, not CLAUDE.md.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (View and edit with /memory; Auto memory)

facts.behavior: @ file references add CLAUDE.md in the file's directory and parent directories to context. Directory references show listings, not contents. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS=1 (v2.1.299+, ignored in project/local settings) stops @ references including contents.
facts.limits: Directory @ references show file listings only.

facts.behavior: If CLAUDE.md sets commit or PR rules, turn off Claude Code's built-in ones with includeGitInstructions and set attribution text with the attribution setting.
facts.limits: Built-in guidance otherwise coexists with CLAUDE.md.

facts.behavior: A gitignored CLAUDE.local.md exists only in the worktree where it was created. To share personal instructions across worktrees, import a file from home (@~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md), which triggers external-import approval in project files. Auto memory, by contrast, is shared across worktrees of the same repo.
facts.limits: Worktree-specific loading under .claude/worktrees/ is documented on the worktrees page, which was not fetched.

https://code.claude.com/docs/en/debug-your-config, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window (linked from memory.md, not fetched)

area: hooks (events, matchers, blocking semantics, JSON output), permissions, settings layering, managed policy settings

facts.behavior: Five types: command (shell, stdin JSON, exit codes/stdout/stderr), http (POSTs JSON, result from response body), mcp_tool (calls a configured MCP server tool), prompt (single-turn Claude model evaluation returning JSON), agent (subagent with Read/Grep/Glob; 'Experimental and may change'). SessionStart and Setup support only command and mcp_tool.
facts.limits: Not all events support every type. All five types: PermissionDenied, PostToolBatch, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PreToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, TaskCreated, TeammateIdle, UserPromptExpansion, UserPromptSubmit. PermissionRequest: no agent. ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, FileChanged, InstructionsLoaded, MessageDisplay, Notification, PostCompact, PostModelSwitch, PreCompact, PreModelSwitch, SessionEnd, StopFailure, SubagentStart, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove: command/http/mcp_tool only. Command hooks 'can't trigger / commands or tool calls'.

facts.behavior: Events: SessionStart, Setup, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Notification, MessageDisplay, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, Stop, StopFailure, TeammateIdle, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, PreCompact, PostCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, SessionEnd. PreToolUse/PostToolUse also fire for subagent tool calls.
facts.limits: PreToolUse does not fire for @-referenced files inserted into the prompt, or for EndConversation. An unknown hook event name yields a Settings Warning and the entry is skipped.

facts.behavior: '*', '' or omitted matches all. Only letters/digits/_/-/space/,/| => exact string or list separated by | or ,. Any other character => JavaScript regex, unanchored ('Edit.*' matches Edit and NotebookEdit). Tool events match tool_name. MCP tools are mcp__<server>__<tool>; use mcp__memory__.* for a whole server, bare mcp__memory matches nothing. SessionStart matches startup/resume/clear/compact/fork; SessionEnd clear/resume/logout/prompt_input_exit/other; PreCompact/PostCompact manual/auto; ConfigChange user_settings/project_settings/local_settings/policy_settings/skills; Elicitation* match MCP server name; DirectoryAdded slash_command/register_repo_root; PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch match canonical model name.
facts.limits: A matcher on an event without matcher support is 'silently ignored' (no matcher support: CwdChanged, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, MessageDisplay, PostToolBatch). FileChanged and StopFailure accept only letters/digits/_/|. FileChanged matcher doubles as the watch list (split on |, literal filenames in the working directory; regex not useful). PreModelSwitch runs every hook regardless of matcher when canonical name can't be determined.

facts.behavior: Exit 0 = success; stdout parsed as JSON only if a single JSON object (otherwise plain text); 'Claude never sees stderr from a hook that exits 0'. Exit 2 = blocking error on events that can block; stderr is the reason; 'Exit 2 blocks even when your hook prints JSON' and JSON can't override it. Any other code = non-blocking error and the action proceeds; 'If your hook is meant to enforce a policy, use exit 2.' Exit 0 from PreToolUse does not approve the call (normal permission flow still applies).
facts.limits: Exit 2 blocks: PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, Stop, SubagentStop, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated (rolls back), TaskCompleted, ConfigChange (except policy_settings), PreCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostToolBatch, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, WorktreeCreate (any non-zero fails), WorktreeRemove. Exit 2 not honored: PermissionRequest (use decision object), StopFailure, PermissionDenied, Notification, Setup, InstructionsLoaded, DirectoryAdded, MessageDisplay. Shows stderr only: PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart, SessionStart, SessionEnd, CwdChanged, FileChanged, PostCompact, PostModelSwitch.

facts.behavior: command/http hooks accept onFailure 'continue' or 'block' (v2.1.295+). 'block' treats can't-start, exit code other than 0 or 2 (even with allow JSON), HTTP error, timeout, or invalid output as a block. Without it a timed-out PreToolUse hook does not block, and a hook that exits 1 is non-blocking.
facts.limits: No effect on Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, or background hooks. On PreModelSwitch a timeout blocks the switch by default. On UserPromptSubmit a timeout cancels the hook and discards its output but the prompt still reaches Claude unless onFailure: block.

facts.behavior: continue (default true; false stops Claude entirely and takes precedence over event decisions), stopReason, suppressOutput ('Has no effect'), systemMessage (warning shown to user), terminalSequence (allowlisted OSC 0/1/2/9/99/777 and BEL only).
facts.limits: Many events discard continue/systemMessage (e.g. ConfigChange, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionEnd, WorktreeCreate/Remove, Elicitation*, FileChanged/CwdChanged discard continue). additionalContext, systemMessage, initialUserMessage and plain stdout each capped at 10,000 characters; overflow goes to a file with a 2,000-character preview and 'Claude Code doesn't ask Claude to read the file.' Fields with wrong type are dropped (see --debug).

facts.behavior: hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: allow (skips the prompt), deny (prevents the call), ask (prompts the user), defer (ends turn for later resumption). permissionDecisionReason shown to Claude for deny, user for ask. updatedInput replaces the entire input object. additionalContext added to Claude's context. Exit 2 acts as deny. Fires before any permission-mode check, in every mode including dontAsk. A hook 'deny' blocks even in bypassPermissions / --dangerously-skip-permissions.
facts.limits: 'allow' does not bypass deny or ask rules from settings, actions no mode auto-approves, network-path reads, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, or org-ask connector tools. In plan mode 'allow' has no effect on non-read-only calls. defer requires -p mode, ignored interactively, only with a single tool call in the turn. AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode need updatedInput paired with allow. Top-level decision/reason deprecated here (approve->allow, block->deny). Multiple hooks: precedence deny > defer > ask > allow; when several return updatedInput the last to finish wins (non-deterministic).

facts.behavior: Matching hooks for an event run in parallel; every hook runs to completion before results merge. One hook's deny doesn't stop sibling hooks from executing (side effects still happen). additionalContext from every hook is kept. Identical handlers defined in more than one settings file run once; a plugin's or skill's copy stays separate. If more than 12 prompt/agent hooks match, 12 run at once.
facts.limits: Don't rely on one hook's deny to suppress another hook's side effects. Ordering is non-deterministic.

facts.behavior: PostToolUse runs after a tool succeeds; decision:block adds reason next to the result (Claude still sees original output); additionalContext; classifierContext (v2.1.236+); updatedToolOutput replaces what Claude sees. PostToolUseFailure fires when a started tool fails or an MCP tool errors; additionalContext only.
facts.limits: PostToolUse 'can't undo actions since the tool has already executed'; telemetry records original output; updatedToolOutput must match the tool's output shape (mismatch ignored for built-in tools). PostToolUseFailure doesn't fire for unknown tools, validation rejections, permission denials, or cancelled tools.

facts.feature: Stop / SubagentStop hooks and loop cap
facts.behavior: Stop runs when the main agent finishes responding; decision:block with reason (or exit 2) keeps Claude working; stop_hook_active is true when already continuing due to a stop hook. Eight consecutive continuations with no tool call in between: Claude Code overrides the next block and ends the turn (resets on tool call); raise with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP. hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext gives non-error guidance. SubagentStop block delivers reason to the subagent.
facts.limits: Stop fires whenever Claude finishes responding, not only at task completion; does not fire on user interrupt; API errors fire StopFailure (no decision control). Hook script should check stop_hook_active.

facts.behavior: UserPromptSubmit runs before Claude processes a prompt (also on scheduled tasks, background subagent reports, cross-session messages). decision:block with reason or exit 2 blocks; additionalContext, sessionTitle, suppressOriginalPrompt. Plain stdout is injected as a system reminder. UserPromptExpansion can block a user-typed command's expansion. Default timeout 30s.
facts.limits: A blocked prompt is still written to transcript and prompt history; suppressOriginalPrompt only removes it from the block message. Timeout discards output but the prompt still reaches Claude unless onFailure: block.

facts.behavior: Runs when a tool call needs a permission decision. hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior allow/deny; updatedInput and updatedPermissions (allow only, re-checked against rules); message/interrupt (deny only). Runs alongside --permission-prompt-tool / canUseTool; first decision wins. If no hook decides in a session that can't prompt, call is denied. Can answer ExitPlanMode approval (keeps current conversation).
facts.limits: Deny and ask rules still apply to an allow. Exit 2 not honored (use decision object). Agent hooks not supported; prompt ok:false has no effect. Sandboxed network requests don't trigger it.

facts.behavior: Fires only in auto mode when the classifier denies a call (including no-verdict denials). hookSpecificOutput.retry: true tells the model it may retry.
facts.limits: Doesn't fire for manual denials, PreToolUse blocks, or deny rules. Claude Code doesn't reverse the denial; retry ignored for no-verdict denials; prompt/agent hooks' output discarded.

facts.behavior: PostToolBatch fires after a full parallel batch resolves, before next model call; decision:block/exit 2 stops the loop before the next model call. TaskCreated: exit 2 or decision:block deletes the task and returns the message. TaskCompleted/TeammateIdle: exit 2 or {continue:false, stopReason}.
facts.limits: TaskCreated ignores continue:false. No matcher support on these events.

facts.behavior: Fires when a settings file, managed policy file, or skill file changes during a session (matchers user_settings, project_settings, local_settings, policy_settings, skills). Exit 2 or decision:block prevents the change from being applied to the running session.
facts.limits: policy_settings changes cannot be blocked (hook fires for logging, blocking ignored). Fires for managed-settings.json or managed-settings.d/ file changes only; NOT for server-managed settings arrival/refresh, macOS managed preferences, or Windows registry policy. Blocked change surfaces no message to user or Claude (debug log only); 'reason' never shown.

facts.behavior: Fires when a CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/*.md file loads (session start or lazily). Input: file_path, memory_type, load_reason (session_start, nested_traversal, path_glob_match, include, compact), globs, trigger_file_path, parent_file_path. Runs asynchronously for observability.
facts.limits: No decision control; cannot block or modify what loads.

facts.behavior: Fires on startup, resume, clear, compact, fork. Output: additionalContext, initialUserMessage (-p mode only), sessionTitle, watchPaths, reloadSkills. CLAUDE_ENV_FILE available to persist exports for later Bash commands. On resume/fork input includes seconds_since_last_response, context_tokens, prompt_cache_likely_expired, estimated_cache_write_usd (v2.1.251+).
facts.limits: Only command and mcp_tool types. Exit 2 shows stderr only (cannot block). Runs in background at launch/--continue/--resume//clear but Claude's first response waits; if you /clear or switch conversation while background hooks run, nothing they return applies. mcp_tool hooks skipped at launch SessionStart and all Setup events.

facts.behavior: Fires on session end (reasons clear, resume, logout, prompt_input_exit, other). Default budget 1.5 seconds shared across all hooks; raised automatically to the highest per-hook timeout in settings files up to 60s; CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS overrides.
facts.limits: No decision control; can't block termination; JSON output discarded. Plugin-provided hook timeouts don't raise the budget. bypass_permissions_disabled reason removed in v2.1.234.

facts.behavior: PreCompact (matcher manual/auto) can block compaction via exit 2 or decision:block; PostCompact receives compact_summary. Auto-compact blocking: if proactive, compaction is skipped; if triggered to recover from an API context-limit error, the error surfaces and the request fails.
facts.limits: PostCompact has no decision control; systemMessage/continue discarded for both.

facts.behavior: PreModelSwitch (v2.1.251+) runs before a requested model switch (/model, picker, /config, fast mode, SDK set_model); exit 2, decision:block or permissionDecision deny cancels; allow/ask supported; input includes context_tokens, prompt_cache_warm, estimated_cache_write_usd. Precedence deny > ask > allow. Default timeout 30s and a timeout blocks the switch. PostModelSwitch runs after any model change and can add additionalContext.
facts.limits: PreModelSwitch not run for automatic fallback or session-resume restore (PostModelSwitch only). 'ask' only works in interactive /model; elsewhere treated as refusal. PostModelSwitch can't block.

facts.behavior: WorktreeCreate replaces default git worktree creation entirely (e.g. for SVN/Perforce); must print the worktree path (command: last non-empty stdout line) or return hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath (HTTP); failure or no path fails creation. .worktreeinclude is not processed when the hook is configured. WorktreeRemove runs when Claude Code cleans up a hook-created worktree; non-zero exit fails removal if directory still exists. Paths with . / .. segments or passing through a repo symlink are refused (v2.1.216+).
facts.limits: Does not run when Claude runs `git worktree add` via Bash (use a PreToolUse Bash hook). WorktreeRemove not run when a subagent or workflow agent finishes (worktree kept). Claude Code never deletes the branch of a hook-created worktree. Only runs for worktrees a WorktreeCreate hook created.

facts.behavior: FileChanged fires via filesystem watcher on watched files regardless of what changed them (Edit/Write, Bash, external); CwdChanged fires when a shell command changes cwd; both can return watchPaths and use CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. DirectoryAdded fires after /add-dir or SDK register_repo_root, runs in background.
facts.limits: No decision control on any. DirectoryAdded doesn't fire for --add-dir startup flag, /permissions Workspace tab, or already-covered directories. Hook commands run unsandboxed.

facts.behavior: Notification hooks filter by notification_type matcher. MessageDisplay can replace on-screen text only (transcript keeps original). Elicitation hooks can accept/decline/cancel an MCP form programmatically; ElicitationResult can modify or block the user's response; decline from any matching hook overrides accept.
facts.limits: Notification hooks can't block or modify notifications; permission_prompt/idle_prompt only fire after ~6s without typing in terminal sessions. StopFailure and InstructionsLoaded have no decision control. Elicitation: user/server never see why hook declined.

facts.behavior: Permission-rule syntax filter (e.g. "Bash(git *)", "Edit(*.ts)") so a hook process only spawns when the tool call matches; for Bash each subcommand and $()/backtick contents is checked. Holds one rule only (no && or ||).
facts.limits: Only evaluated on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied; on any other event the hook 'never runs'. Best-effort: when Claude Code can't determine which commands Bash runs, it runs the hook anyway; docs say use the permission system, not a hook, to enforce a hard allow/deny.

facts.behavior: Default timeout: 600s for command/http/mcp_tool, 30s prompt, 60s agent; 30s for command/http/mcp_tool on UserPromptSubmit/PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch; 10s MessageDisplay; SessionEnd 1.5s budget. A timed-out hook is cancelled and output discarded. async:true runs in background (timeout not enforced); asyncRewake wakes Claude on exit 2. `once` removes a hook after first successful run.
facts.limits: `once` only honored in skill frontmatter. Async output delivered on next conversation turn; each execution is a separate background process. A hook that prints allow then backgrounds a process without redirecting stdout/stderr is blocked ('refusing to honor the suspect capture').

facts.behavior: prompt hooks send hook input to a Claude model (default: the background-functionality model) and expect {ok, reason, impossible}; ok:false on Stop/SubagentStop feeds reason back and continues (unless impossible:true); on PreToolUse denies the call (turn ends by default; continueOnBlock:true returns reason to Claude); on PostToolUse ends turn unless continueOnBlock. agent hooks spawn a verifier with Read/Grep/Glob.
facts.limits: PermissionRequest and PermissionDenied: ok:false has no effect. PostToolUseFailure/TaskCreated: reason returned as tool error regardless of continueOnBlock. Agent hooks experimental, not supported on PermissionRequest.

facts.behavior: HTTP: POSTs JSON; 2xx empty = success; 2xx JSON parsed; headers support $VAR interpolation only for allowedEnvVars; allowedHttpHookUrls and httpHookAllowedEnvVars restrict. mcp_tool: calls a configured MCP tool, input supports ${path} substitution; never starts an OAuth flow.
facts.limits: Non-2xx / connection failure = non-blocking error unless onFailure: block. Starting MCP servers waited on only for blocking events, up to MCP_TIMEOUT.

facts.behavior: Hooks defined in ~/.claude/settings.json (all projects), .claude/settings.json (project, shareable), .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored), managed policy settings, plugin hooks/hooks.json, skill frontmatter (rest of session once invoked), subagent frontmatter (while running). Hooks from settings, managed policy and plugins also run inside subagents with agent_id/agent_type. Hook entries merge across settings levels. Edits are picked up by the file watcher.
facts.limits: Subagent frontmatter Stop converts to SubagentStop. Frontmatter hooks in project subagents run only after workspace trust accepted; -p doesn't count. Cloud sessions don't read local ~/.claude/settings.json. Cloud threads in a project ignore a repo's .claude/settings.json hooks. Hooks load from the cwd's .claude/ with no parent-directory fallback.

facts.behavior: Interactive sessions hold back hooks from every settings file, including ~/.claude/settings.json, until the workspace trust dialog is accepted for the folder or a trusted parent.
facts.limits: -p / SDK sessions never show the dialog and treat the folder as trusted, so hooks in a repo's .claude/settings.json run in a never-trusted folder. Mitigate with --bare, --setting-sources user, or --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'.

facts.behavior: disableAllHooks: true disables hooks; precedence follows settings order so a project false overrides a user true; --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' beats project/local. /hooks menu is a read-only browser showing each hook's source.
facts.limits: 'No way to disable an individual hook while keeping it in the configuration' (delete the entry). disableAllHooks set below managed level can't disable managed hooks.

facts.behavior: allowManagedHooksOnly blocks user, project, local and plugin hooks; exempt: hooks from plugins force-enabled in managed enabledPlugins. Also narrows statusLine, fileSuggestion, subagentStatusLine to managed settings and disables command-source plugins unless disableCommandPluginSources is explicitly false. allowedHttpHookUrls (when defined at any level, HTTP hooks run only for matching URLs, merged) and httpHookAllowedEnvVars.
facts.limits: Managed-only lock; under managedSourcesBehavior merge takes strictest value.

facts.behavior: Common input: session_id, prompt_id, transcript_path, cwd, scratchpad_dir, permission_mode, effort, hook_event_name (+agent_id/agent_type in subagents). Env: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (stays at session-start root even in worktrees), CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, CLAUDE_ENV_FILE (SessionStart/CwdChanged/FileChanged), CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE. OTEL_* vars removed from hook subprocesses. cwd in input follows Claude into worktrees and after cd.
facts.limits: Transcript file is written asynchronously and may lag (use last_assistant_message). No $CLAUDE_MODEL; $ANTHROPIC_MODEL doesn't change on /model. Hooks can't open /dev/tty. Stderr from exit-0 hooks not shown to Claude. additionalContext is saved in transcript and replayed on resume.

facts.behavior: Rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow; first match decides; specificity doesn't change order. A broad deny (Bash(aws *)) beats a narrower allow; a matching ask prompts even when a more specific allow matches. Deny at any settings level can't be overridden by another level or by --allowedTools; --disallowedTools can add restrictions beyond managed.
facts.limits: Rules are enforced by Claude Code, not the model; CLAUDE.md/prompt instructions 'don't change what Claude Code allows'.

facts.behavior: A deny rule with a bare tool name (Bash, Bash(*), or tool-name glob like mcp__*) removes the tool from Claude's context entirely; scoped rules like Bash(rm *) leave the tool and block matching calls. Deny/ask accept tool-name globs ('*', 'mcp__*'); allow globs only after literal mcp__<server>__ prefix.
facts.limits: EndConversation cannot be removed by deny while any other tool remains and ask never prompts for it. Unanchored allow globs are skipped. Deny/ask rule with unknown tool name gives a startup warning (names containing _ or * exempt).

facts.behavior: Bash rules match whole command text; * matches any text incl. spaces; trailing ' *' (or :*) also matches the bare command; the space before * is significant (Bash(ls*) matches lsof). Compound commands split on && || ; | |& & newline and each subcommand must match an allow rule; deny/ask apply if any subcommand (incl. in $(), subshells, loops) matches. Fixed wrapper set stripped before matching: timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob, flagless xargs; known-safe env var assignments stripped for allow, any assignment stripped for deny/ask.
facts.limits: Not a security boundary: Bash(curl *) doesn't stop /usr/bin/curl or sh -c 'curl ...'; Bash(git push *) doesn't stop `git -C . push`. Wrapper list not configurable; npx, docker exec, devbox run, direnv exec not stripped. Argument-constraining patterns are 'fragile'. Startup warning for allow rule with * before the subcommand. Trailing && makes command unparseable (allow doesn't match). Use sandbox or PreToolUse hook for hard enforcement.

facts.behavior: A built-in set (ls, cat, echo, pwd, head, tail, grep, find, wc, which, diff, stat, du, cd, read-only git forms) runs without a prompt in every mode; not configurable; add ask/deny rule to require a prompt. Output redirects, tee targets (v2.1.269+) and input redirects (v2.1.257+) are checked against Edit/Read rules, protected paths and working dirs.
facts.limits: Still prompts for unquoted globs with write-capable flags, docker with another daemon, file -m/-f, ps with env option, unparseable commands, commands over 10,000 characters, writes to special shell vars (PATH, IFS), cd+git into a different dir. Redirect targets /dev/null, fd forms, here-docs unchecked.

facts.behavior: A prefix rule like Bash(watch *) or Bash(find *) can't auto-approve exec wrappers (watch, setsid, ionice, flock) or find with -exec/-delete/-rm/-fprint/-files0-from; in Manual mode they prompt. Exact-match rule (no *) or a PreToolUse allow hook can approve.
facts.limits: A find command containing * is read as a wildcard pattern, not exact.

facts.behavior: Edit rules apply to all built-in file-editing tools; Read rules are applied 'best-effort' to built-in readers (Grep, Glob), @file mentions, pasted image paths, directory listings, IDE context. Read and Edit deny rules also apply to recognized Bash file commands (cat, head, tail, sed, tee) and redirect targets. A Read deny also blocks Edit/Write on the path (Write check v2.1.228+). Gitignore pattern syntax: //path absolute, ~/path home, /path relative to settings source, path or ./path relative to cwd. In deny/ask, single-segment 'src/**' matches at any depth; in allow it matches only <cwd>/src.
facts.limits: Do not apply to commands that read without naming files (grep -r pattern .) or arbitrary subprocesses (Python/Node scripts); use sandbox for OS-level enforcement. NotebookEdit not covered by Read deny. Path rules for Write/NotebookEdit/Glob/MultiEdit are accepted but never consulted (startup warning); use Edit()/Read(). .claudeignore has no effect. Single-leading-slash /path is NOT filesystem-absolute. A ! negation carve-out only affects same-source rules and cannot reopen files in a wholly-blocked directory.

facts.behavior: Permission check covers both requested path and resolved target. Allow rules need both to match; deny rules apply if either matches. Edit/Write refuse writes where the path itself is a symlink and direct Claude to the target; unresolvable/looping paths are refused.
facts.limits: Writes can still pass through a symlinked parent directory or via Bash/PowerShell; those resolve against working dirs and protected paths (not auto-approved in acceptEdits if resolving outside working dirs; prompt in auto mode). Before v2.1.268 deny rules written through a symlinked dir didn't apply to the real path.

facts.feature: WebFetch, MCP, Agent, Cd and parameter rules
facts.behavior: WebFetch(domain:host) matches hostname, case-insensitive, * wildcards (v2.1.172+); bare WebFetch deny removes tool, WebFetch(domain:*) deny keeps tool and refuses each fetch and also feeds sandbox allow/deny list. MCP: mcp__server, mcp__server__*, mcp__server__tool; allow rules with parentheses on mcp__ tools are skipped. Agent(Name) controls subagents. Cd rules (deny/allow) control /cd targets. Tool(param:value) deny/ask rules match one scalar top-level input parameter exactly (e.g. Agent(model:opus), Agent(isolation:worktree), Bash(run_in_background:true)).
facts.limits: Param rules can't match primary content fields (command, file_path, path, notebook_path, url); such rules ignored with startup warning. Omitted params never match. Nested fields not matchable. Any Cd allow rule switches /cd to allowlist mode; Cd is not model-invocable. Bare WebFetch deny doesn't apply to artifact reads. Org-ask connector tools prompt every call even in auto/bypass.

facts.behavior: default (Manual; prompts on first use of each tool), acceptEdits (auto-accepts edits and mkdir/touch/mv/cp in working dir or additionalDirectories), plan (read-only exploration, no source edits), auto (background classifier reviews actions), dontAsk (auto-denies every call that would prompt; pre-approved tools and no-approval reads still run), bypassPermissions (skips prompts). Auto mode is the built-in starting mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions on v2.1.283+. claude -p and SDK runs with no mode set start in Manual from v2.1.302 and deny calls needing approval.
facts.limits: permissions.defaultMode auto and bypassPermissions don't take effect from project or local settings (user/managed or --permission-mode only). Cannot enter bypassPermissions from a session not started with it enabled. permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode / disableAutoMode = 'disable' works from any scope (most useful managed). In interactive terminal sessions with bypass available, plan mode's blocks aren't enforced.

facts.behavior: Even in bypassPermissions: tools matched by an explicit ask rule; org-ask connector tools; AskUserQuestion and requiresUserInteraction MCP tools; rm/rmdir targeting a critical path (no allow rule or PreToolUse allow approves it); cross-session messaging safeguards; reads outside working dirs when permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories is on (v2.1.257+).
facts.limits: A matching deny rule still blocks critical-path removals outright. Critical paths: filesystem root, top-level dirs, home, working directory and its parents, additional dirs' parents (only for globs), rm -rf "$VAR"/* forms. In auto/bypass the prompt has a two-minute countdown then denies (v2.1.281+; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DANGEROUS_RM_TIMEOUT=1 turns off).

facts.behavior: Writes to protected paths are never auto-approved except in bypassPermissions (and interactive plan with bypass available): prompted in default/acceptEdits, routed to classifier in auto, denied in dontAsk. Protected dirs: .git, .config/git, .vscode, .idea, .husky, .cargo, .devcontainer, .yarn, .mvn, .claude (exceptions: .claude/worktrees/, the session's own plan files, background session scratch dir, Markdown files in project auto-memory dir and subagent memory dir when not --restricted). Protected files include .gitconfig, .gitmodules, shell rc files (.bashrc, .zshrc, .profile, .envrc ...), .npmrc, .yarnrc*, .pre-commit-config.yaml, lefthook.*, .mcp.json, .claude.json, .ripgreprc, pyrightconfig.json, etc.
facts.limits: permissions.allow rules in settings do NOT pre-approve protected-path writes (the safety check runs before allow rules); only a session-scoped prompt option for the project .claude/ or ~/.claude/. With --restricted (v2.1.248+) the classifier can't approve them.

facts.behavior: If the classifier blocks 3 times in a row or 20 total, auto mode pauses and prompting resumes; blocked actions listed under /permissions Recently denied. No verdict from classifier or server: action is denied; stops turn after ten server no-verdicts in a row. In non-interactive -p runs with no prompt tool, hitting a threshold means the action doesn't run and Claude keeps working.
facts.limits: Thresholds (3 and 20) not configurable. PreToolUse/PermissionDenied hooks interplay: PermissionDenied only fires for auto mode.

facts.behavior: Claude has access to files in the launch directory (primary working directory until /cd). Extend with --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories. Files in additional dirs follow same rules; reads without prompts. /cd moves the primary dir and applies the new dir's project settings, hooks, MCP, plugins, env after a trust prompt. permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories makes file tools refuse out-of-fence paths in every mode.
facts.limits: Additional directories grant file access, not configuration: only --add-dir/ /add-dir (not settings additionalDirectories) load skills, commands, subagents, enabledPlugins/extraKnownMarketplaces; CLAUDE.md/rules only with CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1. Network paths can't be added as working directories. Hooks and settings.json keys load from cwd's .claude/ with no parent fallback; settings.local.json loads from git repo root (v2.1.211+).

facts.feature: PreToolUse hooks vs mods and rules precedence
facts.behavior: PreToolUse hook decisions don't bypass permission rules: deny and ask rules are evaluated regardless of hook output. A blocking hook (exit 2) stops the call before permission rules are evaluated, even if an allow rule would permit it. With managed settings or Team/Enterprise /login, mod approvals can't override deny rules, ask rules, or PreToolUse blocks.
facts.limits: With neither managed settings nor Team/Enterprise login (API key or long-lived OAuth token), an installed mod's tool.check approval can override a deny rule or PreToolUse block. Mod approval can't approve non-read-only calls in plan mode.

facts.behavior: Permissions control which tools/files/domains Claude Code can use; sandboxing gives OS-level enforcement for Bash, PowerShell, Monitor commands and children. Sandbox paths/domains and permission rules merge into the final sandbox config. With sandbox on and autoAllowBashIfSandboxed true (default), sandboxed Bash runs without prompting even under a bare Bash ask rule (not in plan mode; content-scoped ask rules still prompt).
facts.limits: Permissions alone don't constrain subprocesses; docs recommend both for defense-in-depth.

facts.feature: Workspace trust for project permission rules
facts.behavior: permissions.allow and permissions.additionalDirectories in a project .claude/settings.json apply only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted; deny and ask rules apply immediately. Trust is keyed on git repo root (main checkout for worktrees). .claude/settings.local.json allow rules apply without trust unless the file is tracked in git or .claude is a symlink.
facts.limits: -p / SDK never show the dialog; allow rules/additionalDirectories not used and a stderr warning printed. Home-directory starts hold trust for session only. Hooks, env, helper commands in settings files are used (not gated) when a parent folder is trusted or in -p.

facts.behavior: Bash and WebFetch-domain approvals save an allow rule permanently to .claude/settings.local.json at the git repo root, resolved through worktrees to the main checkout (v2.1.211+); file edits last until session end. Compound-command approvals save a rule per subcommand (up to 5). Claude Code adds **/.claude/settings.local.json to the global git excludes on first write.
facts.limits: Stays with .claude/settings.json outside a git repo, when root is home, on Windows, or when ownership check fails. Some prompts offer only one-time approval. An allow rule in local doesn't outrank an ask rule from project or managed.

facts.behavior: Four scopes: User ~/.claude/settings.json; Shared project .claude/settings.json (commit it); Project local .claude/settings.local.json (personal); Managed (managed-settings.json, MDM, server-managed). ~/.claude.json is a separate file Claude Code writes itself (sign-in, MCP configs, per-project trust, global config keys). CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates user files. Settings files are strict JSON (comments/trailing commas are errors).
facts.limits: Project .claude/settings.json is read from the session's primary working directory (start at repo root). Some keys never take effect from a repo file (scope column in settings index: User, User or managed, Managed, Global config, etc.). Cloud sessions don't read user or local files; hosted multi-repo sessions read only enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces from each repo.

facts.behavior: Highest to lowest: Managed, command line (--settings), project local, shared project, user. Higher level wins for the same key. Lists such as permissions.allow merge (combine) across files rather than override. Exceptions with own rules: fallbackModel (whole value from highest), modelPicker (managed/--settings/user only), availableModels (managed list applied as-is), modelSettings. Env vars are not a level; ANTHROPIC_MODEL overrides model key, decided per pair. An env block in a settings file follows the levels.
facts.limits: --settings can't set Managed or Global config keys. Deny at any scope beats allow at any scope. Telemetry export vars in env don't take effect from project/local settings.

facts.feature: Exceptions to managed precedence (stricter lower-level wins)
facts.behavior: A restrictive lower-level value still counts over managed for: disableClaudeAiConnectors true (any scope), enableArtifact false/disableArtifact true (any scope), isolatePeerMachines true, permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories true (v2.1.257+), autoMode.classifyAllShell true (user or --settings), remoteControlAtStartup false (project/local), crossSessionInbound stricter value, useAutoModeDuringPlan/syncClaudeAiSkills/syncClaudeAiPlugins false, maxEffortLevel lower cap (v2.1.267+).
facts.limits: Only these listed keys; a looser project/local value is ignored.

facts.behavior: Claude Code watches settings files and reloads without restart, including permissions, hooks, apiKeyHelper; a file created mid-session loads if its folder existed. /status shows 'Setting sources' (files loaded, managed source and how delivered); claude doctor lists rejected entries; /permissions lists rules and their source file and applies changes from the next tool call.
facts.limits: Some keys read once at session start (e.g. requiredMinimumVersion, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh). /status doesn't show which file supplied each key. MDM/console managed settings arrive on a schedule (server-managed polled hourly, MDM checked every 30 min), not on save.

facts.behavior: Settings Error (invalid JSON or schema-rejected value in user/project/local file): interactive dialog to fix, exit, or continue without. Settings Warning: individual entries (malformed permission rule, unknown hook event) are skipped and the rest kept. Managed settings: rest of file enforced, invalid entries dropped, some keys fall back to stricter value.
facts.limits: -p runs show no dialog; use claude doctor. A managed document that isn't valid JSON is a separate error.

facts.behavior: Four: server-managed (claude.ai console or Claude apps gateway; fetched at startup and polled hourly), MDM/OS policy (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode plist; Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode Settings value; checked every 30 min), file-based managed-settings.json (+ managed-settings.d/*.json, managed-mcp.json) at /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, /etc/claude-code/, C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\ (reloaded on file change), HKCU registry (Windows/WSL, used only when no admin document present). Applies to terminal, VS Code/JetBrains, desktop Code tab, Agent SDK.
facts.limits: Legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode path not read. Device MDM/file doesn't reach Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions (server-managed does); Cowork never fetches server-managed settings. claude.ai console can't target a group yet. Server-managed changes to hooks/env wait for developer approval dialog in interactive sessions. Server-managed only reaches already-authenticated accounts and is treated as convenience, not enforcement, for machines you can't reach by device management.

facts.behavior: Default managedSourcesBehavior 'first-wins': highest-ranked source delivering at least one policy key wins (order: remote/server-managed, MDM/OS, managed files with managed-settings.d merged over/with managed-settings.json, HKCU) and lower sources are ignored with no warning; /status names used and skipped sources. 'merge' (v2.1.242+) applies every admin source: lists union, locks take strictest, restriction allowlists taken whole from highest source. A few keys (sandbox locks, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, deniedMcpServers, env per-variable, maxEffortLevel, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, etc.) are read from every admin source regardless.
facts.limits: managed-settings.d: files merged alphabetically after managed-settings.json; scalars later wins, lists combine deduped, nested blocks merge key by key; hidden and non-.json files ignored. Under merge, set managedSourcesBehavior in highest-ranked source only. policyHelper output becomes the only managed settings.

facts.behavior: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly makes managed settings the only source of permission rules (drops allow rules from user/project/local, --allowedTools, host parent settings). allowManagedHooksOnly (hooks), allowManagedMcpServersOnly (MCP allowlist), strictKnownMarketplaces / blockedMarketplaces, availableModels / deniedModels, forceLoginMethod / forceLoginOrgUUID, allowedProviders (v2.1.285+), permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode / disableAutoMode, requiredMinimumVersion, sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly / sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly.
facts.limits: A managed model is a starting default, not a lock; the locks are availableModels and deniedModels. forceLoginOrgUUID is not checked for Console credentials after login; claude setup-token and /install-github-app enforce only forceLoginMethod. requiredMinimumVersion blocks outdated binaries from starting but doesn't end a running session. Admin-console-only allowedProviders is 'a convenience... not enforcement'.

facts.behavior: Hosts such as Claude Desktop/IDE/Agent SDK can pass managed policy via SDK managedSettings option. By default Claude Code ignores parent settings when any admin source is present; parentSettingsBehavior: 'merge' (set in highest-priority managed source) keeps only the host's restrictive values.
facts.limits: Unless allowManaged*Only locks are set, the host's permission allow rules and sandbox allowlists still apply. allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly drops parent-supplied allow rules and additionalDirectories.

facts.behavior: Credential order: cloud provider vars (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, Anthropic profile/federation, /login subscription OAuth. Gateway session outranks provider selection. With forceLoginMethod/forceLoginOrgUUID, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN/apiKeyHelper are blocked at startup.
facts.limits: Cloud sessions always use subscription credentials. apiKeyHelper not used by Claude Desktop or cloud sessions; warns if >10s. /login expiry warning 3 days ahead is informational and never blocks.

facts.feature: What runs before folder trust (-p / SDK / parent-trusted)
facts.behavior: Table of repo-supplied content: hooks in settings files, env block, helper commands (apiKeyHelper) and project skill hooks/allowed-tools are used even with only a parent folder trusted or in -p; permissions.allow/additionalDirectories not used until trust; frontmatter hooks in project subagents, @skills-dir plugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, inline subagent mcpServers not used; .mcp.json servers ask in parent-trusted case but connect without asking in -p/SDK; headersHelper not run.
facts.limits: Skill allowed-tools is never gated by workspace trust in any session. --bare reads no project hooks/skills/commands/subagents/plugins/.mcp.json but project env block and helpers like awsAuthRefresh still apply.
