area: Plugins, plugin components, marketplaces, plugin validate, plugin details and token cost, whether plugins can ship rules or CLAUDE.md

facts.behavior: A plugin is 'a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit.' Component types: skills, commands (older format, 'write new ones as skills'), agents, hooks (hooks/hooks.json), hooks module (a 'mod'), MCP servers (.mcp.json), LSP servers (.lsp.json), monitors, output styles, themes, workflows, bin/ executables, settings.json.
facts.limits: Manifest is optional; without it components are loaded from the standard layout. Only `name` is required in plugin.json. Plugin content is not rules/CLAUDE.md (see separate fact).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference (the /plugins-reference URL now serves the manifest reference)

facts.feature: Plugins cannot ship CLAUDE.md or rules into context
facts.behavior: 'A CLAUDE.md at the plugin root isn't loaded as context, and claude plugin validate warns when it finds one. To include instructions that load into Claude's context, put them in a skill.' The validator warning text is 'CLAUDE.md at the plugin root is not loaded as project context'.
facts.limits: The surveyed pages list no .claude/rules/ or rules component type in the plugin standard layout. The only documented ways a plugin adds instructions are skills, commands, agents, output styles and hooks. A rule that must hold every time should be a hook rather than a skill ('add it to the plugin as a hook rather than a skill').

facts.feature: Plugin manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) fields and unrecognized fields
facts.behavior: `name` is the only required key (kebab-case; no spaces, @, :, path separators; every component is namespaced under it). Other fields: displayName, version, description, author, homepage (must parse as URL or plugin fails to load), repository, license, keywords, metadata, defaultEnabled, dependencies, settings, userConfig, channels, skills, commands, agents, hooks, mcpServers, lspServers, outputStyles, workflows, experimental.{themes,monitors,evals}. An unrecognized top-level key is stripped and the plugin loads; validate reports it as a warning.
facts.limits: userConfig options, channels entries, lspServers configs and monitors entries are strict objects: an unknown key is an error and the plugin does not load. `version` is not checked against semver.

facts.behavior: claude plugin validate errors on plugin names starting with claude-, anthropic-, anthropics-, cc-plugin-; names equal to claude, anthropic, anthropics, claude-code, claude-mods; and 'official' beside claude/anthropic. Warns when claude/anthropic/anthropics is a whole word elsewhere (e.g. mcp-for-claude). `claude plugin init` and `claude plugin tag` refuse a name that draws the error.
facts.limits: 'Claude Code still installs and loads a plugin whose name they refuse.' So not enforced at runtime.

facts.behavior: Every component path in a manifest is relative to the plugin root and must start with ./ ; must resolve inside the plugin root and must exist. A path escaping the plugin root (.., or a symlink leading outside) 'doesn't load' and shows `<component> path escapes plugin directory`. validate errors: 'Path contains ".." which could be a path traversal attempt' and 'Path not found'. On macOS/Linux a path containing a backslash is rejected.
facts.limits: Exception: symlinks between plugins within one marketplace. Files outside the plugin directory are not copied into the cache, so scripts in a copied plugin reading ../shared don't find them. `skills` also accepts "."; `mcpServers` also accepts an https bundle URL.

facts.feature: How manifest component keys combine with default directories
facts.behavior: `commands`, `agents`, `outputStyles`, `workflows`, `experimental.themes`, `experimental.monitors` REPLACE the default folder scan; `skills` ADDS to the default skills/ scan; `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `lspServers` MERGE with hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json, .lsp.json. When a default folder exists and the manifest key replaces it, `claude plugin list` and /plugin warn 'Default <folder>/ folder is ignored because the manifest sets "<key>"'.
facts.limits: A later-declared MCP/LSP server with the same name replaces an earlier one.

facts.behavior: Each skill lives in skills/<name>/SKILL.md and runs as /<plugin>:<directory>; frontmatter `name` replaces only the last segment, plugin prefix stays. A SKILL.md at plugin root with no skills/ dir and no skills key loads as a single skill (set `name` in frontmatter, or a marketplace install names it after the cache directory). Claude reads every skill's description; full text loads only when used.
facts.limits: validate does not check a SKILL.md at the plugin root when run against a plugin directory.

facts.behavior: commands/*.md become /<plugin>:<file>; subdirectory adds a segment. Same frontmatter as skills. 'Commands are the older format, and skills supersede them for new work.' Manifest `commands` can be an object map of name to {source|content, description, argumentHint, model, allowedTools}.
facts.limits: An object-map entry setting both or neither of source/content fails validation.

facts.feature: Plugin agents: supported and ignored frontmatter
facts.behavior: agents/*.md define subagents named <plugin>:<name> (subfolders add segments, e.g. my-plugin:review:security). Supported frontmatter: name, description, model, effort, maxTurns, autoCompactWindow, tools, disallowedTools, skills, memory, background, omitClaudeMd, isolation (only "worktree"), color, and experimental cacheTtl.
facts.limits: Ignored fields in plugin agents: permissionMode, hooks, mcpServers, initialPrompt ('An agent file can't add hooks or MCP servers on its own'). Agent frontmatter that doesn't parse: agent still loads with every field ignored, named after the file, description 'Agent from <plugin> plugin'; validate finds these. Manifest `agents` accepts .md files only, not directories.

facts.behavior: hooks/hooks.json (top-level "hooks" wrapper) and the manifest `hooks` key both load and merge. Hooks 'don't wait for one of the plugin's skills or commands to be used. Claude Code registers them when a session loads the plugin, and they fire on their events from then on.' Hook types: shell command, HTTP, MCP tool, prompt, subagent. Every hook process receives CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>. A plugin's own MCP tools are matched as mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>.
facts.limits: A hooks file without the "hooks" wrapper fails to load. If two enabled plugins share a manifest name, only one registers its hooks/hooks.json hooks (note in /plugin Errors tab, v2.1.296+). Hooks have no model-context cost ('harness-only').

facts.feature: Plugin hooks run outside permission rules and sandbox
facts.behavior: 'Claude Code's permission rules and sandbox cover the tool calls Claude makes, not the code a plugin runs by itself.' Command hooks, monitors, MCP servers, LSP servers and mod processes run with full user permissions outside the sandbox. A plugin's MCP tool calls and Bash commands running bin/ executables are tool calls, so permission rules apply to them.
facts.limits: Plugins can execute arbitrary code with user privileges.

facts.behavior: .mcp.json at plugin root (or `mcpServers` manifest key: path, .mcpb/.dxt bundle path or https URL, inline map, or array). Server appears in /mcp as plugin:<plugin>:<server>; tools named mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool> (use in permission rules and hook matchers). On /reload-plugins unchanged servers keep their connection, changed reconnect, removed disconnect. validate checks .mcp.json (v2.1.281+): errors for entries Claude Code would drop, undeclared ${user_config.KEY}, invalid remote url; warnings for http:///ws:// to non-loopback hosts and literal-credential-looking headers.
facts.limits: A reload that would add/remove a plugin MCP server and invalidate the prompt cache is not applied without `/reload-plugins --force`. MCP server added by a project-scope plugin goes through the same per-server approval as project .mcp.json; MCP bundles and files outside the plugin dir are skipped for project-scope plugins. Per-turn MCP cost follows MCP tool search.

facts.behavior: .lsp.json at root or `lspServers` key; servers map directly (no wrapper). Required: command, extensionToLanguage. Plugin configures the connection but does not install the server binary. Two servers claiming one extension: first registered wins, warning in /plugin Errors tab.
facts.limits: `claude plugin validate` 'doesn't read' .lsp.json (per components page); an invalid entry makes the whole file be skipped at load ('Invalid LSP server config for ".lsp.json"').

facts.behavior: monitors/monitors.json (or experimental.monitors): background shell commands started at session start/reload (or on-skill-invoke:<skill>); output reaches Claude as notifications. Run with full user permissions, outside the sandbox.
facts.limits: Interactive sessions only (never -p); not on Bedrock/Vertex-style/Foundry providers; command cannot reference ${user_config.*} and gets no CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_*; disabling a plugin mid-session does not stop running monitors; monitors do not load for project-scope plugins; top-level `monitors` key still loads with a validate warning.

facts.behavior: Files in bin/ are on the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled, so Claude can run them as bare commands. Plugin bin/ dirs come after the user's own PATH entries, so a plugin cannot shadow git, ls, etc.
facts.limits: Not available to commands run inside the PowerShell sandbox; claude.ai and Cowork don't install a plugin with a top-level bin/. Variables like CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT are not in the environment of commands Claude runs via Bash.

facts.behavior: A settings.json at plugin root or `settings` manifest key applies while the plugin is enabled. 'Only two keys take effect, agent and subagentStatusLine, and every other key is dropped.' `agent` runs the plugin's agent as the session main thread. Precedence: settings.json over manifest `settings`; user settings override plugin defaults (lowest layer); two plugins setting same key: last loaded wins.
facts.limits: A plugin cannot ship permissions, env, hooks-in-settings, model, etc. via settings.json; those keys are dropped.

facts.behavior: output-styles/<name>.md appear in /output-style as <plugin>:<name>; themes/<slug>.json appear in /theme (read-only; edits saved as user copy); workflows/*.js run as /<plugin>:<name>. Manifest keys outputStyles, experimental.themes, workflows replace the folder scan.
facts.limits: Plugins containing a theme, output style, monitor or workflow never show under 'Not used recently'. Top-level `themes` key still loads with a validate warning.

facts.behavior: userConfig declares values prompted when the plugin is enabled; sensitive:true masks input and stores in secure credential store. ${user_config.KEY} substitutes in MCP/LSP config, exec-form hook args, and skill/agent content (sensitive values become a placeholder there). CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> exported to hook processes. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (changes per version; don't write state there), ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (~/.claude/plugins/data/<id>/, persists across updates, deleted on last-scope uninstall unless --keep-data), ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}.
facts.limits: Shell-form hook commands, monitor commands and MCP headersHelper reject ${user_config.*} (error, component does not run). `claude plugin install` never prompts for userConfig; use --config KEY=VALUE or `claude plugin configure --values-stdin`. `options` on a userConfig field requires v2.1.271+.

facts.behavior: `dependencies` lists plugins that must be enabled ("name", "name@marketplace", or {name, marketplace, version}). Missing dependencies are installed on /reload-plugins. `claude plugin prune` removes auto-installed dependencies no installed plugin needs.
facts.limits: Cross-marketplace dependencies only if the plugin's own marketplace lists the target in allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn. prune never removes a plugin the user installed; requires -y when non-TTY.

facts.behavior: CLI: 'Validate a plugin or marketplace manifest, or the skills, agents, and commands in a directory.' Picks target by what is in the directory: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, else .claude-plugin/plugin.json, else component files by directory name (v2.1.233+; if both manifests exist it validates both, v2.1.289+). Reports errors/warnings and a verdict. Flags: --strict (warnings become errors; for CI, fails on unrecognized fields and missing metadata), --json (v2.1.259+), --profile directory (also exits 1 when the plugin directory catalog would refuse a submission, e.g. missing README; checks at most 16 MCP/hooks files). Exit codes: 0 passed (with or without warnings), 1 failed, 2 unexpected validator error. Also checks name rules, paths, MCP entries, quoting of ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in shell-form hooks, agent frontmatter parse, CLAUDE.md at plugin root (warning), unknown fields. In-session equivalent: /plugin validate <path>.
facts.limits: Does not follow symlinks (warns about unread linked dirs; errors if the named dir is a symlink); does not check a root SKILL.md; per components page does not read .lsp.json; in a marketplace run it does not open skill/agent/command/hook files of plugins in other directories (validate each plugin dir); does not catch entry hooks given as file path or fetch errors for a source; does not check official-marketplace-name reservation at add time. Default (non-strict) exit is 0 on warnings. Not a runtime gate: Claude Code still loads plugins that fail validate name checks.

facts.feature: claude plugin details and projected token cost
facts.behavior: `claude plugin details <name>` (no flags beyond --help) prints name, version, description, source, then 'Component inventory' (skills, agents, hooks with events, MCP servers, LSP servers; commands counted with skills), 'Projected token cost' (Always-on tokens 'added to every session'), and 'Per-component (rounded)' always-on and on-invoke estimates for each skill/agent/command. Plugin must be loaded (installed, in a skills directory, or via --plugin-dir/--plugin-url in the same command: `claude --plugin-dir ./p plugin details p`). Always-on is the component name plus its `description` and `when_to_use` frontmatter, per skill/agent/command, counted every session where the plugin is enabled; on-invoke is the body loaded when the component runs. Observed output for this repo: house-rules 0.22.0 Always-on ~883 tok.
facts.limits: Hooks ('harness-only — no model context cost') and MCP servers ('tool schemas resolved at runtime; not counted') get no estimate or per-component row; use /context 'MCP tools' for MCP. 'Token counts are estimates and may differ from actual usage.' Unloaded plugin: error, exit 1. Shell-only (no session form). Report-only, nothing enforces a budget.

facts.feature: Plugin context cost in every session (docs statement)
facts.behavior: 'An enabled plugin is part of every session, not only the sessions where you use it.' For each skill, agent, and command Claude can invoke on its own, the name and description are in context every turn; those tokens count toward usage even when nothing runs. Full text of a skill or agent loads only when used. Advice to lower it: shorten skill and agent descriptions; split a large plugin so users install only needed components; check triggering with a tool_used: Skill eval grader after trimming.
facts.limits: Advisory only; no cap, threshold or warning from the CLI on always-on size.

facts.feature: Context cost shown in /plugin before install
facts.behavior: Plugins in Anthropic's official marketplace show a 'Context cost' section in the /plugin details pane with 'Every turn:' and 'When invoked:' lines; the Every turn line is highlighted when the always-on figure is 2,000 tokens or more.
facts.limits: A plugin in your own (third-party) marketplace has no Context cost section. Display only.

facts.feature: Plugin usage tracking: Not used recently, /skill-doctor, /doctor, /usage
facts.behavior: On the /plugin Installed tab, a marketplace-installed plugin moves under 'Not used recently' after at least 14 days and 10 sessions unused; details show 'Last used:'. /skill-doctor flags skills never invoked (including plugin skills). /doctor lists unused user-installed skills, MCP servers and plugins and recommends disabling them. /usage attributes usage to skills, subagents, plugins and MCP servers on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise.
facts.limits: 'Not used recently' never appears for --plugin-dir or skills-dir plugins, managed-enabled or seed-dir plugins, or plugins with a theme/output style/monitor/workflow; hidden when strictKnownMarketplaces is set. Claude Code does not report plugin usage back to authors. Advisory UI.

facts.behavior: Events: claude_code.plugin_installed, plugin_loaded, skill_activated (with plugin.name, marketplace.name), hook_plugin_metrics (official-marketplace plugins only), and plugin.name on the cost counter. Official-tier plugin names reported verbatim; community/third-party names are redacted ('third-party' or omitted) unless OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1. Enterprise Analytics API GET /v1/organizations/analytics/plugins returns per-plugin per-day install and invocation counts.
facts.limits: Requires an exporter or Enterprise plan with read:analytics key.

facts.feature: Marketplace definition and marketplace.json required fields
facts.behavior: A marketplace is a directory/repo with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json listing plugins and where to fetch each; 'a catalog, not a hosted store'. Required top-level: name, owner (owner.name required), plugins. Entry requires name and source. Optional top-level: description (validate warns if missing), version, metadata.{description,version,pluginRoot}, forceRemoveDeletedPlugins, allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn, renames, $schema. Each entry validated on its own, so one invalid entry doesn't fail the marketplace.
facts.limits: Unknown top-level or entry keys are ignored at load (silent typo risk); validate warns ('Unknown field ... Claude Code ignores it at load time'). Duplicate plugin names are a validate error; empty plugins array is a warning.

facts.feature: Marketplace and plugin entry name rules and reserved names
facts.behavior: Marketplace/plugin entry names: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-', starting with letter/digit; validate fails others and Claude Code can't install them. Reserved marketplace names (official, community, directory names, and spellings/impersonations of them, plus inline, builtin, skills-dir, synced, claude-plugin-test, npm/pip/uv/cargo/github/gh, claudeai- prefix) are refused at `marketplace add` unless sourced from github.com/anthropics/. A registered marketplace whose name imitates an official one stops loading with its plugins.
facts.limits: Exact official names pass validate; refusal happens at add time. Entry name vs manifest name: install key/cache dir use the entry name, component namespace and `plugin details` use the manifest name; keep them equal or installs by manifest name fail.

facts.behavior: Plugin `source`: relative path (must start ./, resolves from marketplace root; no '..'), github {repo,ref,sha}, url {url,ref,sha}, git-subdir {url,path,ref,sha}, npm {package,version,registry} (install scripts never run), archive {url,sha256} (https zip; sha256 mismatch refuses install), command {command,timeout,mode} (runs a command on user's machine, shown for confirmation). `sha` is a full 40-char commit SHA and wins over `ref`. Version resolution order: plugin.json version, then entry version, then commit SHA (12 chars) / archive digest; npm and non-git local = 'unknown'. Setting `version` pins users until it changes.
facts.limits: A `url`-type marketplace source fetches only marketplace.json so relative-path plugin sources can't resolve; `settings` marketplaces reject relative paths. If plugin.json and entry both set version, plugin.json wins (validate warns).

facts.behavior: `strict` defaults true: with a plugin.json present, entry commands/agents/skills/outputStyles/themes are appended and entry hooks matchers replace the manifest's per event. With strict:false and plugin.json present, an entry declaring any component field is a conflict and the plugin fails to load ('has conflicting manifests'). With no plugin.json the entry is the manifest regardless. Manifest version overrides entry version; entry defaultEnabled and display fields override manifest.
facts.limits: Entry mcpServers/lspServers/userConfig/channels don't apply when plugin.json exists. Entry `hooks` as a file path or array passes validate but never runs (error at load).

facts.behavior: `claude plugin marketplace add|list|remove(rm)|update`: add accepts URL, path, or GitHub repo (owner/repo, owner/repo@ref, #ref; --sparse sets sparsePaths); update refreshes all if no name; remove uninstalls the marketplace's plugins. Adding writes to extraKnownMarketplaces in user settings. One marketplace per name per user. In-session: /plugin marketplace add|list|update|remove.
facts.limits: Marketplaces added from local path load plugins in place (edits apply at next session or /reload-plugins without bumping version). Remote marketplaces are cached copies.

facts.behavior: From `claude plugin --help`: configure, details, disable, enable, eval, init|new (scaffolds ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ as <name>@skills-dir; --with skills,agents,hooks,mcp,lsp,output-style,channel), install|i (-s user|project|local, --config, --marketplace, -y, --accept-command, --json), list, marketplace, prune|autoremove, tag, test (runs a mod's tests), uninstall|remove, update (restart required to apply), validate. `claude plugins` is an alias.
facts.limits: Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failure; validate adds 2. In-session /plugin and /reload-plugins exist only in interactive sessions (/reload-plugins also works in -p/SDK from v2.1.260 when typed directly). init, update, details, prune, eval, test have no session form.
facts.citation: claude plugin --help ; claude plugin install --help ; claude plugin update --help ; claude plugin init --help ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference

facts.behavior: Creates annotated git tag <name>--v<version> for a plugin release; validates that plugin.json and any enclosing marketplace entry agree on version. Flags: --dry-run, -f/--force (skips dirty-tree and tag-exists checks), -m/--message (%s = version), --push, --remote (default origin). Refuses a reserved Anthropic-looking name.
facts.limits: Exits 1 if no version, tag exists, or working tree dirty. If push fails the local tag is still created.

facts.feature: Plugin loading stages, caching, and reload
facts.behavior: Three layers: settings (enabledPlugins/extraKnownMarketplaces), disk (~/.claude/plugins: installed_plugins.json, known_marketplaces.json, cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/), session (loaded at startup or /reload-plugins). Marketplace plugins are copied to the cache and loaded from the copy; --plugin-dir, skills-dir, and local-path marketplace relative plugins load in place. Plugins load at session start without network. Old version directories get an .orphaned_at marker and are removed after 14 days. /reload-plugins applies pending changes and prints a summary; closing the /plugin panel with pending changes runs it automatically.
facts.limits: Settings/disk changes don't reach a running session until /reload-plugins or restart; monitors need a session restart; a reload that changes MCP tools and invalidates the prompt cache needs --force.

facts.behavior: `claude plugin update` and background auto-update recompute the version and don't replace the cache when it matches; a manifest `version` keeps users on the cached copy until the string changes however many commits are pushed. Auto-update runs in interactive sessions after a random delay of up to ten minutes after the first message, for marketplaces with auto-update on (default: on for official marketplaces such as claude-plugins-official and claude.ai-added ones, off for others). Disabled by DISABLE_UPDATES, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC unless FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS=1. Update is announced 'Plugin updated: <name> · Run /reload-plugins to apply'.
facts.limits: Mid-session updates leave hooks/MCP/LSP on the old path until /reload-plugins. command-source plugins re-run every session regardless of DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER. A managed autoUpdate setting makes the user's /plugin toggle refuse.

facts.feature: Install scopes and where enabledPlugins is set
facts.behavior: Scopes: user (all projects), project (committed .claude/settings.json, each collaborator still installs on their machine for external sources), local (this repo only). enabledPlugins merges key by key; precedence low to high: --add-dir, user, project, local, flag (--settings), managed. Managed true force-enables and false blocks, and nothing overrides them. To opt out of a project-enabled plugin set false in .claude/settings.local.json.
facts.limits: Claude Code does not scan a project's .claude/plugins/ directory. A project-enabled plugin with an external source isn't fetched automatically ('enabled in project settings but isn't installed'); only relative-path marketplace plugins load without install. Project extraKnownMarketplaces apply only after the workspace trust dialog. Skills-dir plugins load only from the session's primary working directory's .claude/skills/, not parent dirs.

facts.feature: Session-only plugins (--plugin-dir, --plugin-url, CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS) and name conflicts
facts.behavior: --plugin-dir <path|.zip> and --plugin-url load a plugin for one session without installing (id <name>@inline); `claude plugin list` shows them only when the same flag precedes the subcommand. Same manifest name precedence: managed enabledPlugins > session-only plugin > installed marketplace plugin > skills-dir plugin > claude.ai-synced plugin. A session-only plugin silently replaces an installed same-named marketplace plugin.
facts.limits: A --plugin-dir copy is ignored if managed settings lock that plugin name; managed disableSideloadFlags rejects the flags and exits 1. Disable via "<name>@inline": false.

facts.behavior: A directory with .claude-plugin/plugin.json saved under ~/.claude/skills/ or the project's .claude/skills/ loads as <name>@skills-dir (auto-loads next session). Enabled by the manifest's defaultEnabled unless a settings file sets it. `claude plugin init <name>` scaffolds one at ~/.claude/skills/<name>/.
facts.limits: Not copied; loads in place. Project .claude/skills/ plugins only load in a trusted folder. Stop loading if managed strictKnownMarketplaces is set without a {"source":"skills-dir"} entry. Plain SKILL.md skills without the manifest are unaffected.

facts.behavior: A project-scope plugin (from committed .claude/settings.json) loads only after the workspace trust check. Its MCP servers go through the per-server approval; MCP bundles (.mcpb/.dxt) and MCP files outside the plugin directory are skipped; background monitors do not load.
facts.limits: Personal-scope plugins have none of these restrictions. Trusting a parent folder or running with -p isn't enough.

facts.feature: Node.js dependency install for cached plugins
facts.behavior: When copying a marketplace plugin into the cache Claude Code automatically installs its Node.js deps if the root has both package.json and a supported lockfile (bun.lock, npm-shrinkwrap.json, package-lock.json, checked in that order), with scripts disabled, frozen versions, 60-second timeout.
facts.limits: Skipped for yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb, git/folder/workspace deps, npm overrides, Bun patchedDependencies, link-mode command plugins, and in-place local-marketplace plugins. 'You can't turn the automatic install off.' Failure leaves the plugin loaded without node_modules (note shown in /plugin and `plugin list`).

facts.feature: Plugin security and trust (install warning, no code review)
facts.behavior: 'A Claude Code plugin you install can execute arbitrary code on your machine with your user privileges.' /plugin shows a trust warning before install (managed pluginTrustMessage appends text). Installing a plugin also enables it unless defaultEnabled:false. Skills, commands and agents 'enter Claude's context as instructions'. Community catalog pins plugins to a commit SHA and Claude Code refuses a different commit. Archive sources with sha256 pin refuse mismatched downloads.
facts.limits: Anthropic 'does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change.' The 'Will install' pane shows a hook exists but not what it runs. Marketplace name indicates publisher, not plugin safety.

facts.behavior: Managed settings keys: strictKnownMarketplaces (allowlist; [] blocks all; alias allowedMarketplaces), blockedMarketplaces (checked first), extraKnownMarketplaces, enabledPlugins (true force-enables, false blocks and hides), syncClaudeAiPlugins, disableSideloadFlags (rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, SDK plugins option, non-SDK --mcp-config, CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS), disableCommandPluginSources, allowManagedHooksOnly, strictPluginOnlyCustomization (blocks skills/agents/hooks/MCP not from a plugin, managed settings or built-ins), pluginSuggestionMarketplaces, pluginTrustMessage, allowedChannelPlugins. Allow/blocklists apply before download and again at session start (installed plugin whose marketplace no longer matches doesn't load).
facts.limits: Allowlist doesn't register a marketplace, restrict entries inside an allowed marketplace, or block --plugin-dir. No per-user targeting, no key to hide /plugin. allowManagedHooksOnly doesn't trust hooks from plugins users enable themselves. Most keys take effect only from managed settings.
