area: Plugin eval runner (claude plugin eval): case format, graders, runs, ablation, thresholds, reports, availability; Anthropic eval guidance

facts.feature: claude plugin eval command (what it is)
facts.behavior: "The `claude plugin eval` shell command runs your plugin against a suite of test cases and scores the results. Each case is a realistic prompt plus one or more graders." CLI help: "Run eval cases (<eval dir>/**/case.yaml or prompt.md + graders/*.md; the eval dir is evals/ unless --eval-dir or the manifest says otherwise) against a plugin and report scored results." Target is a path, a plugin name, or plugin@marketplace id.
facts.limits: Tests plugin behavior, not plugin file syntax (that is `claude plugin validate`). Not the same tool as skill-creator; "neither tool reads the other's case files" (skill-creator uses evals/evals.json). Every eval run and every judge grader is a real model call counted against plan usage or API bill.

facts.behavior: Requires Claude Code v2.1.269 or later; Git 2.31 or later if git is installed (older git: stops before running any case, exit 1; no git: runs normally); a plugin dir with plugin.json or .claude-plugin/plugin.json, or a skills-directory plugin; same auth and provider as normal sessions. Troubleshooting lists "plugin eval is currently in early access" (build predates general availability; run claude update) and "plugin eval is currently unavailable" ("Anthropic has switched the command off server-side. Nothing on your machine turns it back on").
facts.limits: Can be switched off server-side by Anthropic. Before v2.1.283 no git-version check; before v2.1.299 API-error runs were graded on what they produced. Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry users must export the same provider variables in the shell running the suite.

facts.behavior: Interactive: Claude reads the plugin, asks what a good result looks like, proposes prompts that should and should not trigger the plugin, designs graders, runs them once as a trial, and writes one case directory per prompt under evals/. `claude plugin eval init --bare <name>` writes a blank template case (placeholder prompt.md and one placeholder grader) and runs nothing.
facts.limits: Non-bare init needs a terminal; in CI use --bare. Recommended path is init, not hand-writing.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Create your first eval suite, Write a case manually, CI)

facts.behavior: A case is a directory under the plugin's eval directory containing prompt.md, case.yaml, or both. Layout: evals/<case>/prompt.md (frontmatter: case and run fields; body: the prompt), optional case.yaml (context.* fields or whole case), graders/<name>.md (one grader per file), optional case mocks/, fixtures. Cases can be grouped by nesting under a non-case directory. "Give each case at least one grader ... because a case without one fails to load" (error `invalid case.yaml` naming graders). case.yaml requires schema_version "1.1" and name; prompt.md sets schema_version automatically. When both files exist, prompt.md frontmatter overrides matching case.yaml fields and graders/*.md are added after case.yaml graders.
facts.limits: Unknown key in prompt.md frontmatter is an error. Claude receives the prompt body exactly as written; @path mentions are not expanded into attachments. Each run starts in an empty working directory.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Write and refine cases, Eval suite reference)

facts.behavior: Fields: schema_version, name (default dir name), description (humans only), tags (default []), plugins (default nearest enclosing plugin), runs (default 3, range 1-50; --runs overrides), expected_outcome (humans only), model (--model overrides), max_turns (default 10, up to 200), timeout_seconds (default 300, up to 3600), allowed_tools (default []), append_system_prompt, env (keys must match EVAL_[A-Z0-9_]*).
facts.limits: Hitting max_turns is recorded as a run error and usually lowers the score. Non-EVAL_ env keys fail the run. Run inherits only an allowlist of shell env (basics, proxy/cert, provider-selection/auth vars, most ANTHROPIC_* and CLAUDE_CODE_*, EVAL_*).

facts.behavior: context.scaffold_script: Bash script in the case dir run in the empty workspace before Claude starts to create fixtures/git state, only with --scaffold, minimal env, 120-second limit, non-zero exit scores that run 0 with `scaffold failed`. context.history_file: .jsonl transcript to resume; the prompt becomes the next user turn. context.add_dirs: dirs Claude may read, read-only. execution.prompt and a graders list (llm rubric under `criteria`) are also case.yaml-only.
facts.limits: Scaffold runs as you, outside the agent's sandbox; pass --scaffold only for suites you or your organization wrote. Project configuration a scaffold writes (.claude/, CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json) is not loaded. Neither the case's EVAL_* vars nor most shell env reach the script.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Set up fixtures and mocks, case.yaml fields)

facts.behavior: Six types, no others. regex (pattern, flags, match, target): JavaScript regex found in target; match: not_contains or "count:N"; flags: i, inline (?i) unsupported. tool_used (tool, input_match, min default 1, max default unlimited; min 0 max 0 asserts never called). tool_order (before, after). file_exists (path glob, exists). llm (criteria, focus): judge votes PASS in at least two of three votes. baseline (baseline_file, criteria): judge finds run satisfies criteria at least as well as a reference transcript .jsonl. regex, tool_used, tool_order, file_exists "are computed from the transcript and files and cost nothing"; llm and baseline call a judge model and add cost.
facts.limits: "There are no custom-code graders." file_exists counts only files created during the run (not scaffold-created or merely edited files). Grader frontmatter keys: type (required), weight (default 1, any positive number), arm (unset, with-only, both).

facts.feature: Grader targets/focus (what a grader can look at)
facts.behavior: regex target and llm focus accept: last_message (default, final response text), trace (session JSON one message per line; regex sees every message, llm judge sees first 12 and last 12; quotes JSON-escaped), files (list of paths Claude created, not contents), { source: file, path: <path> } (contents of one workspace file after the run; PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP shown to llm judge as image), mock_calls.
facts.limits: files target is paths only, not contents, and excludes scaffold-created or only-modified files. llm judge refuses other binary files such as .pptx or PDF.

facts.behavior: By default the judge for llm and baseline graders is "the model Claude Code uses for background tasks." --judge-model <model> (alias like sonnet or full model ID) chooses it. Docs advise: for long output grade with regex over file contents and keep llm graders for short outputs with concrete PASS/FAIL rubrics; give each case one grader on the result and one on the steps (tool_used/tool_order); if tool_used Skill passes but Δ is negative suspect the judge, re-run with --judge-model sonnet.
facts.limits: llm verdicts vary between runs, more with longer text; a small judge may mark a correct answer wrong over formatting. Cost: three short judge calls per llm or baseline grader per run.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Choose graders that give a stable signal; Command options)

facts.behavior: "each case runs three times by default." A run's score is the fraction of its graders that passed (weighted if weights set); the case's score is the mean across its runs. Each run is a fresh isolated non-interactive session (a `claude -p` child process) with only the plugin loaded, until finished or max_turns/timeout. Suite makes roughly cases x runs agent runs with the plugin plus the same again for baseline, plus judge calls.
facts.limits: Runs per arm: 1-50. A single run is noisy; docs say confirm changes at the default three runs. -j/--concurrency 1-8 (default 1) shortens wall-clock but shares account rate limit.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (How a case is scored, Command options)

facts.behavior: By default a case runs in two arms: with-arm (plugin loaded) and without-arm (no plugin). Summary shows WITH, W/OUT and Δ (with minus without). "If a case scores 1.0 both with and without the plugin, the plugin isn't what made it pass." --ablation none runs one arm (halves cost; table shows SCORE and PASS%); --ablation with-without adds baseline. Graders excluded from score in two-arm runs (scored: false, shown as indicators): every tool_used with tool Skill; regex target mock_calls / llm focus mock_calls when mocked servers are the plugin's own; any grader with arm: with-only. arm: both forces scoring in both arms. If every grader in a case is excluded they are scored normally; under --ablation none nothing is excluded.
facts.limits: Single arm by default for cases with context.history_file when target is a path, and when no plugin is resolved for the case (fix with plugins: ["../.."]). In baseline runs plugin agents fail with `Agent type '<plugin>:<agent>' not found` (expected). Δ is reported but never changes the exit code.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (The no-plugin baseline; Score against the no-plugin baseline)

facts.behavior: --threshold <0..1> default 1.0: a case passes when its with-arm score is at least the threshold; any case below makes the command exit 1. Exit codes: 0 all cases at or above threshold; 1 case below threshold, case file failed to load, no cases found, run couldn't start, run ended on API error, untrusted dir without --trust-plugin, invalid option, or --json write failure; 2 partial run (--max-cost-usd ceiling hit or credential rejected), results.json still written with partial: true; 130 interrupted (partial results written); 143 terminated.
facts.limits: Default 1.0 means any score under perfect fails the build. The with-minus-without delta never changes exit code. Runs ended by API/usage/rate-limit error score 0 without grading and exit non-zero regardless of threshold (including baseline-arm runs).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Command options; Run evals in CI; ended on an API error)

facts.behavior: --max-cost-usd <usd> is "a ceiling on the run's list-price cost estimate, not on plan usage. Checked before each run starts." Once spent nothing further starts; already-started runs finish; if any run is left unstarted exit 2 with partial results. Reported cost is a list-price estimate including judge calls. Docs advise cheap every-change suites use graders that don't call a judge and --ablation none.
facts.limits: Default no ceiling. Spend can exceed ceiling by in-flight runs. Cost ceiling can skip judge graders (skippedPaidGraders: true), making that run's score non-comparable; leave partial documents and such runs out of trend charts.

facts.behavior: --model sets the model for the agent under test (default: case model, else ANTHROPIC_MODEL, else Claude Code default). Docs: "Pin it in CI so a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression"; CI example pins both --model and --judge-model.
facts.limits: Pinning is guidance; not required.

facts.behavior: Target: plugin root dir (e.g. .), a single prompt.md or case.yaml, an installed plugin by name or name@marketplace, name@skills-dir, or omitted (current dir). --case <glob> filters by case name; --tag <tag> keeps cases with any given tag. Named installed-plugin runs write results under ./evals/results/ (or ./<dir>/results/) in the current directory.
facts.limits: Put target before --tag, --allow-tools, --json (they consume following args). Marketplace plugin added from local path that no session could load is refused (`cannot be evaluated where sessions load it`, exit 1).

facts.behavior: Default eval dir is evals/. Set plugin.json "experimental": { "evals": "quality/evals" } or pass --eval-dir to both `plugin eval` and `plugin eval init`; flag wins. Cases, results and init output all move.
facts.limits: Relative path of plain directory names only; absolute path or '..' is an error as a flag, and an unusable manifest value prints a Warning and falls back to evals/. With an array only the first entry is used. Not covered by component path rules; checked at eval run time. experimental.* manifest shape "may still change".
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Use a different eval directory); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md (experimental.evals, Path rules)

facts.feature: Tool grants and run isolation of tools
facts.behavior: "Runs never stop to ask for permission." Built-in tools needing a grant you didn't give (Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch) are removed from the session. Only read-only tools listed in a case's allowed_tools are allowed (Read, Glob, Grep, NotebookRead, Skill, AskUserQuestion, Agent, TodoWrite, TaskCreate/Get/List/Update/Stop) plus --allow-tools grants, which apply to every case. Granting Bash runs commands under Claude Code's OS-level sandbox (writes confined to workspace, home and config unreadable, network limited to granted WebFetch(domain:...)). Case allowed_tools and a skill's allowed-tools cannot widen scaffold, tool grants, or real-server access.
facts.limits: If Bash/PowerShell granted on a machine with no sandbox backend, each run is refused (case shows run error, usually 0); native Windows has none (use WSL2); Linux needs bubblewrap and socat. Ungranted-tool requests show as `not granted` in progress. No network sandbox outside shell commands; a WebFetch(domain:) grant reaches the domain directly.

facts.feature: Run isolation (what loads in a run)
facts.behavior: Each run gets a temporary home dir, working dir and Claude Code configuration. "Nothing personal or project-level loads": user settings, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers, other installed plugins, memory, and skills are absent; no .claude/, CLAUDE.md or .mcp.json loads from above or inside the workspace. Only the plugin under test (its skills, hooks, agents) loads. The case definitions (eval dir, prompt, graders, sibling cases) are hidden from the agent. The Artifact tool is off. Managed policy settings still apply.
facts.limits: Isolation limits the agent under test, "isn't a boundary against the plugin's own code". Plugin hooks and real MCP servers run outside the agent's sandbox and could modify files graders read; treat scores as advisory unless run in a container/CI runner. A passing suite is not a security vetting.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (What a run can access; How runs are isolated)

facts.behavior: First run against a directory asks `Trust this plugin directory?` before loading anything, unless already accepted in an interactive claude session; in a git repo yes trusts the whole repository (interactive sessions too). When stdin/stdout isn't a terminal or --json is used the run is refused with exit 1; --trust-plugin asserts trust (for CI, only for a plugin you would run yourself). Named installed or skills-dir plugins skip the prompt.
facts.limits: Pointing eval at a plugin is the same trust decision as `claude --plugin-dir`.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Trust the plugin directory); claude plugin --help (eval entry)

facts.behavior: One Markdown file per tool at evals/mocks/<server>/<tool>.md (suite-wide) or a case's own mocks/ (overrides suite file by file). Body is the tool result; supports {{input.<field>}} and {{file:fixtures/...}}; frontmatter: type (fixed or agent), expect (input guard; violation aborts the run with score 0), error, abort_when. _server.md (one agent mock for several tools) and _tools.json (saved tools/list). Default --mocks record answers from mocks and does not start the plugin's real servers; a tool with no mock file is unavailable to Claude. Agent-mock answers are saved to mock-recordings/ with ADOPT.txt; copying to mocks/.replay/<server>/ replays them with no model call.
facts.limits: Agent mocks use the judge model and vary between runs; share a budget of 4x the case's max_turns calls per run (default 40), exceeding aborts with score 0. Real servers need --allow-real-servers or --mocks off plus an --allow-tools grant (mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>), and run as you outside the sandbox. expect regex uses a small dialect (no groups/alternation/lookaround; flags i and s only); invalid pattern stops case loading.

facts.behavior: Every run with at least one case writes <eval dir>/results/<timestamp>/ with aggregate-result.json and report.html (override with --output-dir). Console summary columns CASE, WITH, W/OUT, Δ, RUNS, COST, NOTES plus a mean Δ line. report.html is "a single self-contained file that makes no external requests"; shows verdict line (Plugin effect vs baseline), tiles (suite score, ablation delta, baseline score, cases passing threshold, perfect runs), per-case cards with threshold tick and red edge for negative Δ, per-run grader pass/fail with explanations, llm judge votes and evidence, prompt and graders. aggregate-result.json (and --json output) is versioned schemaVersion 1, camelCase, with partial/partialReason, aggregates (overallScore, casesPassed, casesTotal, meanDelta), cases[].aggregates.score/delta, cases[].arms.with[].error/aborted/skippedPaidGraders, costUsd, durationSeconds, claudeVersion. --json [path] prints/writes the document and makes the run quiet.
facts.limits: Docs say add results/ to .gitignore. Scripts should ignore unrecognized fields. Report write/publish problems never change the exit code. --json needs a path ending .json.

facts.behavior: If signed in with a claude.ai subscription and artifacts are available, Claude Code also publishes the report as a private artifact and prints `Published: <url>`. --no-publish keeps it local; --publish-report publishes even where it would stay local by default.
facts.limits: No Published line with API-key auth (local file is the report). A run started by a Claude Code session stays local (`kept local`) unless --publish-report is passed.

facts.behavior: Docs example: claude plugin eval . --trust-plugin --json results.json --threshold 0.8 --model claude-sonnet-5 --judge-model claude-haiku-4-5 --no-publish --max-cost-usd 20; fail the build on exit code. Runner needs a Claude Code install and credentials in env (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or cloud provider vars). For predictable cost: judge-free graders for every-change suites, --ablation none, exclude partial documents from trends.
facts.limits: The example is documentation guidance, not enforced; CI must supply install, credentials and trust itself.

facts.behavior: --keep-temp keeps each run's sandbox dir and prints its path; --verbose; --report; --no-scaffold; -j/--concurrency; --output-dir. `claude plugin eval --help` is the complete list per docs.
facts.limits: I could not run `claude plugin eval --help` directly: the session's Bash guard refused any command containing the word eval. Only the eval entry in `claude plugin --help` was read.

facts.behavior: "`experimental.evals`: Directory that holds the plugin's eval cases when it isn't the default `evals/`. `claude plugin eval --eval-dir` overrides it." Part of the `experimental` container (themes, monitors, evals) "whose manifest shape may still change".
facts.limits: plugins-reference page has no other eval content (no case format, graders, or thresholds); those are on the plugin-evals page.

facts.behavior: Per the Anthropic blog: skill-creator helps write evals ("tests that check Claude does what you expect for a given prompt"); users define test prompts, optional files and what good output looks like. Adds "a benchmark mode that runs a standardized assessment using your evals" tracking eval pass rate, elapsed time, token usage. Evals run in parallel on independent agents, each "in a clean context with its own token and timing metrics". Comparator agents run A/B comparisons (two skill versions, or skill vs no skill) judging outputs "without knowing which is which". Description tuning suggests edits to cut false positives and negatives. Evals can catch regressions when models change and show when a capability-uplift skill is no longer needed if the base model passes without it. Available on Claude.ai and Cowork; in Claude Code as a plugin (anthropics/skills repo).
facts.limits: Uses its own evals/evals.json format, not read by claude plugin eval and vice versa. Blog gives no numeric limits; results stored by the user locally, in a dashboard or CI (no hosted store described).

facts.behavior: Code-based graders: fast, cheap, objective, reproducible, easy to debug; weakness "Brittle to valid variations that don't match expected patterns exactly." Model-based: flexible, scalable, capture nuance; non-deterministic, more expensive, "require calibration with human graders for accuracy." Human: "Gold standard quality", used to calibrate model graders; expensive and slow. "It is often better to grade what the agent produced, not the path it took."
facts.limits: Engineering-blog guidance only; not a harness feature.

facts.behavior: "20-50 simple tasks drawn from real failures is a great start." "A good task is one where two domain experts would independently reach the same pass/fail verdict." Each task should have a known working reference output that passes all graders. "Test both the cases where a behavior should occur and where it shouldn't." Award partial credit for multi-component tasks. Start each trial from a clean environment. A 0% pass rate across many trials "is most often a signal of a broken task, not an incapable agent."
facts.limits: Advice only; no numeric thresholds are given.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: pass@k, pass^k, scoring modes
facts.behavior: pass@k "measures the likelihood that an agent gets at least one correct solution in k attempts"; pass^k "measures the probability that all k trials succeed" (75% per-trial over three trials is about 42% for all three). Use pass@k "for tools where one success matters, pass^k for agents where consistency is essential." Scoring can be weighted (combined grader scores must hit a threshold), binary (all graders must pass), or hybrid.
facts.limits: claude plugin eval does not expose pass@k or pass^k; it reports mean score per case against a single --threshold. The post gives no numeric pass-rate thresholds.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: capability vs regression evals, saturation, reading transcripts
facts.behavior: Capability evals ask "What can this agent do well?" and should start at a low pass rate ("a hill to climb"); regression evals ask whether the agent still handles prior tasks and should be near 100%; high-pass capability evals can "graduate" into regression suites. An eval at 100% "tracks regressions but provides no signal for improvement" (saturation). "You won't know if your graders are working well unless you read the transcripts and grades from many trials"; "we do not take eval scores at face value until someone digs into the details of the eval and reads some transcripts"; failures should seem fair.
facts.limits: Advice only; the harness does not enforce reading transcripts, though report.html exposes per-run grader explanations and the trace.

unreachable: `claude plugin eval --help` (full flag list): every Bash call containing the word eval was refused by the worktree guard, so only the eval entry in `claude plugin --help` was read. Flags were taken from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md instead.

https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md has no case-format, grader, threshold, or report content; only the experimental.evals key. The detail is on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md, which I read in full.

area: sessions and resume, worktrees and cleanup, sandboxing, checkpoints, background tasks, what carries between sessions

facts.behavior: Sessions are saved continuously to local transcript files as you work, stored as JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl (project = working dir path with non-alphanumerics replaced by -). Retention is 30 days by default.
facts.limits: Entry format is internal and changes between versions; scripts parsing it can break. Retention configurable via cleanupPeriodDays; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR moves storage; CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY suppresses writes; --no-session-persistence only with -p. Desktop/Cowork transcripts use desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays.

facts.behavior: claude --continue reopens the most recent session in the current directory; claude --resume opens the picker; --resume <name> resumes by name; --resume <transcript-path> resumes a .jsonl; --from-pr <n> filters the picker to sessions linked to a PR; /resume switches session inside a session.
facts.limits: -p/SDK sessions and sessions whose first prompt was /loop are hidden from the picker and from --continue (resumable by session ID; claude -p --continue includes them). --continue skips a still-running background session and exits with a message. Resume by name resolves across repo and its worktrees; ambiguous name opens picker (CLI) or errors (/resume). Default display names (e.g. my-app-3f) are not resume handles; generated titles are.

facts.behavior: Restores conversation history (from last compaction summary onward), model, agent (--agent/agent setting), permission mode (terminal resume), active goal (turn count/timer/token baseline reset), unexpired session-scoped scheduled tasks; interrupted tool calls are marked cut off and Claude is told to check whether they took effect.
facts.limits: Not restored: --mcp-config, --settings, --plugin-dir, --fallback-model, --add-dir directories and directories added mid-session with /add-dir (pass again); background Bash and monitor tasks are not restored (ended background subagents/bash/workflows appear as a note that they did not finish). settings.json/settings.local.json are re-read at launch. Messages summarized by the last compaction are not reloaded.

facts.behavior: Terminal --continue / --resume <id> / --resume <unique name> without -p restores the session's permission mode; plan mode is restored via picker, /resume, -p (under conditions), VS Code; auto restored only if account still meets auto mode requirements.
facts.limits: A session that ended in bypassPermissions is NOT restored to bypass on terminal resume (starts in the mode a new session would; re-enable with launch flag or defaultMode). Manual resumes as Manual only when a new session would start in auto by default. Pass --permission-mode or --dangerously-skip-permissions to override. Plan mode not restored with --fork-session or when a deny rule removes ExitPlanMode. /resume inside a session continues in current mode except plan.

facts.feature: Resume of a running background session
facts.behavior: claude --resume / /resume on a conversation belonging to a still-running background session opens that session (claude attach); a prompt on the command line is sent to it as its next turn. /resume inside a session moves the current conversation to the background and attaches. Before v2.1.285 Claude Code refused.
facts.limits: Not opened (exit status 1 with attach command printed) when command has piped I/O, session-configuring flags (--permission-mode, --model, --settings), output-reading flags (--output-format, --json-schema), or limit flags (--max-turns, --max-budget-usd), or agent view is off; prompts starting with / or ! are not sent; --fork-session resumes a copy.

facts.behavior: Picker shows sessions from the current worktree (including bg sessions) plus sessions that added the current directory with /add-dir. Ctrl+W widens to all worktrees of the repo, Ctrl+A to all projects, Ctrl+B filters to current git branch, Ctrl+R renames, Space previews, paste a PR/MR URL to search. Selecting a session from another worktree of the same repo resumes it in place; if its worktree is gone it resumes in current directory; unrelated-project selection copies a cd+resume command to clipboard.
facts.limits: Per project directory storage; /cd relocates a session's transcript to the new directory's project storage. Cross-project ID lookup resolves only if exactly one other project has a transcript for the ID.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md (Use the session picker; Where the session picker looks)

facts.behavior: Name via claude -n <name>, /rename, Ctrl+R in picker, auto title on plan accept, Remote Control rename, desktop rename. Unnamed sessions get a generated title (summary of first prompt by a background small/fast model request; none for direct claude -p runs) and a default display name.
facts.limits: Default display name is not resumable by name. /clear with no argument keeps a --name/ /rename name but not the AI-generated title; /clear <name> names the session you leave.

facts.behavior: /branch [name] copies the conversation so far and switches the running process into the copy; original is unchanged and remains in picker. CLI: claude --continue --fork-session. Branch inherits: history up to that point; 'Allow for this session' grants (same process); in-flight background subagents and background Bash (output appears in the branch); Remote Control connection.
facts.limits: --fork-session in a separate process starts without session grants (re-approve). Resuming the same session in two terminals without forking interleaves messages into one transcript. Forked worktree session starts in the launch directory and leaves original session's worktree untouched.

facts.behavior: /clear starts fresh with empty context and saves the previous session (resume via /resume, or via rewind menu 'previous session' entry in the same process). /compact [instructions] replaces history with a summary. /context shows what consumes context.
facts.limits: The rewind menu previous-session entry is available only until you exit Claude Code or resume a different session. Prompt history recall (Up-arrow) is stored per working directory and reaches past sessions of the same project; after /clear new session's prompts list first.

facts.behavior: /export copies the conversation to clipboard or saves a plain-text file. For scripts: claude -p --output-format json/stream-json, claude -p --resume <id>, transcript_path in hook and status line input, SessionEnd hook can archive transcript.
facts.limits: /export is human-readable only; transcript JSONL format is internal and unstable.

facts.feature: Session data deletion (claude purge, claude rm)
facts.behavior: Transcripts age out under the retention sweep; claude purge deletes all Claude Code state for a project (transcripts, tasks, file history, config entry). claude rm <id> deletes a background session and its worktree when that is safe.
facts.limits: claude rm leaves the transcript on disk and still resumable via claude --resume.

facts.behavior: claude --bg starts a session in the background; claude agents lists background agents; attach <id|name>, logs <id|name>, stop|kill <id> (conversation kept), rm <id>, respawn [id|--all] (restart so it runs current version); --session-id <uuid>; --teleport; --remote-control; --cloud.
facts.limits: stop keeps the conversation; resume works once stopped.

facts.behavior: Claude Code automatically tracks changes made by its file editing tools; every prompt that starts a turn creates a checkpoint. Snapshots are kept for the 100 most recent checkpoints per session; checkpoints are saved with the conversation so /rewind works after resume. Snapshots deleted by the retention sweep ~30 days after the session last saved one (cleanupPeriodDays).
facts.limits: Rewinding to a checkpoint whose snapshots are gone can fail with 'No files were restored'. Messages typed mid-turn get no checkpoint of their own (marked 'No code restore'); restore via the prompt that started the turn.

facts.behavior: /rewind, or Esc twice on an empty prompt, opens the rewind menu with: Restore code and conversation; Restore conversation; Restore code; Summarize from here; Summarize up to here; Never mind. Code restore options appear only if tracked file changes exist at that point. Summarize compresses context without changing files; originals stay in transcript.
facts.limits: If prompt has text, double Esc clears it instead (saved to history). Rewound messages can return if you exit before sending another prompt. Not a replacement for version control.

facts.feature: Checkpoint limits: Bash changes not tracked
facts.behavior: Only direct file edits through Claude's file editing tools are tracked.
facts.limits: Files modified by Bash commands (rm, mv, cp, etc.) cannot be undone through rewind.

facts.feature: Checkpoint limits: subagent, external, symlink edits
facts.behavior: Foreground forked skill (context: fork, background: false) edits are restored by rewind. Checkpointing tracks only files edited within the current session.
facts.limits: Other subagents (including background forked skills and background /code-review --fix): rewind restores only files Claude had already edited in your conversation; subagent edits to other files stay (use git). Manual edits outside Claude Code and other concurrent sessions are normally not captured. Symlinked and hard-linked files are skipped on code restore with a 'Restored the code, but skipped N files' warning.

facts.behavior: claude --worktree <name> creates an isolated git worktree under .claude/worktrees/<name>/ at the repo root on a new branch worktree-<name>; omitted name generates one like bright-running-fox. Reusing a name opens the existing worktree. --worktree '#1234' (or PR/MR URL) fetches the PR head from origin into .claude/worktrees/pr-<number>. --tmux creates a tmux session for the worktree.
facts.limits: Requires a git repo (otherwise WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks). Interactive runs require workspace trust (-p skips the check). Docs advise adding .claude/worktrees/ to .gitignore (advisory). A fresh worktree needs dependencies installed. Refuses to create when .claude, .claude/worktrees or the worktree dir is a symlink. Skips repository-config filter drivers (Git LFS shows pointer files; run git lfs pull). Four rare config conditions block creation entirely.

facts.behavior: Default 'fresh': branch from the repository's default branch on the remote (origin/HEAD, fetched if not fetched in 24h, capped at 5s, falls back to cached ref or local HEAD). 'head': branch from current local HEAD (inside a worktree, that worktree's HEAD). Subagent worktrees use the same base.
facts.limits: Cannot be set to a branch name (use git worktree add). A reopened worktree with default fresh base resets to default branch only if: no uncommitted/untracked changes, still on its created branch, and no own commits or its PR was merged with remote branch deleted; otherwise reopens at old tip.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (Choose the base branch; Reuse a worktree name)

facts.behavior: A .worktreeinclude file at the project root (gitignore syntax) lists gitignored files (e.g. .env) copied into every worktree Claude Code creates with git: --worktree, subagent worktrees, desktop parallel sessions.
facts.limits: Only files that match a pattern AND are gitignored are copied; tracked files never duplicated. Not processed when a WorktreeCreate hook replaces creation (copy in the hook). **/ patterns have special rules for wholly ignored directories.

facts.behavior: Asking Claude to work in a worktree creates one with EnterWorktree; Claude can switch to another worktree under .claude/worktrees/ by path; ExitWorktree leaves it. Transcript follows the session to the worktree directory (v2.1.198+).
facts.limits: Entering a path outside the repo's .claude/worktrees/ requires user approval; an EnterWorktree permission rule or 'don't ask again' does not suppress it, only bypassPermissions does (v2.1.206+). ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} in hooks stays at the original project root; hook input cwd follows the worktree. A WorktreeCreate-hook worktree keeps its transcript at the launch directory.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (Ask Claude to create a worktree; Resume a worktree session)

facts.behavior: On exiting an interactive worktree session Claude checks for changed/untracked files, uncommitted submodule work, and new commits. Clean + unnamed session: worktree and branch removed automatically. Clean + named session: prompts first. Has work: prompts keep or remove (keep prints a 'claude --worktree <name> --resume' command). State cannot be verified: prompts rather than removing.
facts.limits: Applies to worktrees Claude created with git; WorktreeCreate-hook worktrees use the WorktreeRemove hook. Non-interactive -p runs have no exit prompt: worktrees are not cleaned up and the lock Claude took stays until a later session's stale-lock sweep; remove with git worktree remove (git worktree unlock if locked). Removal deletes the directory and its branch with the work in them.

facts.feature: Periodic sweep of subagent and background-session worktrees
facts.behavior: Claude Code runs a periodic sweep removing worktrees it created for subagents and background sessions once older than cleanupPeriodDays. Subagent worktrees with no changes are removed automatically when the subagent finishes. Claude holds a git worktree lock on a running agent's/background session's worktree; the sweep releases locks Claude set for exited processes.
facts.limits: Sweep leaves in place: worktrees with changed/untracked files or unpushed commits; submodules with changes or uninspectable (v2.1.274+); worktrees where config blocks creation; worktrees of a --worktree session you have not backgrounded (any age); worktrees you made with git worktree add; any worktree without Claude's marker in git metadata (including WorktreeCreate-hook worktrees). Never releases locks you set yourself. Manual: git worktree remove (--force for dirty).

facts.behavior: Resuming a session that ended inside a worktree (without exiting it) returns the session to that worktree: interactive, -p with --continue/--resume, and Agent SDK. Claude Code first verifies the worktree is a checkout separate from the main one. If the worktree dir is gone, resumes in the launch directory and clears the binding. --fork-session starts in the launch directory.
facts.limits: Launching from inside a worktree: Claude Code re-enters only worktrees it created under .claude/worktrees/ or that it can vouch for; others decline (launch from main checkout). Refuses network-path worktrees. In -p and SDK, every refusal except a gone worktree aborts the resume with a stderr error (startup_failure_reason worktree_unverified / worktree_resume_refused). Interactive refusals continue without isolation with messages like 'Did not re-enter your worktree'.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (Resume a worktree session; The session resumes outside its worktree)

facts.behavior: While a session is isolated in a worktree (via --worktree, EnterWorktree, or resume), Claude Code blocks tool calls: (1) Edit/Write/NotebookEdit targeting a path in the main checkout; (2) Bash/PowerShell/Monitor commands whose working directory resolves to the main checkout or cannot be verified outside it; (3) Bash/Monitor commands that redirect git into the main checkout (git -C, --git-dir, GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, cd into main checkout then git); (4) Bash/Monitor commands whose text cannot be shown to keep any git inside the worktree (computed command names, unparseable syntax, expansions like ${!name}). Applies to every subagent spawned from the isolated session.
facts.limits: Reads path an edit targets, command cwd, and command text only; does not track which files a shell command writes, so cp or shell redirects into the main checkout are not refused by these checks (left to permissions and sandbox). The command-shape check cannot be turned off. PowerShell gets only the working-directory check. Covers the repo launched from and the main checkout a linked worktree links to.

facts.behavior: Subagents can run in their own temporary worktrees: ask Claude to 'use worktrees for your agents', or set isolation: worktree in a custom subagent's frontmatter. Same base branch and .worktreeinclude as --worktree.
facts.limits: A subagent in its own worktree takes its startup instruction files from the main conversation; when its worktree is in the default .claude/worktrees/ location it does not load the worktree-root CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/ as it reads files there, even if they differ on the worktree's branch.

facts.feature: What worktrees share with the main checkout
facts.behavior: Shared: the repository's .git directory (sandbox allows writes so git commit works); project-scope plugins (v2.1.200+); 'Yes, and don't ask again' Bash approvals are saved to the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json (v2.1.211+), applying to all worktrees and surviving removal; main checkout's project skills/agents/commands are read through when the worktree has no .claude/skills (skills read-through v2.1.277+). Desktop-app worktree sessions read settings, hooks, skills, agents, commands, .mcp.json from the main checkout root.
facts.limits: On Windows and where Claude Code does not use the repo root, permission rule stays with the worktree. CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ still load from the worktree. If worktree has its own .claude/skills only that copy loads.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (What worktrees share with the main checkout)

facts.behavior: A WorktreeCreate hook replaces the default git worktree logic entirely (including location other than .claude/worktrees/); WorktreeRemove cleans up. Also lets /batch run outside a git repo (v2.1.281+).
facts.limits: Hook-created dirs pass the isolation check only if no git repository contains them; .worktreeinclude not processed; the sweep keeps hook-created worktrees (no marker).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (Non-git version control; Replace worktree creation with a hook)

facts.behavior: Docs describe creating worktrees with git worktree add (specific existing branch or location outside the repo), starting claude there, git worktree list, git worktree remove.
facts.limits: Claude Code's own sweep and exit cleanup do not remove worktrees you created with git worktree add.

facts.behavior: OS-enforced boundary around the shell commands Claude runs (Bash, PowerShell, Monitor and child processes), built on @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime. macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux and WSL2 use bubblewrap (plus socat; optional seccomp filter for Unix-socket blocking). Enabled via /sandbox or sandbox.enabled.
facts.limits: Not on native Windows (commands run unsandboxed). By default, if the sandbox cannot start (missing dependency/unsupported platform), Claude Code runs commands WITHOUT sandboxing unless sandbox.failIfUnavailable is true. Runs outside the sandbox: Read/Edit/Write/WebFetch/WebSearch tools (governed by permission rules), command hooks, local MCP servers, plugin monitors, LSP servers, statusline and apiKeyHelper commands, mods' processes, and commands you type at the ! prompt in most sessions. Computer use is not sandboxed.

facts.behavior: Writes allowed to the working directory (and subdirectories), a per-user temp directory, and directories added via --add-dir / /add-dir / permissions.additionalDirectories. Reads: most of the machine, including credential files such as ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials. Adjust with sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite / denyWrite / denyRead / allowRead (narrower path wins; deny holds inside wider allow); arrays merge across settings scopes. Edits apply to the running session. For a linked git worktree, writes to the main repo's shared .git are allowed, except hooks/ and config.
facts.limits: Read tool is not stopped by denyRead (separate permission rules). permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories removes sandboxed read access to home and user-file dirs. sandbox.filesystem.disabled (v2.1.216+) turns off the filesystem layer only from user, managed or --settings sources (not project settings). Sandbox paths use ~/ and absolute conventions, unlike Read/Edit rule //path.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md (What the sandbox restricts; How sandboxing works; Disable filesystem isolation)

facts.behavior: Inside writable directories, the sandbox still denies writes to: .claude settings files and .claude/skills, agents, commands, hooks dirs, .mcp.json, .claude/workflows, .claude/scheduled_tasks.json (cwd and directories above it); in the working directory only: .bashrc/.zshrc, .gitconfig, .vscode, .idea, and hooks and config inside .git; bare-repo-making files (HEAD, objects, refs, config); most of ~/.claude (or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), ~/.claude.json, .credentials.json.
facts.limits: No exemption: an allowWrite entry or Edit allow rule does not lift protection; only filesystem.disabled turns it off (for every path). Applies to sandboxed commands, not to Claude's Edit/Write tools (permission system has its own protected paths). On Linux/WSL2 a top-level HEAD/objects/refs created mid-command is deleted. Can cause 'unable to unlink old' on git merge/checkout.

facts.behavior: Sandboxed commands have no direct route out (Linux/WSL2 separate network namespace; macOS Seatbelt blocks all but the proxy). A local proxy checks each hostname against allowedDomains (starts empty) and deniedDomains. New hosts: prompt in manual/acceptEdits/plan; allowed in bypassPermissions; refused in dontAsk; in auto mode refused unless the command listed the host and the classifier approved (per-command allowed domains, v2.1.271+). strictAllowlist (user/managed/--settings) or allowManagedDomainsOnly (managed) refuse non-allowlisted hosts in every mode. Proxy refuses hostnames resolving only to loopback/link-local/own addresses (localhost allowed).
facts.limits: Applies to sandboxed commands only; allowedDomains does not limit WebFetch. Proxy does not terminate or inspect TLS by default; domain fronting is possible; allowing broad domains like github.com can enable exfiltration. Tools that ignore proxy variables (plain ssh, most DB drivers) cannot connect; non-TCP (UDP, QUIC, ICMP) cannot leave. 'Yes, and don't ask again' saves a WebFetch(domain:...) allow rule. WebFetch(domain:) allow rules also pre-allow domains for the sandbox.

facts.behavior: Auto-allow mode: Claude Code approves a Bash command automatically (no prompt) when it runs inside the sandbox, even in Manual mode. Regular permissions mode: all Bash commands go through the regular permission flow even if sandboxed. Chosen in /sandbox Mode tab, saved to .claude/settings.local.json; autoAllowBashIfSandboxed defaults to true.
facts.limits: Even in auto-allow: Bash deny rules still block; rm/rmdir on critical paths still go through permission flow; content-scoped ask rules like Bash(git push *) still prompt; a bare Bash ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands (but not in plan mode); Monitor commands are not auto-approved; commands like FOO=bar npm test, make CC=clang, eval "ls" go through the regular flow. Auto-allow is separate from auto mode (classifier).

facts.feature: Unsandboxed retry (dangerouslyDisableSandbox) and strict sandbox mode
facts.behavior: When a command fails in the sandbox Claude may retry with dangerouslyDisableSandbox. Approval: bypassPermissions runs it without a prompt; manual/acceptEdits prompt ('Bash command (unsandboxed)'); auto mode uses the classifier; dontAsk denies; a matching allow rule (e.g. Bash(curl *)) also approves the retry. An ask rule Bash(dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true) forces a prompt in every mode. sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: false (strict sandbox mode, shown in /sandbox Overrides) makes Claude Code ignore the parameter.
facts.limits: With the retry disabled, commands still run unsandboxed if they match excludedCommands. Strict mode covers commands Claude runs; commands typed at the ! prompt run unsandboxed except in background sessions and Linux sessions with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB. A false in user, --settings or managed settings beats a project true (v2.1.285+). Disabling in managed settings or --settings makes the sandbox admin-required (repo settings that loosen it are ignored).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md (The unsandboxed retry escape hatch; Turn off the retry with strict sandbox mode)

facts.behavior: Command patterns (Bash(...) rule syntax; pattern without wildcard is an exact match; end with ' *' for arguments) run outside the sandbox, with no filesystem restrictions and no network proxy, then go through the regular permission flow (read-only and allow-listed commands run without prompt; classifier in auto mode).
facts.limits: Every command in a chained call must match; matching is on the call text (scripts or make targets that call docker internally do not match, nor /usr/local/bin/docker); calls with redirects, cd, or $(...) stay sandboxed. Under an admin-required sandbox, entries in .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json are ignored. Docs warn broad entries give full access.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md (Run commands outside the sandbox with excludedCommands)

facts.behavior: Declares credential files and environment variables to protect from sandboxed commands: deny blocks file reads (like denyRead) and unsets env vars before each sandboxed command; mask substitutes credentials (requires experimental network.tlsTerminate).
facts.limits: By default sandboxed commands inherit Claude Code's environment, including secrets, and can read ~/.ssh and ~/.aws. File protection is part of the filesystem layer and does not apply if filesystem.disabled; env-var protection still does. If managed settings configure sandbox.filesystem or any credentials.files deny, only managed settings can set filesystem.disabled.

facts.behavior: Managed settings can require the sandbox: enabled, failIfUnavailable (Claude Code refuses to start when sandbox unavailable), allowUnsandboxedCommands:false; managed Boolean keys override local values; array keys merge unless locked (allowManagedDomainsOnly etc.).
facts.limits: Docs: sandboxing 'reduces risk but is not a complete isolation boundary': TLS not inspected, Unix socket allowances (e.g. docker.sock) can enable bypass, broad write paths ($PATH dirs, shell rc files) enable escalation, enableWeakerNestedSandbox weakens Linux isolation, allowAppleEvents on macOS removes code-execution isolation (user/managed/CLI settings only). Subagents run in the same process with the parent's sandbox config; background sessions are sandboxed when their settings enable it. failIfUnavailable makes Claude Code exit on native Windows.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md (Configure the sandbox for your organization; Limitations)

facts.behavior: Claude Code can run a Bash command asynchronously and immediately return a background task ID; Ctrl+B (twice in tmux) moves a running Bash call or agent to the background; a command reaching its timeout is moved to the background instead of stopped (unless it starts with sleep). Output is written to a file Claude reads with the Read tool; /tasks shows running shells and subagents.
facts.limits: Cleaned up automatically when Claude Code exits (detached processes such as setsid/timeout also stopped on macOS/Linux); not restored on resume. Terminated if output exceeds 5GB. Stopped on critical OS memory pressure after 30 minutes idle with no turn/subagent running (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=1 turns off). No time limit in local interactive sessions; unattended (-p, cloud) sessions stop at a time limit. A background command started by a foreground subagent ends when that subagent's run ends. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 or --bare disables all background tasks (timeouts then stop the command).

facts.behavior: claude --bg starts a session in the background; sessions can be backgrounded from inside a session (left arrow on an empty prompt returns to agent view) with their background tasks continuing; claude agents/attach/logs/stop/rm manage them. Backgrounded --worktree sessions' worktrees become sweepable background-session worktrees. Strict sandbox mode also covers ! shell-mode commands in background sessions.
facts.limits: Interrupted background subagents/Bash from a previous process are not restarted on resume. claude --continue does not open a still-running background session. Menu rows unavailable in background sessions and -p runs for some features.

facts.behavior: Claude's to-do checklist (separate from the background task view); persists across context compactions; expanded view restored on --resume/--continue when tasks remain; CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID=<name> shares a task list across sessions via a named directory in ~/.claude/tasks/.
facts.limits: Task-tracking tools are on by default only on Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and earlier models; other models need CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 or similar opt-in. Not shared across sessions unless the env var is set.

facts.behavior: Typing Enter while Claude works queues the message (and most commands/! shell commands). Messages go to Claude after current tool calls finish in the same turn; commands run after the turn ends. Ctrl+Enter or Ctrl+X Ctrl+S sends queued items now (v2.1.275+); Up takes queued items back; Esc interrupts and sends queued items.
facts.limits: Some commands (/model, /effort, /fast, /status) run immediately instead of queueing. Mid-turn messages have no checkpoint of their own.

facts.behavior: Claude Code keeps a history of typed prompts; Up-arrow recall reaches prompts from past sessions of the same project. Input history is stored per working directory; Ctrl+R reverse search (fullscreen dialog scopes: session, project, all projects).
facts.limits: Duplicate consecutive prompts record once; history expansion with ! disabled by default; CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY suppresses writes.

facts.behavior: Asks a question answered from the existing conversation without adding to conversation history; works while Claude is working; no tool access; single response; replays newest 20 prior side exchanges; press f to fork into a background subagent.
facts.limits: Side questions and answers never enter conversation history; cannot read files or run commands; terminal thread is held in memory only.

facts.behavior: After 3+ minutes away with the terminal unfocused (and at least three turns), Claude Code shows a one-line recap generated in the background; /recap generates one on demand. Capped at 400 characters; on by default, toggle in /config.
facts.limits: Never appears in non-interactive mode; /recap only runs when you ask for it yourself (not from relayed messages or cloud scheduled-task prompts).

facts.feature: What carries between sessions (summary from fetched pages)
facts.behavior: Carries via transcript resume: conversation (from last compaction), model, agent, permission mode (with the exceptions above), active goal, unexpired session-scoped scheduled tasks, rewind checkpoints, task list view. Carries independent of resume: settings.json/settings.local.json re-read each launch; auto memory stored under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/; prompt history per working directory; shared task list via CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID; plugins and permission approvals shared across worktrees of a repo.
facts.limits: Does not carry: --mcp-config, --settings, --plugin-dir, --fallback-model, --add-dir and /add-dir directories, background Bash/monitor tasks, 'Allow for this session' permission grants in a separate --fork-session process, bypassPermissions mode. A compaction-summarized past is not reloaded. Auto memory and CLAUDE.md semantics are documented on pages outside this area's fetched set (memory page not fetched).

facts.behavior: claude --help lists: -c/--continue, -r/--resume, --fork-session, --session-id, -n/--name, -w/--worktree [name], --tmux, --bg/--background, --no-session-persistence (print mode only), --bare (skips hooks, auto-memory, CLAUDE.md discovery, background prefetches), --safe-mode (disables customizations), --restricted (removes command-running tools, confines file tools to working dirs), --system-prompt-snapshot on|off (records the system prompt once per conversation and reuses it on resume until compaction), --autocompact, --setting-sources, --add-dir, --settings.
facts.limits: --no-session-persistence only works with -p. --bare sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1 and turns off background tasks. --system-prompt-snapshot default on: a later launch with different --system-prompt text does not change a resumed conversation's prompt until compaction.
