https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view (background sessions detail; referenced but not fetched)
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory (retention sweep rules; referenced but not fetched)
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window (what survives compaction; referenced but not fetched)

area: subagents, agent definitions, model and effort selection, agent teams, workflows, how an omitted model is resolved

facts.behavior: Order: 1. per-invocation `model` parameter from Claude; 2. frontmatter `model` (`inherit` means the main model); 3. `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, if set; 4. the main conversation's model. An installed mod's `agent.spawn` hook can override the per-invocation parameter. Family aliases (`opus`) resolve to the main conversation's exact model, including `[1m]`, when the main model is in that family. `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` aliases always resolve to the version the alias points to.
facts.limits: Before v2.1.251, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL overrode frontmatter including inherit. Subagents that inherit pick up a /model switch when Claude starts them (session model as of start). Omitting model in a definition does not pin anything; it falls through to env var then main model.

facts.feature: Force one model for every subagent (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE)
facts.behavior: Set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL plus CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 (v2.1.257+): frontmatter `model` fields are ignored and Claude can't pass a model. Setting only FORCE makes subagents use the main model, except Explore, which keeps its listed model.
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.257+. Env var, so per-session/settings env, not per-agent. Also applies to teammates (first two sources dropped).

facts.behavior: The default model for subagents, agent team teammates, and workflow agents that aren't assigned a model another way. Accepts an alias such as haiku or a full model name. A per-invocation model or a definition's model field, including inherit, takes precedence.
facts.limits: Lower priority than per-invocation and frontmatter unless FORCE is set. Subject to availableModels allowlist.

facts.behavior: Only `name` and `description` required. Fields: tools, disallowedTools, model (sonnet/opus/haiku/fable/full ID/inherit), effort (low..max), permissionMode, maxTurns, autoCompactWindow (100000-1000000), skills (up to 32), mcpServers, hooks, memory (user/project/local), background, omitClaudeMd, isolation: worktree, initialPrompt, color, experimental.cacheTtl (5m/1h).
facts.limits: Fields are camelCase. Unknown fields are ignored silently; `claude --debug` reports them (v2.1.296+). permissionMode, mcpServers, hooks ignored for plugin agents. Files with no name, bad opening ---, invalid name, name without description, or unparseable YAML are skipped silently or with a debug log; `claude plugin validate <dir>` (v2.1.233+) checks. Names cannot contain `:` or start with `-`, max 256 chars.

facts.behavior: Priority: managed settings 1 (highest), --agents CLI flag 2, .claude/agents/ project 3, ~/.claude/agents/ user 4, plugin agents/ 5. Same-name resolved by priority. Project dirs scanned from working directory up to repo root, closest wins. Directories scanned recursively; identity comes only from `name`.
facts.limits: Duplicate names in one tree not reliably resolved (filesystem-dependent); /doctor reports them. Hot reload within seconds, but restart needed for first agent file in a new agents dir, --add-dir agents, or --disable-slash-commands sessions.

facts.behavior: Resolution order (first wins): explicit choice (CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, --effort, /effort); settings (per-model modelSettings or effortLevel); model default (high on most models, medium on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, xhigh on Opus 4.7). Skill and subagent frontmatter `effort` overrides the session level while that skill/subagent runs but does not override the environment variable. Organization and maxEffortLevel caps still apply (lower cap wins).
facts.limits: effortLevel in settings accepts low/medium/high/xhigh, not max. Unsupported levels fall back to highest supported at or below. Models not listed don't support effort. Teammates inherit the lead's effort by default.

facts.feature: Per-invocation effort parameter on Agent calls
facts.behavior: A per-invocation `effort` parameter (v2.1.292+) overrides the frontmatter field and persists across resumes.
facts.limits: Non-fork subagents only. CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL still takes precedence over frontmatter effort.

facts.behavior: Aliases: default, best, fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m], opus[1m], opusplan. On the Anthropic API: opus -> Opus 5.5, sonnet -> Sonnet 5.5, haiku -> Haiku 5.5; fable -> Fable 5.1. Bedrock/Agent Platform: opus 5.5, sonnet 4.5, haiku 4.5; Foundry: opus 4.6, sonnet 4.5, haiku 4.5; Claude Platform on AWS: opus 5.5, sonnet 4.6, haiku 4.5. Pin with full model name or ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL.
facts.limits: Sonnet 5.5 needs v2.1.284+, Opus 5.5 v2.1.280+, Haiku 5.5 v2.1.293+, Fable 5.1 v2.1.257+. On third-party providers unpinned aliases may lag newest release.

facts.feature: Session model selection priority and defaults
facts.behavior: Priority: /model during session; --model at startup; ANTHROPIC_MODEL; settings `model`; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL (v2.1.236+) for new sessions. Default model: Opus 5.5 on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise/API/AWS/Bedrock/Agent Platform; Sonnet 4.5 on Foundry. Fable is never the account-type default. Resumed sessions keep transcript model unless --model/ANTHROPIC_MODEL/ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL family var applies (v2.1.195+).
facts.limits: --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL apply only to that session. ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL ignored if set to default/inherit/opusplan/haiku, or enforceAvailableModels on.

facts.behavior: Uses opus in plan mode, then switches to sonnet for execution. Context window follows opus and sonnet; opusplan[1m] requests 1M for both.
facts.limits: If availableModels excludes newest Opus but permits an older one, plan mode uses newest permitted Opus (Anthropic API and Claude Platform on AWS only).

facts.behavior: Set in managed or policy settings; covers /model, --model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, model setting, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL, resume, alias vars, /fast, subagent and teammate models, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, skill and command models, advisorModel, background agents, fallbackModel, auto-mode classifier. /model rejects blocked model; --model/ANTHROPIC_MODEL/model setting replaced at startup with warning; subagents and teammates fall back to another model instead of failing (newest permitted version of a blocked family alias on Anthropic API/Claude Platform on AWS, else inherited model, with warning); skill/command overrides ignored and run on session model.
facts.limits: availableModels alone does not restrict the Default option; add enforceAvailableModels: true (v2.1.175+). User/project/local settings cannot extend a managed list. An entry naming a specific model disables that family's wildcard. [] blocks all named selections. deniedModels and availableModelsMatch: exact need v2.1.283+.

facts.behavior: `fallbackModel` setting or `--fallback-model sonnet,haiku`: a chain of up to three models tried in order when the primary is overloaded, unavailable, or returns a non-retryable server error. The chain also applies to subagents (v2.1.247+); a switched agent's report starts with a warning that it switched model.
facts.limits: Auth, billing, rate-limit, request-size errors do not trigger it. Switch lasts the current turn only.

facts.feature: Automatic model fallback on safety classifiers
facts.behavior: Fable models, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5 may refuse cybersecurity or biology content; flagged requests re-run on a fallback model (e.g. Sonnet 5.5 cyber flags re-run on Sonnet 5; biology refused on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5).
facts.limits: switchModelsOnFlag: false or /config 'Ask each time' prompts before switching.

facts.behavior: Explore (read-only, Write/Edit denied, quick/medium/very thorough, skips CLAUDE.md and git status; model is Opus alias on subscription/Console/gateway setups, main model on Bedrock etc.); Plan (read-only, inherits main model, skips CLAUDE.md and git status); general-purpose (all subagent-available tools); claude (catch-all, follows model order, default for dispatched background sessions); statusline-setup (Sonnet); claude-code-guide (Haiku).
facts.limits: Explore and Plan are one-shot and cannot be resumed. Deny with `Agent(Explore)` in permissions.deny or --disallowedTools; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1 (v2.1.198+) removes Explore/Plan; CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1 removes all in non-interactive/SDK. An Agent call without subagent_type fails if no general-purpose agent exists.

facts.behavior: `tools` is an allowlist (inherits all subagent-available tools if omitted; fails to launch if nothing resolves). `disallowedTools` denylist applied first; a specifier like Bash(git push *) removes the whole tool. Always removed: Agent at depth limit, AskUserQuestion, EndConversation, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode (unless permissionMode plan), ScheduleWakeup, WaitForMcpServers, Workflow. Background subagents keep only a fixed built-in set plus all MCP tools.
facts.limits: `Agent(worker, researcher)` in tools restricts spawnable types only for the main-thread agent (--agent); in subagent definitions the type list is ignored. The same definition can resolve differently foreground vs background. Subagents (and so workflow agents) cannot call Workflow.

facts.behavior: If the main session is bypassPermissions, acceptEdits, or auto, the subagent runs in that mode and ignores permissionMode. Under default, dontAsk, or plan, the subagent uses its own permissionMode, except bypassPermissions (v2.1.267+) and auto when unavailable keep the main mode. dontAsk auto-denies prompts.
facts.limits: permissionMode ignored for plugin agents. Background agents surface permission prompts in the main session.

facts.feature: Hooks scoped to subagents and SubagentStart/SubagentStop
facts.behavior: Frontmatter hooks run only while the agent is active; Stop converted to SubagentStop. PreToolUse exit code 2 blocks (e.g. read-only SQL validator). settings.json supports SubagentStart/SubagentStop with matchers on agent name. Tool hooks in settings apply inside subagents too.
facts.limits: Frontmatter hooks in project agents require trusting the folder (parent folder trust not enough; -p sessions don't count); skipped and logged until trusted. Ignored for plugin agents. The system prompt asking the agent to refuse is advisory; the hook is the enforcement backstop.

facts.behavior: A non-fork subagent starts with its own system prompt plus environment details (not the Claude Code system prompt), the delegation message, CLAUDE.md files (except Explore, Plan, and omitClaudeMd agents), git status snapshot, preloaded skills, and a sibling roster when it has SendMessage. It does not receive conversation history, invoked skills, already-read files, output style, or main auto memory.
facts.limits: omitClaudeMd: true skips user/project/local CLAUDE.md (managed policy still loads). Docs say: restate any rule the subagent must follow in the delegation prompt. Context window size comes from its own model.

facts.behavior: Subagents can spawn subagents up to 3 layers deep by default; CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH sets the limit (1 disables nesting). Default concurrent limit is 20 Claude-spawned agents; CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS changes it (v2.1.217+).
facts.limits: Ultracode sessions exempt from the concurrent limit; forks via /subtask never blocked but occupy slots; resumes bypass limit. At depth limit Agent is withheld (except forks).

facts.behavior: Agents Claude spawns from the main conversation start in the background by default (fork mode on by default; from v2.1.302, and in interactive terminal from v2.1.232). Forks (/subtask or Claude-initiated) inherit full conversation, system prompt, tools, model, history and share the parent's prompt cache; only the result returns. A fork cannot spawn further forks.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 turns fork mode off and lets Claude wait; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 makes Claude wait. While fork mode is on Claude cannot wait for a subagent in interactive sessions. Forks skip tool filters; per-invocation effort not for forks. `Agent(fork)` in permissions.deny stops forks.

facts.behavior: SendMessage with name or agent ID resumes a completed agent in the background with full history and original tool set. Claude can name a subagent via Agent tool's `name`. Transcripts at ~/.claude/projects/{project}/{sessionId}/subagents/agent-{agentId}.jsonl, deleted after cleanupPeriodDays (30 default). Messages from another agent are task direction but cannot approve permission prompts or change permissions, CLAUDE.md, or config.
facts.limits: Cannot resume an agent you stopped yourself; Explore/Plan cannot be resumed; SendMessage refuses names taken by a newer agent.

facts.behavior: Final reports are scanned for imitation of Claude Code tags and permission-related text; the scan may insert a backslash or prepend a `[harness: subagent output matched...]` marker and never removes content. Reports are labeled as subagent output with no authority from the user.
facts.limits: Not a security boundary; permissions and sandboxing still apply.

facts.behavior: Agent gets a temporary git worktree branched from the default branch (not the session's HEAD); removed automatically if no changes made. A cd in one Bash call doesn't persist; commands resolving to the main checkout fail; Bash commands redirecting git into the main checkout are blocked; commands whose git target can't be verified from text (runtime-computed command names) are refused. If the main session runs in a worktree, checks apply to every subagent it spawns.
facts.limits: PowerShell gets only the working-directory check. Applies only to agents with isolation: worktree (or call-level isolation), not other subagents.

facts.behavior: memory: user (~/.claude/agent-memory/<name>/), project (.claude/agent-memory/<name>/), local (.claude/agent-memory-local/<name>/). Adds read/write instructions, first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md, and Read/Write/Edit tools.
facts.limits: No effect when auto memory is off.

facts.behavior: Inline definitions connect at subagent start and disconnect at finish; string references share parent's connection. --strict-mcp-config, --bare, managed MCP, allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers apply.
facts.limits: Inline servers from a project agent file load only after trusting the folder (v2.1.238+); user-level, --agents, and managed definitions skip this check.

facts.behavior: Claude uses each subagent's description to decide when to delegate. Combined descriptions over 15,000 tokens trigger a startup warning.
facts.limits: Warning only; put detail in the body, which loads only when the agent runs.

facts.behavior: Auto-compaction triggers on the subagent's own context window; CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE applies; autoCompactWindow sets per-agent window (CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW takes precedence). maxTurns stops the agent; output marked partial and can be resumed. Subagents inherit the main session's extended thinking setting (v2.1.198+).
facts.limits: autoCompactWindow no effect when run as main session via --agent; split-pane teammates ignore it; requires v2.1.296+.

facts.feature: Running an agent as the whole session (--agent / agent setting)
facts.behavior: `claude --agent code-reviewer` or `agent` key in .claude/settings.json (CLI flag overrides). The agent's prompt replaces the default system prompt unless empty; choice persists on resume. @-mention `@"name (agent)"` guarantees that agent runs.
facts.limits: @-mention still sends full message to Claude, which writes the task prompt. Plugin agents need `plugin:name` to disambiguate.

facts.behavior: Experimental and disabled by default. Enable with CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1. Without it no team is set up, no team directories are written, and Claude does not spawn or propose teammates. While enabled, a subagent that Claude names launches as a teammate (unless a fork or call-level isolation), and Claude Code does not ask you to confirm the launch.
facts.limits: Requires interactive session; with -p / Agent SDK, named subagents run as ordinary subagents. Set variable to 0 in settings to make named subagents launch as subagents again (managed/higher-precedence settings can still enable).

facts.behavior: First that applies: 1. model the spawn prompt names; 2. subagent definition's model (inherit = lead's model); 3. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (if not inherit); 4. the lead's current model. mod agent.spawn hook can replace source 1. With CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 the first two don't apply. Teammates inherit lead's effort by default.
facts.limits: `teammateDefaultModel` removed in v2.1.234 (ignored). A teammate's model and fast mode are fixed at spawn; /model and /fast from a teammate view set the lead's, not teammate's. Subject to availableModels with substitution.

facts.behavior: Applies definition's tools (adds SendMessage and Task tools for in-process), model, disallowedTools (in-process), effort (in-process), autoCompactWindow (in-process), body (appended to default system prompt for in-process; replaces it for split-pane).
facts.limits: `skills` and, for in-process, `mcpServers` from the definition are NOT applied; teammate loads skills/MCP from project and user settings. Project-scope definitions re-applied on restore only if folder trusted.

facts.behavior: Teammates start with the lead's permission mode, except dontAsk, which they don't inherit. If lead runs --dangerously-skip-permissions all teammates do. Teammate permission prompts appear in the lead session. Plan approval: a teammate spawned while lead is in plan mode works read-only until plan ready; Claude Code approves the plan in the lead's session as soon as the request arrives, without the lead reviewing it.
facts.limits: Cannot set per-teammate permission modes at spawn (can change after). Teammates can't approve permission prompts or supply user consent; in auto mode the classifier treats relayed approval claims as untrusted and reviews each inter-agent message before delivery.

facts.feature: Agent team architecture, tasks, and limitations
facts.behavior: Lead, teammates, shared task list, mailbox (JSON at ~/.claude/teams/{team}/inboxes/). Tasks pending/in progress/completed with dependencies; claiming uses file locking. Team config removed at session end; task list at ~/.claude/tasks/{team}/ stays (cleanupPeriodDays). Teammates load CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills; lead's history does not carry over.
facts.limits: No /resume or /rewind restore of in-process teammates; task status can lag; one team per session; no nested teams (teammates cannot spawn teammates); in-process teammates' own subagents run foreground (background: true errors); lead fixed; split panes need tmux or iTerm2 (not VS Code terminal, Windows Terminal, Ghostty). Do not edit team config by hand. No hard teammate-count limit; docs suggest 3-5 (advisory).

facts.behavior: TeammateIdle (exit 2 keeps teammate working with feedback), TaskCreated (exit 2 prevents creation), TaskCompleted (exit 2 prevents completion).
facts.limits: Apply to agent teams only.

facts.behavior: teammateMode setting / --teammate-mode: in-process (default), auto, tmux, iterm2.
facts.limits: Split-pane requires tmux or iTerm2 with it2.

facts.behavior: Agent teams use significantly more tokens than a single session; costs page says approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode. Docs advise: use Sonnet for teammates, keep teams small, keep spawn prompts focused, shut down teammates when done. In-process teammate cache TTL is 5 minutes by default; subagentPromptCacheTtl=1h extends it (higher write rate).
facts.limits: All advisory; nothing caps teammate count or token use.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs.md (Agent team token costs; Manage agent team costs); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams.md

facts.behavior: A JavaScript script that orchestrates many subagents; Claude writes it, a runtime executes it in the background; intermediate results stay in script variables. Started by asking for a workflow, the `ultracode` keyword (typed prompts only), `/effort ultracode`, a bundled workflow (/deep-research), or a saved workflow. Saved to .claude/workflows/ or ~/.claude/workflows/ (project wins on name clash); plugin workflows namespaced.
facts.limits: Up to 16 concurrent agents by default (CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS 1-256, v2.1.269+); 4,096 items per parallel()/pipeline(); 1,000 agents total per run; no mid-run user input; no direct filesystem/shell from the script; import() fails. Keyword does not trigger via -p, unstamped SDK prompts, scheduled tasks, webhooks. Script can only be started from a file the session may read. Date.now/Math.random throw in scripts.

facts.behavior: Each workflow agent's model is picked in the same order as subagents; a model the script names for a stage counts as the per-invocation model. When nothing else assigns one, the agent runs on the session's model. availableModels substitution applies. A `Large workflow` warning appears in the task panel when more than 25 agents are scheduled or projected tokens exceed 1.5 million.
facts.limits: Warning is advisory and does not pause or limit the run; not shown with ultracode on. workflowSizeGuideline (unrestricted/small<5/medium<10/large<50, default medium, small on Pro) is advice to Claude, not a cap. Docs advise checking /model before a large run and asking for a smaller model for light stages.

facts.behavior: Per-run prompt shows phases (Yes / Yes and don't ask again / View raw script / No). Auto mode: first launch only (skipped with ultracode). Manual/accept edits: every run unless 'don't ask again'. Bypass permissions and claude -p / Agent SDK: no prompt; -p runs the Workflow call through normal permission evaluation (allow `Workflow` rules, auto mode, hook allow, etc.). Workflow agents use the session's permission rules and normal sandboxing.
facts.limits: The ultracode keyword only chooses structure; it does not change permissions.

facts.feature: Workflow resume, stall handling, usage-limit pause
facts.behavior: Runs resumable in same session: completed agents return saved results until the first changed or failed agent, after which all later agents rerun. Stalled agents restart automatically up to 5 times (stallMs / CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS). Usage-limit hit pauses run (v2.1.271+) if interactive claude.ai session, autoContinueAtUsageLimit on, reset within 24h, waited fewer than twice.
facts.limits: No pause in -p, SDK, background session, Remote Control, or agent team teammate; affected agent fails instead.

facts.behavior: Toggle in /config, `disableWorkflows: true` in settings (also in managed settings), or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1. When disabled, /workflows, workflow commands, /workflow-authoring unavailable, ultracode keyword and toggle removed.
facts.limits: An in-progress run keeps going. No managed setting disables ultracode alone; effort caps lower the effort level but not turn ultracode off.

facts.behavior: A Claude Code setting (not an effort level) that turns on automatic workflow orchestration for the session at any effort level; `/effort ultracode`, `--effort ultracode` (also sets xhigh), or `ultracode: true` setting. Claude plans a workflow for each substantive task.
facts.limits: With ultracode on: Large workflow warning not shown, concurrent subagent limit not enforced for Agent-tool subagents, auto-mode first-launch approval skipped. Uses more tokens per request.

facts.behavior: Fable, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7+ always use adaptive reasoning; thinking cannot be turned off on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable. `ultrathink` in a prompt requests deeper reasoning for that turn without changing session effort. Thinking tokens billed as output tokens.
facts.limits: MAX_THINKING_TOKENS only applies on fixed-budget models (Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1); adaptive models ignore nonzero budgets, use effort instead.

facts.behavior: Fable 5.1/5, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7+ use 1M window by default with no suffix; Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 need [1m]. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 removes [1m] variants and treats default-1M models as 200K.
facts.limits: Plan/usage-credit access restrictions apply to 4.6 1M; Haiku 5.5 costs more per token over 100K prompts.

facts.feature: Cost guidance: model choice and subagent delegation
facts.behavior: Docs: Sonnet handles most coding tasks and costs less than Opus; reserve Opus for complex architectural decisions or multi-step reasoning; for simple subagent tasks specify `model: haiku`; a switch to Opus also applies to subagents that inherit the session model. Delegate verbose operations (tests, docs, logs) to subagents so only a summary returns; subagent requests still draw on usage; choose a smaller model or run every subagent on one model. Use plan mode for complex tasks to avoid rework.
facts.limits: All advisory; nothing enforces a model choice. Costs page also notes unexpected high API spend usually traces to long uncleared sessions or Opus left as default.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs.md (Choose the right model; Delegate verbose operations to subagents; Work efficiently on complex tasks)

facts.behavior: /usage shows Session block (cost computed locally at list price unless modelPricing managed setting), prompt-cache line for main conversation only (not subagents), plan usage breakdown attributing usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, with recommendations and `f` fix shortcut (v2.1.305+; runs /effort commands, gives Claude steps for other rows). Spinner token count covers current turn output including foreground subagents. /insights reports on sessions. Status line can show cost and prompt_cache.
facts.limits: Dollar figure is an estimate; /usage Session block cost not relevant for Pro/Max billing; figures from this machine only; `f` only acts on some rows.

facts.feature: Cost controls: context, hooks, skills, MCP
facts.behavior: Docs advise: /clear between tasks, custom compaction instructions, keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines and move workflow-specific instructions to skills (load on demand), PreToolUse hooks to preprocess output (e.g. filter test output), prefer CLI tools over MCP, disable unused MCP servers (MCP tool definitions deferred by default), code intelligence plugins, specific prompts. Prompt caching and auto-compaction are automatic.
facts.limits: Guidance is advisory except prompt caching/auto-compaction (automatic). Long-session usage climbs from long context, cache misses after cache lifetime, scheduled tasks, cross-session messages, goal check-ins (max 3 idle per goal), subagents/workflows, teammates, compaction.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs.md (Reduce token usage; Why usage climbs in a long session)

facts.behavior: Teams/Enterprise: seat allowance with five-hour and weekly windows, usage credits, spend limits at org/group/member level. Console: workspace spend limits, 'Claude Code' workspace, rate-limit recommendations table (TPM/RPM per user by team size). Cloud providers: your cloud billing; OpenTelemetry or gateway for attribution. modelPricing managed setting changes reported figures only.
facts.limits: Rate-limit table is a recommendation; limits apply at org level not per user. Claude Code does not send metrics from cloud providers to Anthropic.

facts.behavior: Automatic prompt caching. DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 disables for all models; per-tier DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU/SONNET/OPUS/FABLE. Subagent cache TTL set via subagentPromptCacheTtl / experimental.cacheTtl (5m or 1h). Forks reuse parent's cache; non-fork subagents have a separate cache; workflow agents with identical model/effort/agent type/tools/schema/cwd share prefix cache (stagger up to CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS, default 5000).
facts.limits: Subagent/teammate/workflow cache default 5 minutes, even on subscription; 1h cache writes billed at higher rate.

area: git and GitHub integration: commits, PR creation, GitHub app and Actions, code review, branch handling, worktree branches

facts.feature: Commits and PR creation by asking Claude
facts.behavior: You can create pull requests by asking Claude directly ("create a pr for my changes"), or guide Claude step by step. Docs say: "Review Claude's generated PR before submitting and ask Claude to highlight potential risks or considerations." Session is linked to the PR when Claude creates it with `gh pr create` or `glab mr create`, and when Claude works on an existing PR.
facts.limits: Docs give prompt recipes only. They describe no built-in commit-message format rule, no required branch, and no default-branch push block in these pages. Commit-message format and attribution are not documented in these four pages.

facts.behavior: `claude --from-pr 123` opens the session picker filtered to sessions linked to a specific pull request. Accepts a PR number, a GitHub or GitHub Enterprise PR URL, a GitLab merge request URL, or a Bitbucket pull request URL. Sessions are linked automatically when Claude creates the pull request.
facts.limits: Opens a picker, not a direct resume. Linking happens on `gh pr create` / `glab mr create` or when working on an existing PR.

facts.behavior: Installs the Claude GitHub App, sets an authentication secret (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) as a repository secret, pushes a branch with selected workflow files and opens GitHub in browser with a PR ready to create. Requires GitHub CLI authenticated with `gh auth login` (warns if missing) and admin access to the repository. Esc stops setup partway; a step in progress finishes.
facts.limits: Works only with github.com repositories; on gitlab.com or bitbucket.org remotes it prints a notice and exits. Quick setup works with Claude API and subscriptions; Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry need the cloud-provider page. You must create and merge the setup PR yourself. Re-running with an existing claude.yml offers 'Update workflow file with latest version'.

facts.behavior: Install the Claude GitHub App, add secret ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (generated with `claude setup-token`), copy examples/claude.yml into .github/workflows/. App permissions the Action relies on: Contents, Issues, Pull requests (read and write).
facts.limits: Needs admin access to repository. Org rollout: install app at org level, org-level Actions secret, workflow per repo or reusable workflow. OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran setup-token, so shared secrets should use an API key. Workload identity federation (OIDC) inputs exist (anthropic_federation_rule_id etc.) and need id-token: write.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions.md (Manual setup, Set up for an organization)

facts.behavior: The Claude GitHub App is shared by the Action, Code Review, and auto-fix for PRs in cloud sessions. Permissions: Actions rw, Administration r, Checks rw, Contents rw, Discussions rw, Issues rw, Members r, Merge queues r, Metadata r, Pull requests rw, Repository hooks rw, Statuses r, Workflows rw. 'When you install the app, you accept its full permission set. GitHub doesn't let you accept a subset.'
facts.limits: A custom GitHub App (Contents, Issues, Pull requests) covers only the Action, not Code Review or web auto-fix. New permissions require owner approval and installation keeps old permissions until approved.

facts.feature: Claude Code GitHub Action: interactive mode (@claude)
facts.behavior: With no `prompt` input, Claude waits for the trigger phrase (`@claude` by default, `trigger_phrase` input) in an issue or PR comment, PR review, or body/title of a newly opened issue, then responds; progress and results appear as a comment. Claude can analyze code, implement changes, and push commits. Trigger must be the complete word `@claude`, not `/claude` or `@claude-bot`.
facts.limits: Needs the workflow file in the repo; the `if: contains(...)` is a runner-saving filter and the Action also checks the phrase itself. Workflow permissions in example: contents/pull-requests/issues write, id-token write, actions read.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions.md (Interactive and automation modes; Respond to @claude mentions; Troubleshooting)

facts.feature: Claude Code GitHub Action: automation mode (prompt input)
facts.behavior: When the workflow provides a `prompt` input, Claude runs without waiting for a mention on any GitHub event including cron. By default results appear in the workflow run log, not a comment. Claude can post to the issue/PR only when the prompt directs it and it has a tool that can post.
facts.limits: For a plain-text prompt, Claude has no shell or GitHub API access until you grant tools via `--allowedTools` in `claude_args` or `permissions.allow` in the `settings` input. A skill invocation can use its own `allowed-tools` frontmatter. Scheduled workflows run only from the default branch; in public repos the schedule is disabled after 60 days without repo activity.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions.md (Interactive and automation modes; Run on a schedule)

facts.behavior: Two checks before Claude starts, run fails if either rejects: (1) Write access: on issue and PR events the triggering user must have write access (override with `allowed_non_write_users` plus your own `github_token`); events no user authors, such as schedule, skip it. (2) Human actor: on every event a bot actor is rejected unless listed in `allowed_bots`, which keeps bots from triggering Claude in a loop.
facts.limits: Scheduled runs are attributed to the user who last changed the cron; if a bot, list it in allowed_bots.

facts.feature: Action: skills and plugins as prompt; code-review plugin workflow
facts.behavior: `prompt` accepts a skill invocation. Repo skills in .claude/skills need actions/checkout first; plugin skills need `plugin_marketplaces` and `plugins` inputs and a namespaced prompt `/plugin-name:skill-name`. Example installs `code-review@claude-code-plugins` and runs `/code-review:code-review --comment <repo>/pull/<n>` on opened/synchronize/ready_for_review/reopened. Quick-setup review workflow posts each review on the PR (inline comment per issue, or one summary comment when none); before v2.1.229 it wrote only to the workflow run log.
facts.limits: Without `--comment`, Claude posts nothing and findings are only in the run log. `--allowedTools "mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment"` in claude_args is required because the Action starts the inline-comment MCP server only when named there. Claude skips draft and closed PRs, PRs it judges not to need review (automated or trivial), and PRs that already have a comment from Claude. On public repos GitHub withholds secrets from fork PR runs, so review runs only for same-repo branches.

facts.feature: Action: CI does not run on Claude's commits with GITHUB_TOKEN
facts.behavior: Docs: 'GitHub doesn't trigger workflows on commits made with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`.' Fix: omit `github_token` so the Action authenticates as the Claude GitHub App, or pass a custom app token. Default (no github_token) authenticates as the Claude GitHub App.
facts.limits: CI workflow triggers must include events Claude's pushes produce (push, pull_request).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions.md (Troubleshooting: CI not running on Claude's commits)

facts.behavior: Docs: create a CLAUDE.md in the repository root for style, review criteria, project rules; 'Claude follows these guidelines when creating PRs and responding to requests.' Cost controls named: specific requests, issue templates, concise CLAUDE.md (read every run), `--max-turns` in claude_args, workflow-level timeouts, GitHub concurrency controls. Credentials: never commit keys, use GitHub Secrets; grant only needed permissions and review Claude's changes before merging.
facts.limits: All advisory guidance; the Action does not enforce a human review before merge. `claude_args` accepts any CLI argument (--max-turns, --model, --mcp-config, --allowedTools, --debug).

facts.feature: Action: cloud providers and beta upgrade
facts.behavior: `use_bedrock`, `use_vertex`, `use_foundry` inputs route inference through the cloud provider using OIDC federation. Upgrade from @beta to @v1: remove `mode`, replace `direct_prompt` with `prompt`, move CLI options into `claude_args`.
facts.limits: Details are on a separate cloud-providers page not read here.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions.md (Use a cloud provider; Upgrade from beta)

facts.feature: Code Review managed service (GitHub PR review)
facts.behavior: Several agents review each PR on Anthropic infrastructure: Find, Verify (filters false positives), Rank, Post. Findings arrive as inline comments ranked by severity, a summary in the review body, and a check run named 'Claude Code Review'. Default focus is correctness: 'bugs that would break production, not formatting preferences or missing test coverage.' Models are chosen by the service; thoroughness via review level Quick/Standard (default)/Deep set by an Owner, per org or per repo.
facts.limits: Team and Enterprise plans only; GitHub (incl. GHES and GHE Cloud with data residency) only; not available with Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configuration, or CMEK. 'A review never approves or blocks the pull request'; the check run 'doesn't conclude as a failure' (neutral, or skipped if a push changed no files). Read-only access to repo, does not push commits, does not build or run your code, does not run in self-hosted environments. It can resolve its own earlier comment threads. AI may miss bugs.

facts.behavior: Three markers: Important (red, 'A bug that should be fixed before merging'), Nit (yellow, 'minor issue, worth fixing but not blocking'), Pre-existing (purple, 'A bug that exists in the codebase but wasn't introduced by this PR'). Optional collapsed 'Why this was flagged' section.
facts.limits: Severity is advisory; nothing gates merge. To gate, parse the check run Details last line `<!-- bughunter-severity: {...} -->` with gh and jq in your own CI (`normal` key = Important count); a missing line means no verdict, not zero findings.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review-pull-requests.md (Severity levels; Read the result from a script)

facts.feature: Code Review: when reviews run and comment commands
facts.behavior: Per-repo setting: once when a PR opens, after every push, or only on request (Manual). Someone with write access can comment `@claude review` (single review), `@claude review always` (subscribe to push-triggered reviews), `@claude review once`, `@claude review stop|off|pause` (unsubscribe). A later automatic review focuses on what changed since the last review and posts fewer nits and pre-existing findings; `@claude review` covers the whole PR again.
facts.limits: Command must be a new top-level PR comment, whole command on one line at start, commenter needs write/maintain/admin permission, bots ignored, PR must be open. Automatic reviews skip draft PRs and fork PRs (fork needs `@claude review`; `always` doesn't subscribe on forks; Re-run does not work on forks). A new request does not start a second review if one is already running on the latest commit. In 'After every push' mode you cannot stop reviews by comment, only by converting to draft. If the repo also runs the GitHub Action with default `@claude` trigger, `@claude review` also starts the Action; set a different `trigger_phrase` to avoid.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review-pull-requests.md (Comment commands; Review drafts and forks; Use alongside the Action)

facts.behavior: To dismiss without a code change, resolve the thread on GitHub ('Replying alone doesn't dismiss a finding'). Pushing a fix lets the next review resolve its earlier thread. A reply does not start a review; the next review reads replies and may resolve or post one follow-up reply. Findings whose inline comment GitHub rejected appear in the check run table or as Files changed annotations.
facts.limits: You can merge without responding unless branch protection requires conversation resolution.

facts.feature: Customize Code Review with REVIEW.md and CLAUDE.md
facts.behavior: The service reads CLAUDE.md (root plus parent directories of each changed file; a subdirectory CLAUDE.md when the PR changes a file under it) as project context and flags violations. REVIEW.md at repo root (and subdirectory REVIEW.md files) gives review-only rules: recalibrate severity, cap nits, skip paths, add checks, require evidence. Root REVIEW.md can include up to eight other root-level files via a line containing only `@filename`.
facts.limits: REVIEW.md is read from the PR's base branch or default branch, 'never from the pull request's own changes'. Honored instructions from the root file (lower severity, exclude paths, cap nits) apply only when read from a protected default branch; branch protection means classic rule or ruleset on the default branch, ruleset only on other branches. If protection cannot be confirmed no REVIEW.md is read; an unprotected default branch reads root file only (no includes, no subdirectory files). Includes: root only, one level, max eight files, 150,000 bytes combined, over 64 Markdown links skips the whole root REVIEW.md. The local /code-review command reads CLAUDE.md but not REVIEW.md.

facts.feature: Comparison of ways to get a review
facts.behavior: Options: Code Review service (Team/Enterprise, GitHub, Anthropic infra); `/code-review` in your session (any plan, runs in your session; see code-review-local page); Ultrareview (cloud sandbox, requires claude.ai sign-in); Claude in your own CI via GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD (your runners, anyone with API key or cloud creds); your own reviewer as a subagent or skill.
facts.limits: Details of /code-review and ultrareview are on separate pages not read here.

facts.behavior: `claude ultrareview [target]` runs ultrareview non-interactively, prints findings to stdout, exits 0 on success or 1 on failure. `--json` for raw payload, `--timeout <minutes>` overrides 45-minute default. `--post` on a github.com PR target posts the finished findings to the PR as one plain comment from your GitHub account; `--no-post` is the default (--post/--no-post need v2.1.227+).
facts.limits: Posting only for github.com PR targets; requires claude.ai sign-in per the review comparison table.

facts.behavior: Starts Claude in an isolated git worktree at `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`, on a new branch named `worktree-<name>`. If no name is given Claude generates one (e.g. bright-running-fox). Passing the same name opens the existing worktree. A worktree is created from an existing commit, so the repo needs at least one commit (otherwise `Failed to resolve base branch "HEAD": git rev-parse failed`).
facts.limits: Interactive runs require workspace trust (otherwise exits with an error); `-p` skips the trust check. Docs tip (advisory): add `.claude/worktrees/` to .gitignore. Git-only unless WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks are configured. Refuses to create a worktree when `.claude`, `.claude/worktrees`, or the worktree dir is a symlink.

facts.behavior: New worktrees branch from the repository's default branch on the remote (`"fresh"`, default, usually main). `"head"` branches from current local HEAD (carries unpushed commits; inside a worktree resolves to that worktree's HEAD). For fresh, Claude Code fetches the default branch if not fetched in the last 24 hours (capped at five seconds, falls back to cached ref) and falls back to local HEAD if no remote or origin/HEAD unavailable. Subagent worktrees use the same base.
facts.limits: `worktree.baseRef` cannot be a branch name; to start from a specific existing branch use `git worktree add` directly. Fetch never prompts for passwords/passphrases/host confirmation.

facts.feature: Worktree from a PR/MR (--worktree '#1234' or URL)
facts.behavior: `--worktree` accepts `#<number>`, a GitHub PR URL, or a GitLab MR URL. Fetches the head commit from `origin` and creates the worktree at `.claude/worktrees/pr-<number>`. github.com fetches `pull/<number>/head`; gitlab.com `merge-requests/<number>/head`; other hosts try pull first then merge-requests.
facts.limits: Reads only the number from the URL and always fetches from `origin`. Fetch fails (exit with 'Error creating worktree: Failed to fetch PR/MR #<n>') if git/ssh would prompt. GitLab MR support needs v2.1.233+. Quote `#` in shell. A PR/MR reference name is always reopened at its old tip.

facts.behavior: Asking Claude to 'work in a worktree' creates one with the EnterWorktree tool; Claude can switch to another worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` by passing the target path (previous one stays on disk). ExitWorktree exits one.
facts.limits: Entering a path outside the repository's `.claude/worktrees/` directory asks for your approval; an EnterWorktree permission rule or 'don't ask again' does not suppress the prompt, only bypassPermissions mode does (v2.1.206+). `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in hooks stays at project root after entering; hook input `cwd` follows the worktree.

facts.behavior: On exit of an interactive worktree session Claude checks for changed/untracked files, uncommitted work in submodules, and new commits. Clean + unnamed session: worktree and its branch removed automatically. Clean + named session: prompts first. Has work: prompts keep or remove (removing deletes directory and branch with the work). State cannot be verified: prompts rather than auto-removing.
facts.limits: Applies to worktrees Claude created with git; WorktreeCreate-hook worktrees use WorktreeRemove. `-p` runs have no exit prompt: no cleanup, lock left until a later stale-lock sweep; remove manually with `git worktree remove` (and `git worktree unlock` if locked).

facts.behavior: While a session is isolated in a worktree, Claude Code blocks: (1) Edit/Write/NotebookEdit targeting a path in the main checkout; (2) Bash/PowerShell/Monitor commands whose working directory resolves to the main checkout or cannot be verified to stay outside it; (3) Bash/Monitor commands that redirect git into the main checkout via `git -C`, `--git-dir`, `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`, or `cd` into main checkout before git; (4) Bash/Monitor commands when it cannot verify from the command text that any git stays inside the worktree (computed command names, unparseable syntax, expansions like `${!name}`). Covers sessions started with --worktree, EnterWorktree, or resumed, and every subagent spawned from the isolated session, interactive or background.
facts.limits: The command-shape check 'You can't turn this check off.' None of the checks track which files a shell command writes: `cp` or a shell redirect into the main checkout without running git there is not refused (falls to normal permissions and sandboxing). For PowerShell only the working-directory check applies. Checks cover the repo launched from and the main checkout a linked worktree is linked from.

facts.behavior: Ask Claude to 'use worktrees for your agents' or set `isolation: worktree` in a custom subagent's frontmatter. Each subagent gets a temporary worktree removed automatically when it finishes without changes; one with changes stays until the periodic sweep can remove it without losing work. Uses the same base branch setting as --worktree.
facts.limits: A subagent in its own worktree takes startup instruction files from the main conversation; when the worktree is under .claude/worktrees/ it does not load that worktree's root CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/ as it reads files there.

facts.behavior: Claude Code removes worktrees it created for subagents and background sessions once older than `cleanupPeriodDays`. Holds a `git worktree lock` while an agent runs; the sweep releases locks Claude set for exited processes.
facts.limits: Sweep keeps a worktree that still holds work (changed/untracked files or unpushed commits), has dirty submodules (v2.1.274+), belongs to a non-backgrounded --worktree session, was created by you with `git worktree add`, or lacks Claude's marker in git metadata (including WorktreeCreate-hook worktrees). Never releases a lock you set yourself. Does not sweep worktrees of unbackgrounded `--worktree` sessions regardless of age.

facts.behavior: A `.worktreeinclude` file at project root (gitignore syntax) copies gitignored files such as .env into every worktree Claude Code creates with git (--worktree, subagent worktrees, desktop parallel sessions).
facts.limits: Only files that match a pattern AND are gitignored are copied; tracked files never duplicated. Not processed when a WorktreeCreate hook is used (copy inside the hook). `**/` patterns reach into wholly-ignored directories only under stated conditions.

facts.feature: Worktree reuse and reset on reopen
facts.behavior: Passing --worktree a name whose directory exists opens that worktree. With baseRef fresh, a reopened worktree resets to the default branch if: no uncommitted changes/untracked files, still on the branch Claude Code created, and no commits of its own or its PR/MR was merged and remote branch deleted.
facts.limits: Otherwise reopens at old tip (also when baseRef is head, state unverifiable, or name is a PR/MR reference). Before v2.1.208 always reopened at old tip.

facts.behavior: Resuming a session that ended inside a worktree (without exiting it) returns the session to that worktree, including `--continue`/`--resume` with `-p` and the Agent SDK. Claude Code verifies the worktree is still a separate checkout and declines otherwise. `--fork-session` starts in the launch directory. Deleted worktree: resumes in launch directory and clears binding. `claude --worktree <name> --resume` is printed on exit when keeping a worktree. `--resume <session-id>` searches the current project dir and its git worktrees, then other projects.
facts.limits: Non-interactive resume stops with an error for every refusal except a gone worktree. Never resumes into a worktree at a network path. Launching from inside a worktree not created under .claude/worktrees may decline.

facts.feature: Worktree creation safety: git filter drivers and refusal checks
facts.behavior: Claude Code skips the repository's own filter drivers (e.g. `git lfs install --local`) when creating a worktree, so LFS files are pointer files until `git lfs pull`. In four cases it creates no worktree (cannot read .git/config, filter name with '=' or newline, conditional includeIf in repo config, or repo config sets an LFS program key). Refuses (`Refusing to use <path> as an isolation worktree`) a directory whose git metadata resolves into the main checkout.
facts.limits: Global-config LFS installs are unaffected. Refused directory is left in place.

facts.feature: What worktrees share with main checkout
facts.behavior: Share the main repo's `.git` directory (sandbox allows these writes so `git commit` works in a worktree). Project-scope plugins load in worktrees (v2.1.200+). 'Yes, and don't ask again' Bash approvals in a worktree save to the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json (v2.1.211+). If the worktree has no .claude/skills (also agents, commands) the main checkout's load.
facts.limits: On Windows and where Claude Code doesn't use the repo root, the rule stays with the worktree. Desktop-app worktree sessions read settings, hooks, skills, agents, commands, .mcp.json from the main checkout root; CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules still load from the worktree.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (What worktrees share with the main checkout)

facts.behavior: Use `git worktree add ../project-feature-a -b feature-a` (new branch) or `git worktree add ../project-bugfix fix-issue-456` (existing branch) to check out a specific existing branch or place the worktree outside the repo; then run `claude` inside.
facts.limits: Worktrees you create yourself are never swept. Isolation enforcement applies to sessions isolated in a worktree, including resumed ones.

facts.feature: WorktreeCreate / WorktreeRemove hooks and non-git VCS
facts.behavior: A WorktreeCreate hook replaces the default git worktree logic entirely, including placing worktrees outside .claude/worktrees/; for SVN, Perforce, Mercurial. Pair with WorktreeRemove. Also lets `/batch` run outside a git repository (v2.1.281+).
facts.limits: Hook must print the directory path; .worktreeinclude is not processed. A hook-created directory inside a repository is refused. Hook worktrees are never swept.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (Non-git version control; Replace worktree creation with a hook)

facts.behavior: Creates a tmux session for the worktree. Requires `--worktree`. Uses iTerm2 native panes when available; `--tmux=classic` for traditional tmux.
facts.limits: Only meaningful with --worktree.

facts.behavior: `claude rm <id>` removes a background session; removal can be refused over the session's worktree. The refusal prints the flag to pass: `--discard-unpushed <commit>@<worktree-id>` (v2.1.260+) discards a worktree with unpushed commits and those commits; `--force-remove-worktree <worktree-id>` (v2.1.268+) deletes a worktree directory git or the WorktreeRemove hook couldn't remove.

facts.feature: Auto mode classifier rules for git (Git Destructive)
