facts.limits: 'Most fetches' only; see tools-reference WebFetch behavior for exceptions.

facts.behavior: In an interactive session, shows the workspace trust dialog when started in an untrusted folder. Servers in a project's .mcp.json have their own approval prompt.
facts.limits: A -p session shows neither prompt. Starting in the home directory holds trust for the current session only (not written to disk; no setting to persist). Project scope lists sessions that skip the MCP prompt.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, Claude Code asks before running a Bash command it can't fully analyze. An allow rule for part of a command, such as Bash(git *), doesn't skip that prompt.
facts.limits: Manual mode; sandboxed commands can run without it.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, unmatched commands require approval by default.
facts.limits: Manual mode only.

facts.behavior: API keys and tokens are stored in the macOS Keychain when available. On Linux in a file with mode 0600, on Windows in a file that inherits the access controls of your user profile directory.
facts.limits: Covers Claude Code's own credentials; docs on this page do not describe scanning or redacting secrets in project files or prompts.

facts.behavior: Recommends against enabling WebDAV or allowing Claude Code to access paths such as \\* that may contain WebDAV subdirectories; WebDAV may let Claude Code trigger network requests to remote hosts, bypassing the permission system.
facts.limits: Windows only; guidance only.

facts.behavior: Review suggested commands before approval; avoid piping untrusted content directly to Claude; verify proposed changes to critical files; use VMs to run scripts and make tool calls, especially with external web services; report suspicious behavior with /feedback.
facts.limits: Docs say while protections significantly reduce risk, no system is completely immune to all attacks.

facts.behavior: Project-scoped MCP servers are defined in .mcp.json (can be checked in). Servers at other scopes, claude.ai connectors, and plugins are configured outside the repo, so reviewing .mcp.json doesn't show every server. MCP permissions are configurable. Managed MCP configuration restricts servers org-wide. Encourages own servers or trusted providers.
facts.limits: Anthropic reviews connectors against listing criteria before adding to the Directory but does not security-audit or manage any MCP server.

facts.behavior: Each cloud session runs in an isolated Anthropic-managed VM; network access limited by default and configurable (disabled or specific domains); GitHub credentials stored encrypted on Anthropic's servers and never enter the VM (short-lived session-scoped credential; GitHub traffic via Anthropic proxy); all operations audit-logged; session VMs reclaimed after inactivity; sessions deletable.
facts.limits: Self-hosted environments: isolation, egress, and git credentials are the deployment's responsibility. Cloud sessions do not load plugins from user settings or repo .claude/settings.json.

facts.behavior: The GitHub proxy rejects branch deletions and pushes of anything other than a branch, such as a tag. GitHub applies the repository's branch protection rules and rulesets to the GitHub access you connected.
facts.limits: Cloud sessions in Anthropic-hosted environments only. A rule that the connected access can bypass doesn't block a session's push.

facts.behavior: Web interface connects to a Claude Code process on your local machine; all code execution and file access stays local; traffic goes through the Anthropic API over TLS; uses multiple short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials. While connected, the session transcript is stored on Anthropic servers to sync across devices.
facts.limits: No cloud VMs or sandboxing involved.

facts.behavior: Review all suggested changes; use project-specific permission settings; run whole Claude Code process inside sandbox runtime or dev container; audit with /permissions; use managed settings to enforce org standards; share permission configs via version control; monitor via OpenTelemetry metrics; audit or block settings changes during sessions with ConfigChange hooks.
facts.limits: Recommendations; ConfigChange hooks and managed settings require setup.

facts.behavior: Report Claude Code vulnerabilities via HackerOne, do not disclose publicly, include reproduction steps.
facts.limits: Process guidance.

facts.behavior: On-demand single security pass over the changes on your current branch.
facts.limits: Covers only changes on the current branch; reads source in checkout, not a running site or deployed service; run when you ask.

facts.behavior: Plugin makes Claude review its own code changes for common vulnerabilities (injection, unsafe deserialization, unsafe DOM APIs) while it works and fix findings in the same session. Runs automatically once installed. Installed via /plugin install security-guidance@claude-plugins-official; can be enabled for a team via enabledPlugins in .claude/settings.json or managed settings.
facts.limits: Not built in: must be installed. Requires Python 3.7+ (3.10+ for agentic commit review and for all model-backed reviews on third-party providers); creates a venv under ~/.claude/security/ and installs Claude Agent SDK (needs pip and network). Not loaded in cloud sessions from user or repo settings. Available on all plans.

facts.behavior: When Claude writes to a file, scans new content for risky patterns (eval(, new Function, os.system, child_process.exec, pickle, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, .innerHTML =, document.write, edits under .github/workflows/). Pattern match with no model call, no usage cost. Runs after the edit lands and appends the warning to Claude's context; each warning fires once per pattern per file per session.
facts.limits: Does not block the edit. Works outside git repos. Fires on PostToolUse for Edit, Write, NotebookEdit only.

facts.behavior: After each turn, computes a git diff of everything changed in the working tree during the turn (edit tools, Bash, subagents) and sends it to a separate Claude security review in the background; if issues are found Claude is re-prompted with the findings. Catches authorization bypass, IDOR, injection, SSRF, weak crypto.
facts.limits: Covers up to 30 changed files per turn; fires at most three times in a row before yielding to you; skipped silently outside a git repo or without Anthropic auth/third-party provider; review model can miss issues; does not block writes.

facts.behavior: When Claude runs git commit or git push through its Bash tool, runs a deeper agentic review in the background that reads surrounding code (callers, sanitizers, related files).
facts.limits: Only commits/pushes Claude makes through Bash; commits from your own shell, including the ! shell escape, are not reviewed. Capped at 20 per rolling hour. Not re-prompted if findings duplicate the end-of-turn review. Does not block commits. Needs git repo.

facts.behavior: End-of-turn and commit reviews run as a separate Claude call with fresh context and a security-focused prompt; per-edit check is deterministic string match.
facts.limits: None of the layers block writes or commits; findings reach the writing Claude as instructions; treat as one layer of defense in depth.

facts.behavior: Markdown file claude-security-guidance.md loaded as additional context for the model-backed reviews. Locations: ~/.claude/claude-security-guidance.md (user), .claude/claude-security-guidance.md (project), .claude/claude-security-guidance.local.md (local); all existing are concatenated.
facts.limits: Combined cap of 8 KB. Additive only: a rule saying to ignore a vulnerability class does not suppress findings. Guidance for the reviewer, not deterministic guardrails; for hard enforcement use a hook that blocks the edit or a CI check. Applies only to model-backed reviews.

facts.behavior: security-patterns.yaml (also .yml and .json) under .claude/ (and user-scope equivalent) adds regex or substring rules with rule_name, reminder (capped 1 KB), regex, substrings, paths, exclude_paths. Example: substrings sk_live_, AKIA flagged as hardcoded API key prefix.
facts.limits: Up to 50 custom rules; skips regexes prone to catastrophic backtracking; additive, cannot disable built-ins; YAML requires importable PyYAML (JSON works anywhere); warn only, not blocking; paths globs match full path so prefix with **/.

facts.behavior: Per-edit check costs nothing; end-of-turn and commit reviews spend usage. Both model-backed reviews use Claude Opus 4.7 by default; SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL sets end-of-turn model, SG_AGENTIC_MODEL sets commit review model.
facts.limits: Commit review may take several model turns per commit.

facts.behavior: ENABLE_PATTERN_RULES=0, ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0, ENABLE_COMMIT_REVIEW=0, ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW=0 (all model-backed), SECURITY_GUIDANCE_DISABLE=1 (entire plugin); /plugin disable or uninstall.
facts.limits: If enabled via managed settings only an administrator can disable it; project-enabled uninstall writes override to .claude/settings.local.json.

facts.behavior: Built on hooks: SessionStart (bootstrap venv), UserPromptSubmit (capture working-tree baseline), PostToolUse on Edit/Write/NotebookEdit, Stop (end-of-turn review), PostToolUse on Bash filtered to git commit/push. Diagnostics in ~/.claude/security/log.txt.
facts.limits: Reviews skip silently without git repo, without auth, or if PyYAML missing for yaml patterns.

facts.behavior: Defense in depth: security-guidance plugin (in session), /security-review (on demand, single pass), Claude Security plugin (multi-agent repo or diff scan), Code Review (on PRs, Team and Enterprise plans), and your own CI static analysis/dependency scanners.
facts.limits: Plugin is not a guarantee and does not replace later checks; reviews read source, not running services.

facts.behavior: Consumer (Free, Pro, Max): choice to allow data to be used to improve future models; Anthropic trains when setting is on (including Claude Code use). Commercial (Team, Enterprise, API, 3rd-party platforms, Claude Gov): Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms, unless customer opts in (e.g. Developer Partner Program).
facts.limits: Development Partner Program is first-party API only, not Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform.

facts.behavior: Consumer: 5 years if data use for improvement allowed, 30 days if not. Commercial (Team, Enterprise, API): standard 30 days; zero data retention available to qualified accounts for Claude Code on Claude for Enterprise.
facts.limits: ZDR not in standard Enterprise plan; enabled per organization by account team. Cloud sessions can be deleted, permanently removing event data.

facts.behavior: Claude Code clients store session transcripts locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default to enable resumption. Adjust with cleanupPeriodDays.
facts.limits: Plaintext, so secrets that appear in a session sit on disk. Transcripts of sessions started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork are exempt from that limit by default. See claude-directory#application-data.

facts.feature: Data in transit and at rest
facts.behavior: Data sent includes all user prompts and model outputs, encrypted in transit via TLS 1.2+. At rest: Anthropic API AES-256 disk encryption (ZDR for no server-side persistence); Bedrock AES-256 with AWS keys (KMS CMK available); Google Cloud's Agent Platform Google-managed keys (CMEK available); Foundry depends on hosting option.
facts.limits: Compatible with most VPNs and LLM proxies.

facts.behavior: Repo cloned into the session's isolated VM; Anthropic stores the session transcript; all outbound traffic goes through a security proxy for audit logging and abuse prevention; prompts, code changes, outputs follow same data policies as local. Claude accesses only the repository where the session is initiated, not connected-but-unused repos.
facts.limits: Self-hosted environments: see self-hosted-environments#what-stays-on-your-infrastructure.

facts.behavior: Latency, reliability, and usage patterns sent to Anthropic and third-party logging infrastructure over TLS. Metrics never include your code, prompts, or file paths. Opt out with DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1.
facts.limits: Default on only for Claude API; default off on Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS (unless CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST set). DISABLE_TELEMETRY also disables feature-flag evaluation, which can make Remote Control unavailable.

facts.behavior: Error messages and stack traces from Claude Code internals sent to a third-party error tracker over TLS; known patterns of secrets, file paths, emails, and other personal info are redacted before leaving the machine. Opt out with DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1.
facts.limits: On only when signed in with Pro or Max, v2.1.198+, connecting directly to Claude API, and no ZDR/HIPAA agreement. Redaction is of known patterns only.

facts.behavior: Disables all non-essential traffic at once, including surveys, telemetry, and feature-flag evaluation.
facts.limits: Does not affect the WebFetch domain safety check or official plugin marketplace auto-install (opt-outs: skipWebFetchPreflight; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL). All env vars can be set in settings.json.

facts.behavior: Sends a copy of conversation history including code to Anthropic; user chooses current session only (default) or also other sessions from the same project over last 24h or 7 days. Encrypted in transit, stored in Google Cloud Storage; optionally creates a GitHub issue in the public repo. Transcripts retained 5 years. Opt out with DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1.
facts.limits: On third-party providers or no Anthropic credentials, writes to local archive ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ instead (known API key/token patterns redacted). Claude-drafted feedback (SendFeedback tool) queues locally and sends nothing until the user chooses to send; same path and retention.

facts.behavior: Rating prompt records only the rating; no transcripts. Optional follow-up 'Can Anthropic look at your session transcript?': Yes uploads conversation transcript, subagent transcripts, and raw session log (known API key/token patterns redacted; source code and file contents uploaded as-is; retained up to 6 months); No/Don't ask again send nothing. Not used for training.
facts.limits: Never shown for ZDR orgs, where feedback disabled by policy, or with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC. On Bedrock/Agent Platform/Foundry/Claude apps gateway, Yes writes to ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ locally. Disable with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1 (also disabled by DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DO_NOT_TRACK); feedbackSurveyRate setting (0 to 1) controls frequency; CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY_FOR_OTEL=1 opts ratings back in to the OTel collector only.

facts.behavior: Error reporting, telemetry, and bug reporting disabled by default on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS. Surveys and WebFetch domain safety check run regardless of provider. Signed-in Claude apps gateway sessions have usage analytics, error reporting, and survey ratings disabled by the gateway credential, with no setting to re-enable.
facts.limits: Provider env vars (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX/BEDROCK/FOUNDRY/ANTHROPIC_AWS) must be 1.

facts.behavior: Before fetching a URL, WebFetch sends only the requested hostname (not URL, path, or contents) to api.anthropic.com to check a safety blocklist. Passing hostnames cached five minutes; blocked or failed hostnames re-checked next request.
facts.limits: Runs regardless of provider; not affected by CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC. If api.anthropic.com is blocked, WebFetch fails until allowlisted or skipWebFetchPreflight: true is set; disabling means WebFetch attempts any URL without the blocklist, so pair with WebFetch permission rules.

area: Checkpointing and rewind of file edits

facts.behavior: Checkpointing automatically captures the state of your code before each prompt you send that starts a turn. Every such prompt creates a new checkpoint. Tracks all changes made by Claude's file editing tools.
facts.limits: Only prompts that start a turn get a checkpoint; messages typed mid-turn get none of their own.

facts.behavior: Claude Code keeps file snapshots for the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session. Discarding an older checkpoint deletes snapshot files no remaining checkpoint references, except each file's first snapshot (used by the VS Code extension as baseline for session diffs).
facts.limits: Older than 100 checkpoints cannot be restored.

facts.behavior: Claude Code saves checkpoints with the conversation, so you can still run /rewind after you resume a session.
facts.limits: Subject to the snapshot retention sweep.

facts.behavior: Claude Code deletes a session's file snapshots in the retention sweep, by default about 30 days after the session last saved one. Rewinding to a checkpoint whose snapshots are gone can fail with 'No files were restored'. Set cleanupPeriodDays to keep snapshots longer.
facts.limits: Default about 30 days; configurable only via cleanupPeriodDays.

facts.behavior: Run /rewind, or press Esc twice when the prompt input is empty, to open the rewind menu listing prompts sent in the session. Select a point, then choose an action.
facts.limits: If the prompt input contains text, double Esc clears it instead (saved to input history; Up recalls it).

facts.behavior: Revert both code and conversation to that point.
facts.limits: Code-restore options appear only when the selected checkpoint has tracked file changes to revert; otherwise only Restore conversation, summarize options and Never mind are offered. Subject to the tracking limits below.

facts.behavior: Rewind to that message while keeping current code. The original prompt is restored into the input field to re-send or edit.
facts.limits: Does not touch files.

facts.behavior: Revert file changes while keeping the conversation.
facts.limits: Only for tracked file edits; see limitations.

facts.feature: Summarize from here / Summarize up to here
facts.behavior: Summarize from here compresses the conversation from this point forward into a summary, freeing context window space. Summarize up to here compresses the conversation before this point, keeping later messages intact. A 'Summarized conversation' marker appears. Like a targeted /compact; stays in the same session. Optional instructions can guide the summary (type at 'add context (optional)'; number key summarizes immediately).
facts.limits: Does not change files on disk; original messages stay in the session transcript. To branch and preserve the original session use /branch or claude --continue --fork-session.

facts.feature: Rewound messages can return on exit
facts.behavior: If you exit before sending another prompt after rewinding, the rewound messages can return. To remove them again run /rewind and select the same prompt, then Restore conversation. Sending a prompt before exit makes Claude Code save the rewound conversation.
facts.limits: Files you restored stay as the rewind left them.

facts.behavior: If you ran /clear earlier in the same Claude Code process, the rewind menu shows an entry at the top '/resume <session-id> (previous session)' to resume the pre-clear conversation.
facts.limits: Available only until you exit Claude Code or resume a different session.

facts.behavior: Checkpointing does not track files modified by Bash commands (e.g. rm, mv, cp). Only direct file edits made through Claude's file editing tools are tracked.
facts.limits: Bash-made file modifications cannot be undone through rewind.

facts.behavior: Claude Code usually doesn't capture subagent edits in session checkpoints. A foreground forked skill (context: fork, background: false) edits the working tree during your own turn, so rewind restores it as usual. For any other subagent, rewinding restores only files Claude had already edited in your conversation; the subagent's edits to other files stay, so use git to revert them. Includes background forked skills (the default) and a background /code-review --fix run.
facts.limits: Subagent edits to files not already edited in the conversation are not reverted.

facts.behavior: Checkpointing only tracks files edited within the current session. Manual changes outside Claude Code and edits from other concurrent sessions are normally not captured, unless they modify the same files as the current session.
facts.limits: Rewind may not preserve or revert outside edits predictably.

facts.behavior: A message typed while Claude was still working can be marked 'No code restore' in the rewind menu; edits after it count toward the prompt that started the turn. Selecting the prompt that started the turn and choosing Restore code reverts the whole turn's edits.
facts.limits: The marked message offers only Restore conversation, which leaves files as they are.

facts.feature: Symlinked and hard-linked paths not restored
facts.behavior: Restore code skips any tracked path that is a symlink or hard link and shows a 'Restored the code, but skipped N files' warning. Skipped files keep current contents. Debug log at ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt (via /debug) names skipped paths.
facts.limits: Examples: dotfile-manager symlinked configs, pnpm hard-linked files; recovery is to ask Claude to reverse the edit or edit manually.

facts.behavior: Checkpoints are designed for quick, session-level recovery. For permanent version history and collaboration, continue using version control such as Git for commits, branches, and long-term history.
facts.limits: Not a replacement for version control; docs describe no git integration (checkpoints are not commits and do not restore git state).

area: Anthropic best-practices and common-workflows guidance for Claude Code, and the /doctor prompt-audit

facts.behavior: "Run `/doctor prompt-audit` in a session. Claude looks for problems such as instructions written for older models, references to files or commands that don't exist, and files that contradict each other. You get a report of findings with proposed edits, and nothing in your files changes until you ask Claude to apply them." Default scope: CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md, plus the rules, skills, commands, subagents and output styles under .claude/ and ~/.claude/. Accepts a path to audit one file or directory (e.g. /doctor prompt-audit .claude/skills/deploy). Alias of /doctor is /checkup.
facts.limits: On-demand only; not run automatically, not a hook, not a CI gate. Report-only until the user asks to apply. Runs through the bundled /claude-api skill, so unavailable while that skill is off via skillOverrides or disableBundledSkills. Requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later. Docs do not list the specific patterns flagged beyond the three named problem classes.

facts.behavior: "Flag instructions written for older models in your prompts, skills, and tool descriptions and propose fixes as a diff." Invoked as /claude-api prompt-audit (the /claude-api subcommand list: migrate, upgrade, managed-agents-onboard, managed-agents-secure, prompt-audit, cost-optimize, build-eval, hillclimb, preserved-thinking-migration).
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.221 or later. Part of the bundled /claude-api skill for Claude API / Managed Agents projects (also auto-activates when code imports anthropic or @anthropic-ai/sdk). User-invoked, proposes a diff; does not run automatically.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md (Work on Claude API projects table) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands.md (/claude-api row)

facts.behavior: "Run a setup checkup that diagnoses installation, settings, extension, and CLAUDE.md problems and proposes fixes that Claude applies after you confirm." Covers installation health (duplicate installs, PATH, unparseable settings, newer version), extensions (unused skills/MCP servers/plugins vs context cost, slow hooks), CLAUDE.md files (local duplicates of checked-in ones, checked-in content Claude could derive from the codebase, always-loaded guidance Claude offers to migrate into skills and nested CLAUDE.md), permissions (offer to make auto mode default and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands), usage (changes /usage recommends, last 7 days). Also lists duplicate subagent names in one directory and gives an estimate of skill-listing context cost.
facts.limits: Claude reports findings first and asks confirmation before changing anything. Usage check needs v2.1.305+, applies to Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, and is omitted while Remote Control is connected. Not automatic.

facts.behavior: CLI help: "Check the health of your Claude Code installation. Reads settings files in the current directory without a trust prompt. For a full checkup that can also fix issues, run /doctor in a session." Prints read-only installation and settings diagnostics without starting a session; lists invalid settings (e.g. array matcher in hooks); Search line shows ripgrep path or 'OK (bundled)'.
facts.limits: Read-only, no fixes, takes only -h/--help. Shows Search as OK even when WSL search is slow/incomplete.

facts.feature: Best-practices: context window is the core constraint
facts.behavior: "Claude's context window fills up fast, and performance degrades as it fills." "The context window is the most important resource to manage." Suggests tracking usage with a custom status line.
facts.limits: Guidance only; not enforced.

facts.feature: Best-practices: give Claude a way to verify its work
facts.behavior: "Give Claude a check it can run: tests, a build, a screenshot to compare." Options by gating strength: ask in one prompt; set a /goal condition (separate evaluator re-checks after every turn); a Stop hook that "blocks the turn from ending until it passes"; a verification subagent or dynamic workflow so a fresh model tries to refute the result. Have Claude show evidence (test output, command and result, screenshot). Recommends running /verify yourself after Claude's check passes.
facts.limits: Only the Stop hook is a deterministic gate (with a cap on consecutive blocks); /goal can be stopped by Claude Code if Claude stalls; the rest is prompt guidance.

facts.behavior: /run launches and drives the app; /verify "Build and run your app to confirm a code change does what it should, without falling back to tests or type checks"; /run-skill-generator records a launch recipe as .claude/skills/run-<name>/. /verify records its own recipe to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md at repo root (or touched package dir in a monorepo); at repo root the recorded skill replaces bundled /verify. Claude edits the recorded file only when it steered a run wrong.
facts.limits: Inference of launch is unreliable for projects needing a database, env file, graphical session or multi-step build.

facts.feature: Best-practices: explore, plan, then code (plan mode)
facts.behavior: Four phases: explore, plan, implement, commit. Plan mode via Shift+Tab until status bar shows '⏸ plan mode on' or `claude --permission-mode plan`: "Claude reads files and answers questions without making changes." Ctrl+G opens the plan in a text editor. "If you could describe the diff in one sentence, skip the plan." Planning most useful when uncertain, multi-file, or unfamiliar code.
facts.limits: Plan mode adds overhead; docs say skip it for small clear fixes. Plan mode itself blocks edits until approval (permission mode); the 'when to use it' guidance is advisory.

facts.feature: Best-practices: provide specific context in prompts
facts.behavior: Scope the task, point to sources, reference existing patterns, describe the symptom. Use @ to reference files, paste images, give URLs (allowlist domains via /permissions), pipe data (`cat error.log | claude -p ...`), let Claude fetch via Bash/MCP. "Vague prompts can be useful when you're exploring."
facts.limits: Guidance only.

facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md is read at the start of every conversation. "Keep it concise. For each line, ask: 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' If not, cut it. Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions." Include: commands Claude can't guess, non-default style rules, test instructions, repo etiquette, architectural decisions, env quirks, gotchas. Exclude: things derivable from code, standard conventions, detailed API docs, frequently changing info, long tutorials, file-by-file descriptions, self-evident practices. Domain knowledge only sometimes relevant belongs in skills. Emphasis ("IMPORTANT") on a single line that gets skipped; emphasizing many lines dilutes all. Check into git. /init generates starter. /context confirms loading. 'If Claude already does something correctly without the instruction, delete it or convert it to a hook.' For a checked-in CLAUDE.md, /doctor proposes cuts for content derivable from the codebase.
facts.limits: No required format. Memory docs: CLAUDE.md is 'context, not enforced configuration'.

facts.feature: Memory docs: instruction writing guidance (size, specificity, consistency)
facts.behavior: "Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence." Write instructions concrete enough to verify ("Use 2-space indentation" not "Format code properly"). Group under markdown headers and bullets. Contradictory instructions: "Claude may pick one arbitrarily"; review CLAUDE.md, nested CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ periodically. Move part-of-codebase instructions into path-scoped rules. Imports (@path, max depth four hops) organize but do not reduce context cost since imported files load at launch. Block-level HTML comments in CLAUDE.md are stripped before injection (preserved in code blocks).
facts.limits: Target is a recommendation, no enforcement. Subdirectory CLAUDE.md load on demand when Claude reads/writes/edits a file there, not at session start.

facts.behavior: Memory docs table: auto memory is loaded every session as "first 200 lines or 25KB". Scope: per repository, shared across worktrees.
facts.limits: Applies to the auto-memory index only, not CLAUDE.md files.

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md is advisory; hooks are deterministic
facts.behavior: "Unlike CLAUDE.md instructions which are advisory, hooks are deterministic and guarantee the action happens." "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook." Debug doc: "Permissions and hooks enforce limits regardless of what Claude decides. Use CLAUDE.md for 'we do it this way here.' Use permissions or hooks for security boundaries and anything that must never happen." Claude can write hooks for you; /hooks lists configured hooks.
facts.limits: Bash permission rules match the literal command string, not the underlying executable (Bash(rm *) does not block /bin/rm or find -delete); use PreToolUse hook or sandbox for hard guarantee.

facts.feature: Best-practices: permissions, auto mode, allowlists, sandboxing
facts.behavior: From v2.1.283 auto mode is the built-in starting permission mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions: "a separate classifier model reviews most actions instead of you and blocks only what looks risky, such as scope escalation, unknown infrastructure, or hostile-content-driven actions." Earlier versions: only on Pro, Max, Team. Manual mode asks before file writes, Bash, MCP. Permission allowlists (/permissions) and /sandbox cut prompts. `claude --permission-mode auto -p` for non-interactive; repeated classifier blocks in -p do not stop the run (falls back per permission-modes docs).
facts.limits: Classifier can block; thresholds in permission-modes page (not fetched).

facts.behavior: "CLI tools are the most context-efficient way to interact with external services" (gh, aws, gcloud, sentry-cli). Without gh unauthenticated API requests often hit rate limits. `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>` connects MCP servers.
facts.limits: Guidance only.

facts.behavior: SKILL.md in .claude/skills/<name>/ gives domain knowledge and reusable workflows; Claude applies automatically or user invokes /skill-name. `disable-model-invocation: true` for side-effect workflows triggered manually. Skill listing descriptions are budgeted at 1% of context window (skillListingBudgetFraction), each entry's combined description+when_to_use capped at 1,536 chars (skillListingMaxDescChars), least-invoked descriptions dropped first; warning in debug log. Skill content is added when invoked and not re-read; after compaction only the start of an invoked skill may be kept, so put key instructions near top.
facts.limits: A rule that must hold every time should be a hook, not a skill.

facts.behavior: "Show what each of your skills costs in context and how often it gets used"; flags skills never invoked and where to turn them off; lists unused plugins.
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.252+ and feature-flag fetching; excludes bundled and enterprise skills; not available over Remote Control.

facts.behavior: Subagents in .claude/agents/ run in own context with own tools; "Delegate research with 'use subagents to investigate X'" to keep main context clean. Subagent frontmatter example: name, description, tools, model. Subagent for verification/adversarial review: reviewer sees only diff and criteria. Built-in Explore and Plan agents skip CLAUDE.md at startup; custom subagents load it unless omitClaudeMd is set.
facts.limits: Reviewer prompted to find gaps will usually report some; docs advise telling it to flag only correctness/stated-requirement gaps to avoid over-engineering.

facts.behavior: "Before treating a task as done, have a subagent review the diff in a fresh context and report gaps." Bundled /code-review skill "reviews the current diff for bugs in a fresh subagent and returns findings to the session." Writer/Reviewer pattern across two sessions; fresh context avoids bias toward just-written code.
facts.limits: Guidance; not automatic.

facts.feature: Let Claude interview you / spec first
facts.behavior: For larger features, prompt Claude to interview using the AskUserQuestion tool and write SPEC.md, then start a fresh session to execute it. Best specs are self-contained: name files and interfaces, state out of scope, end with an end-to-end verification step.
facts.limits: Guidance only.

facts.behavior: Esc stops mid-action (context preserved); Esc+Esc or /rewind restores conversation and/or code or summarizes from a message; /clear resets context between unrelated tasks. "If you've corrected Claude more than twice on the same issue in one session... Run /clear and start fresh with a more specific prompt." Every prompt that starts a turn creates a checkpoint; files snapshotted before each change; checkpoints persist with the conversation across resume.
facts.limits: "Checkpoints only track changes made through Claude's file editing tools. Changes made through Bash commands or external processes are not captured. This isn't a replacement for git."

facts.behavior: "Claude Code automatically compacts conversation history when you approach context limits." /compact <instructions> for control; Summarize from here / up to here via /rewind; CLAUDE.md can carry compaction instructions (e.g. preserve modified files list and test commands); /btw asks side questions whose answer never enters conversation history. Troubleshooting: 'Autocompact is thrashing' error stops retries when context refills several times in a row; recover by reading smaller chunks, /compact with focus, subagent, or /clear. /compact can return 'Not enough messages to compact.'
facts.limits: Compaction summarizes lossy; thrashing stops retries automatically.

facts.behavior: Kitchen sink session (fix: /clear between unrelated tasks); correcting over and over (after two failed corrections /clear and rewrite prompt); over-specified CLAUDE.md (prune, or convert to hook); trust-then-verify gap ("If you can't verify it, don't ship it"); infinite exploration (scope narrowly or use subagents).
facts.limits: Guidance only; docs say patterns 'aren't set in stone' and intuition varies.

facts.behavior: `claude --continue` resumes most recent session in current directory (prints 'No conversation found to continue' if none); `claude --resume` or /resume picks from list; /rename names sessions; `claude --from-pr <n>` filters sessions linked to a PR (linked when Claude runs gh pr create or glab mr create).
facts.limits: Sessions saved locally.

facts.behavior: `claude --worktree <name>` creates an isolated git checkout on its own branch for a parallel session; Fan-out: /batch <instruction> splits a change across 5 to 30 subagents, each in its own worktree. Auto memory is shared across worktrees; a gitignored CLAUDE.local.md exists only in the worktree where created (share via an @~/ import). CLAUDE.md inside worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ has special handling (see worktrees doc).
facts.limits: Repository needs at least one commit (else 'Failed to resolve base branch "HEAD"'). Cleanup, .worktreeinclude, non-git VCS are in the worktrees page (not fetched).

facts.behavior: Worktrees, cross-session messaging, desktop app sessions, Claude Code in the cloud, agent view (`claude agents`, research preview), agent teams ("experimental and disabled by default"). Fresh-context reviewer improves review.
facts.limits: Agent view is a research preview; agent teams experimental, off by default.

facts.behavior: `claude -p` for CI, pre-commit hooks, scripts; --output-format json|stream-json (--verbose); piping works like Unix tool. "The run still creates a resumable session unless you pass --no-session-persistence." Fan-out loop uses --allowedTools and --permission-mode dontAsk, which denies anything else that would need approval; an installed mod can still approve some calls.
facts.limits: Test on 2-3 files before running all.

facts.behavior: @file includes the file content when within the Read tool token limit (25,000 tokens default); text file larger than 256KB isn't included. Directory references show listings, not contents. @ references add CLAUDE.md of the file's directory and parents to context. MCP resources via @server:resource. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS=1 (v2.1.299+, ignored in project and local settings) stops inclusion of contents/listings.
facts.limits: Size limits as stated.

facts.behavior: Options: cloud scheduled tasks/routines (claude.ai/code/routines; run when computer off; can trigger on API calls or GitHub events), desktop scheduled tasks, GitHub Actions, /loop (current CLI session; --resume/--continue restore unexpired fixed-interval loops). Prompt tip: "be explicit about what success looks like and what to do with results. The task runs autonomously, so it can't ask clarifying questions."
facts.limits: /loop only lives in the session; details on routines page not fetched.

facts.behavior: Claude Code works in any directory (notes vaults etc.); reads files fresh on each tool call. Claude answers capability questions from current documentation; /powerup gives interactive lessons.
facts.limits: Doc-based answers, not demonstrations.

facts.behavior: Recipes for codebase overview, finding code, fixing bugs (give repro command and stack trace), refactoring in small testable increments, tests (be specific; Claude matches existing test style), PRs ("Review Claude's generated PR before submitting"), documentation, images (drag, Ctrl+V paste, path).
facts.limits: Illustrative prompts; no enforcement.

facts.behavior: Use /compact; restart between tasks; ignore large build dirs; `claude --safe-mode` disables all customizations (CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP, custom commands/agents/output styles/keybindings) to isolate causes, managed hooks/settings still apply. Heap over 2.5GB shows a critical memory warning; /heapdump writes .heapsnapshot (contains full conversation and credentials) and -diagnostics.json to ~/Desktop (safe to attach only the diagnostics file). Markdown tables over 200 rows are truncated in display only. Bundled ripgrep issues: install system ripgrep and set USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0. /doctor, /mcp, /feedback, /context, /hooks, /debug, /status are listed diagnostic commands.
facts.limits: WSL cross-filesystem search returns fewer results while claude doctor reports Search OK. pbcopy/xclip fail inside sandbox; use /copy.

facts.feature: Debug your configuration: /context and common causes
facts.behavior: /context shows context breakdown by category (system prompt, tools, MCP, subagents, memory files, skills, messages); subdirectory CLAUDE.md files do not appear at session start. Adherence drops when instructions are vague, conflicting, or the file is long. Hook matcher is a case-sensitive single string ('Edit|Write'; comma separator only v2.1.191+); array matcher is listed as invalid setting and under PreToolUse/PermissionRequest none of that file's hooks load; hooks go under 'hooks' in settings.json, not ~/.claude.json; settings.json edits take effect in the running session after a brief delay.
facts.limits: Misspelled tool names in a matcher fail silently.

area: Tools reference, context window and compaction, prompt caching, and implications for instruction-file size and tool behavior

facts.behavior: The tool names are the exact strings you use in permission rules, subagent tool lists, and hook matchers. Rule format ToolName(specifier) is shared by permissions.allow/deny, --allowedTools/--disallowedTools, skill allowed-tools, and hook `if`. Hook matcher fields use bare tool names, not the parenthesized form.
facts.limits: Tools such as ExitPlanMode or ShareOnboardingGuide accept only a bare name. WebSearch takes no specifier.

facts.behavior: An Edit(...) allow rule also grants read access to the same path. A Read(...) deny rule also blocks Edit and Write on the same path, including creating a new file there.
facts.limits: Write's Read-deny check requires v2.1.228+. Edit(...) rules cover Edit, Write, NotebookEdit; Read(...) rules cover Read, Grep, Glob, LSP.

facts.behavior: Permission column shows whether tool prompts in Manual mode for paths inside the working directory. Read, Grep, Glob are No but still prompt outside working directory and additional directories. Bash is Yes but runs a built-in set of read-only commands without prompting. In auto mode a classifier decides most prompts.
facts.limits: Applies to Manual mode inside the working directory only.

facts.behavior: Spawns a subagent in a separate context window; parent sees only the final result, not intermediate tool calls. Launching doesn't itself prompt; the subagent's own tool calls are checked against permission rules. Claude Code runs subagents in the background by default apart from listed foreground cases. Background subagent permission prompts surface in the main session; Esc denies that one call.
facts.limits: maxTurns in subagent definition caps turns and marks result partial. If tools list matches nothing usable, Agent returns an error instead of launching. tools+disallowedTools: disallowedTools wins. A tool not available to subagents is never granted even if listed.

facts.behavior: Neither field set: inherits every tool available to subagents. tools only: only those. disallowedTools only: every parent tool except those. Both: disallowedTools takes precedence.
facts.limits: Limited to the tools available to subagents. SubagentHandback is added in auto mode for local non-fork subagents (v2.1.271+) regardless of tools/disallowedTools. Subagents never get EndConversation. Subagents get Task tools only when the session has them.

facts.behavior: Each command runs in a separate process. cd in the main session carries over only inside the project dir or added working directories; otherwise reset to project dir with 'Shell cwd was reset to <dir>'. Env vars don't persist. Aliases/functions from ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile are sourced at session start and applied to every Bash command.
facts.limits: Subagent sessions never carry over cwd changes. CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR=1 disables carry-over. Persist env vars via CLAUDE_ENV_FILE or a SessionStart hook.

facts.behavior: Claude manages the timeout parameter per call; default two minutes, ceiling ten minutes (BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS). You never set a per-command timeout. A foreground command that hits timeout is moved to the background instead of stopped, unless it starts with sleep.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 or bare mode disables auto-backgrounding so the command stops instead. cd inside a moved command doesn't carry over.

facts.behavior: Output streamed to a working file; a command whose output passes 5 GB is killed. Valid result: inline up to roughly 30,000 characters by default, past that a file path (truncated past 64 MiB) plus a preview of up to first 2,000 characters. Failure: inline up to roughly 10,000 characters, head-and-tail excerpt, no file path.
facts.limits: BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH sets read-back window, default 30,000, hard ceiling 150,000; doesn't raise inline ceilings. bashOutputMaxChars setting up to 128,000 sizes both (v2.1.261+). Exit 1 counts as valid only for grep, rg, egrep, fgrep, find, diff, test, [, git diff, git grep; any other exit 1 (pgrep, jq -e, cmp) counts as failure.

facts.feature: Bash background commands and time limit
facts.behavior: Claude can set run_in_background: true; list and stop via /tasks. A command from a foreground subagent stops when that subagent ends; main-conversation or background-subagent commands keep running after a final response. Unattended sessions (-p, Agent SDK, CI, cloud) have a time limit: 30 minutes default, max 2 hours (10 minutes default in -p with text prompt).
facts.limits: No time limit in local terminal, desktop, or VS Code sessions. Time limit requires v2.1.285+; applied everywhere before v2.1.288. Raise via BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS above 1800000 or BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS above 7200000; cannot shorten.

facts.behavior: CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT (e.g. 4G) caps memory of Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands via a memory cgroup, one cap for all of a session's commands. Kernel kills a command that can't stay under it with no message naming the cap.
facts.limits: Linux and WSL only; v2.1.233+. Falls back to no cap if cgroup setup fails. Result held until relaunch. Permission-gating hooks are excluded from the cap.

facts.behavior: Exact string replacement (old_string/new_string), no regex or fuzzy matching. Checks: read-before-edit, exact match, uniqueness (longer context or replace_all: true). A file changed on disk after read can still be edited when old_string matches current content exactly and unambiguously and reading wouldn't prompt. A path matched by a Read deny rule is refused.
facts.limits: Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and older always require a prior read; newer models can edit an unread file when reading wouldn't need a permission prompt and Read is available. A PARTIAL view read doesn't count. A Bash view counts only for cat, nl, bat, batcat, head, tail, sed -n 'X,Yp', grep, egrep, fgrep, rg on one file with no pipes or redirects; zero-match searches don't count. Viewing a file this way also loads subdirectory CLAUDE.md and path-scoped rules.

facts.behavior: Edit and NotebookEdit refuse a file that isn't valid UTF-8 (Edit allows little-endian UTF-16 BOM) and leave it untouched; error tells Claude to use a shell command that keeps the encoding. Write can replace such a file unless new content contains U+FFFD, and saves as UTF-8.
facts.limits: Covers legacy encodings, binary files, invalid UTF-8 sequences.

facts.behavior: Creates a new file or overwrites an existing one with the full content provided; doesn't append or merge. For partial changes Claude uses Edit.
facts.limits: Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and older require a prior read to overwrite an existing file; newer models can overwrite an unread file under the same conditions as read-before-edit. Notebooks and PARTIAL-view files require the read on every model. New files need no read. Before v2.1.228 every model required the read. Bash viewing satisfies the requirement under Edit's rules.

facts.behavior: Returns file contents with line numbers; Claude is instructed to always pass absolute paths. Handles images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP; resized/recompressed), PDFs (over 10 pages read in ranges, up to 20 pages at a time; needs pdftoppm), and .ipynb notebooks. Reads files only, not directories. Refuses binary extensions (.xlsx, .parquet, .heic, .zip); an @-mentioned refused file gives Claude only its path.
facts.limits: Image over 128 MB refused. Notebook over 256 KB of cells or token limit errors; notebook file over 100 MB refused. Empty file and offset-past-end return notices.

facts.behavior: One call returns at most 25,000 tokens by default (CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS) and refuses a whole file over 256 KB, so Claude reads larger files in pages with offset and limit. Whole file over token limit: first page with a PARTIAL view notice. Whole file over 256 KB, or offset/limit read over token limit: an error telling it to read a portion or use Grep. On v2.1.296+ Claude can set allow_large: true to read the whole file in one call, sized against remaining context window.
facts.limits: Images, PDFs and notebooks keep their limits. allow_large requires v2.1.296+.

facts.behavior: On macOS, Linux and WSL, Glob and Grep are left out of the default tool set; Claude searches with find and grep through Bash, which run embedded bfs and ugrep, and searches reach hooks and permission rules as Bash calls. On Windows they are in the default set. They return when named in --tools or --allowedTools at startup (naming either in --allowedTools restores both), when Bash is removed by deny rule/--disallowedTools/--restricted, or when a subagent lists them in tools without Bash.
facts.limits: An allow rule in a settings file does not restore them.

facts.behavior: Finds files by name pattern with ** recursion; results sorted by modification time and capped at 100 files, with a truncation flag. Doesn't respect .gitignore by default (CLAUDE_CODE_GLOB_NO_IGNORE=false makes it respect). Permission is decided before checking that the directory exists.
facts.limits: Null byte in pattern or path returns an error.

facts.behavior: Built on ripgrep with ripgrep regex syntax (not POSIX); respects .gitignore (pass the path directly to search an ignored file). Output modes files_with_matches (default), content, count. glob, type, multiline: true parameters. Rejected pattern returns ripgrep's diagnostic.
facts.limits: Before v2.1.208 a rejected input was reported as 'No files found'. Patterns match within a single line unless multiline.

facts.behavior: Code intelligence from a running language server; after each file edit it automatically reports type errors and warnings. Also definitions, references, type info, symbols, implementations, call hierarchies.
facts.limits: Inactive until a code intelligence plugin is installed; you install the server binary. Inactive in cloud sessions. Error result when the server can't start.

facts.behavior: Runs a command in the background and feeds each output line back to Claude; can open a WebSocket. Uses the same permission rules as Bash. Every watch has a deadline: 5 minutes default, max 30 minutes, max 10 minutes in -p single-prompt runs; one notice at deadline. In auto mode allow rules naming Monitor are set aside so the classifier reviews commands.
facts.limits: Not available on Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform or Foundry, nor when DISABLE_TELEMETRY or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC is set; on Windows needs Git Bash. WebSocket: text messages become events, binary replaced by placeholder, message over 1 MiB ends the watch, URLs to private/link-local/cloud-metadata addresses denied; opening a WebSocket prompts.

facts.behavior: Modifies Jupyter notebook one cell at a time by cell_id; modes replace (default), insert (needs cell_type), delete. Permission rules use Edit(...) path format.
facts.limits: No string replacement across the notebook; refuses non-UTF-8 notebooks.

facts.behavior: Runs PowerShell natively; enabled automatically on Windows without Git Bash, default on for claude.ai/Console accounts with Git Bash, opt-in on Linux/macOS/WSL (needs pwsh 7+). Match Bash|PowerShell in hooks that inspect shell commands. On Windows with Git Bash, any Bash deny rule (even scoped) turns PowerShell off without warning.
facts.limits: Preview: profiles not loaded; no sandboxing on Windows. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1 or a scoped PowerShell rule keeps it on alongside a Bash deny.

facts.behavior: Fetches a URL, converts HTML to Markdown, runs the prompt against content in a separate model call, and Claude receives that result rather than the raw page (lossy by design). Reads up to 100,000 characters per call; caches 15 minutes; 5-minute page deadline; HTTP upgraded to HTTPS; cross-host redirect returned as text, not followed. Prompts in Manual and acceptEdits modes except allowed/denied domains and preapproved documentation domains.
facts.limits: Refuses localhost and dotless hostnames (use curl via Bash). Explicit WebFetch(domain:) rules override the preapproved set. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH=1 turns it off (v2.1.285+). Team/Enterprise: withheld until org policy loads. Sandboxed commands don't inherit preapproved domains; WebFetch never reads the sandbox allowlist.

facts.behavior: Runs a query against Anthropic's web search backend and returns titles and URLs, not page contents; up to eight backend searches per call. allowed_domains or blocked_domains (not both). Permission rule is bare WebSearch only. Backend not configurable.
facts.limits: Interactive session cap of 200 calls (main conversation and subagents combined), refilling about 100/hour on v2.1.290+; /clear resets. In -p and Agent SDK the limit is per turn. Raise via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION (cannot be turned off). Not exposed on Amazon Bedrock.

facts.behavior: Asks multiple-choice questions; questions stay open until answered by default. askUserQuestionTimeout setting (60s, 5m, 10m) auto-closes an unanswered question and tells Claude the user may be away.
facts.limits: Timer never starts in background sessions, screen reader mode, or Remote Control sessions. Permission prompts incl. plan approval never auto-resolve on idle.

facts.behavior: Ends the session only as a last resort against sustained abuse or when explicitly demonstrated. Never prompts, PreToolUse hooks don't run for it, and deny/ask rules, --disallowedTools and --tools cannot remove it while other tools remain.
facts.limits: Appears only on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5 or later, interactive terminal sessions, not --bare, not cloud providers. Subagents never get it. Removed if deny rules remove every other tool and match it, unless explicitly allowed.

facts.behavior: Claude drafts feedback reports; drafts saved under ~/.claude/feedback/drafts/ and nothing is sent until the user chooses. At most three cards per session by default; queue holds 10 drafts; drafts expire after 30 days or cleanupPeriodDays if shorter. Off via feedbackDrafts setting or CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK=0.
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.238+. Omitted in -p, Agent SDK, cloud sessions, Bedrock/Platform on AWS/Vertex/Foundry, ZDR and HIPAA orgs. Sending from the card never includes the transcript.

facts.behavior: Task-tracking tools are provided by default only on Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and earlier models; on newer models they are left out because definitions and reminders take up context and Claude tracks multi-step work without a checklist. TodoWrite is disabled by default in favor of the Task tools; CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0 re-enables it.
facts.limits: Opt in via CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1, --allowedTools, or --tools. Background and cloud sessions provide them on every model. Applies in v2.1.268+. Unknown model IDs (gateway) treated as not-default. Subagents get them only if the session has them.

facts.behavior: TaskOutput was removed in v2.1.277; Claude reads a background task's output file with Read instead.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: EnterWorktree creates an isolated git worktree and switches into it, or with a path switches into an existing one. A path outside .claude/worktrees/ prompts for approval; new-worktree creation and paths under .claude/worktrees/ don't prompt. ExitWorktree returns to the original directory.
facts.limits: Prompt for outside paths since v2.1.206. From within a worktree session or a subagent with pinned working directory (isolation: worktree) only the path form exists and the target must be under .claude/worktrees/ of the session's repo. ExitWorktree unavailable to subagents already in their own working directory.

facts.behavior: Cron tools (CronCreate/Delete/List) are session-scoped, restored on --resume/--continue if unexpired. ScheduleWakeup reschedules a self-paced /loop one minute to one hour out. Skill runs a skill in the main conversation (skills add no new tool entries). ToolSearch loads deferred tools; WaitForMcpServers appears only when tool search is disabled. Workflow runs a dynamic workflow of subagents. Artifact, PushNotification, RemoteTrigger, SendUserFile need claude.ai/Anthropic-hosted infrastructure. ReportFindings renders code-review findings. SendMessage/ListAgents are cross-session (v2.1.224+).
facts.limits: Per-tool availability notes in the table; several not available on Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, Foundry. The advisor is a server tool with no name usable in permission rules or hook matchers.

facts.behavior: To check what's loaded, ask Claude directly (conversational summary); /mcp for exact MCP tool names.
facts.limits: No exact built-in tool listing command stated.

facts.feature: What loads before the first prompt
facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md, auto memory, MCP tool names, and skill descriptions all load into context before you type. AGENTS.md files can load in place of CLAUDE.md. Output style and --append-system-prompt text may add more. Path-scoped rules load alongside matching files as Claude reads them.
facts.limits: The page gives only representative token counts; it states no recommended CLAUDE.md size or line limit.

facts.behavior: After compaction: system prompt and output style still apply; project-root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules re-injected from disk; auto memory re-injected from disk; skill descriptions rebuilt and re-injected (v2.1.304+); git status snapshot refreshed if session started with one; plan-mode plan re-injected from disk; rules with paths: frontmatter and nested CLAUDE.md reloaded on demand; context hooks added earlier is summarized with the conversation; SessionStart hooks matching the compact source run and add output.
facts.limits: Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md load into message history, so compaction summarizes them away. 'If a rule must persist across compaction, drop the paths: frontmatter or move it to the project-root CLAUDE.md.'

facts.behavior: Claude Code re-reads up to five files Claude read or edited, most recently modified first. A file over 5,000 tokens comes back as a path reference ('Referenced file') without content.
facts.limits: Five files, 5,000 tokens each.

facts.behavior: Re-injected, capped at 5,000 tokens per skill and 25,000 tokens total; oldest dropped first. Truncation keeps the start of the file, so put the most important instructions near the top of SKILL.md.
facts.limits: Per-skill 5,000 and total 25,000 token caps.

facts.behavior: Background commands and background subagents keep running; Claude Code reminds Claude which are still running so it doesn't start a duplicate.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: As of v2.1.198 the summarization request inherits the session's extended thinking configuration.
facts.limits: Affects only summary production; session settings unchanged.

facts.behavior: Claude Code compacts automatically as you approach the limit, so a full context doesn't end the session. Manual options: /compact [focus instructions], /rewind then Summarize from here/up to here, /autocompact <tokens> (e.g. 500k) to set when the automatic pass runs, /clear between tasks, delegate large reads to subagents. Idle compaction can compact a conversation you leave idle (idleCompaction setting, v2.1.290+).
facts.limits: Threshold depends on model and configuration (model-config 'Default auto-compact thresholds'; not on these pages). 1M window supported on Fable models, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.6 and later, Sonnet 4.6.

facts.behavior: /context shows a live breakdown by category with optimization suggestions, including which CLAUDE.md and auto memory files loaded. /memory opens and edits those files.
facts.limits: The visualization uses representative numbers, not real ones.

facts.behavior: A subagent handles research in its own context window so large file reads stay out of yours; only the summary and a small metadata trailer come back.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: Prompt cache layout and prefix matching
facts.behavior: Each request re-sends the full context; the API caches by exact prefix match, so a change anywhere in the prefix recomputes everything after it. Order: system prompt (core instructions, tool definitions; changes when set of loaded tool definitions changes), project context (CLAUDE.md, auto memory, unscoped rules; changes at session start, /clear, /compact), conversation (every turn). A system prompt change invalidates everything.
facts.limits: No per-file or per-segment caching. Plan mode and skill loading append as conversation messages so prefix stays intact.

facts.behavior: Project-root and user-level CLAUDE.md are read once at session start and held in memory. Editing mid-session does not invalidate the cache, but the edit also doesn't apply; new content loads on next /clear, /compact, or restart.
facts.limits: Nested CLAUDE.md and paths: rules load on demand; editing one before it loads takes effect, after load it is conversation history and a mid-session edit doesn't change it.

facts.behavior: Each model has its own cache; /model switch means the next request reads the whole history with no cache hits. /model at the terminal asks to confirm only while the cache is warm (one TTL) and the new model isn't the last responder; PreModelSwitch hook can require or skip confirmation. opusplan toggles, automatic model fallback, and a skill/command frontmatter model that differs are also model switches.
facts.limits: Before v2.1.238 it asked even after cache expiry. Skill-frontmatter model switch lasts that turn; context: fork skill sets the forked subagent's model instead.

facts.behavior: On most models changing effort mid-session invalidates the cache; Claude Code asks to confirm while cache is warm. On Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 with API key or Claude subscription, changing effort keeps the cache and applies without asking.
facts.limits: Exception doesn't apply on Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, a Claude apps gateway, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS, or HIPAA orgs. Before v2.1.260 Fable 5.1 also invalidated.

facts.behavior: Enabling fast mode adds a request header that is part of the cache key, so the first fast-mode request misses the whole cache; cost applies once per conversation. Turning it off, fallback to standard speed, and turning it back on keep the cache. /clear and /compact reset this.
facts.limits: If the model doesn't support fast mode, enabling it also switches model.

facts.behavior: Tool definitions sit in the system prompt layer, so cache invalidates when the set of definitions changes. With tool search deferring MCP tools (default on supported models) Claude Code keeps the first request's tool list for the whole conversation and a mid-session server change doesn't disturb the cache. With tools loaded upfront: server connect/dynamic tool add invalidates; stdio server dropping keeps cache; remote reconnect keeps it unless WaitForMcpServers is added once; removing a tool on purpose (deny rule, disabling in /mcp) invalidates.
facts.limits: Advisor toggle (/advisor) keeps the cache. Editing MCP config doesn't change the cache; takes effect after restart. Tool search off/unavailable on Vertex earlier than Opus 4.5/Sonnet 4.5/Haiku 4.5 and Azure-hosted Foundry that rejects it.

facts.behavior: A plugin's skills, commands, agents, hooks, monitors, themes never invalidate the cache; content is appended after the conversation. Plugin MCP servers follow MCP rules. Changes go through /reload-plugins; if the reload would trigger a full re-read it shows a warning and doesn't apply, and /reload-plugins --force applies it. Disabling a plugin enabled earlier restores the previous request shape, reading older cache if within TTL.
facts.limits: /reload-plugins in non-interactive sessions needs v2.1.260+ and doesn't apply plugin MCP server changes; --plugin-dir auto-apply needs v2.1.265+.

facts.feature: Deny rule for an entire tool and cache
facts.behavior: A bare tool-name deny (Bash, WebFetch, Bash(*), or tool-name glob like "*" or "mcp__*") removes the tool from the next request; with tool search active the definitions don't change and cache survives, otherwise the definition is removed and the cache invalidated (also when the rule is removed).
facts.limits: Scoped deny rules like Bash(rm *) and all allow/ask rules don't change which tools Claude sees; checked at call time, prefix intact.

facts.behavior: Compaction replaces history with a summary, invalidating the conversation layer by design; reuses the system prompt layer; reloads project context from disk, which cache-hits only if CLAUDE.md and memory are unchanged since session start. The summarization request uses the same system prompt, tools and history plus an appended instruction, so while the cache is warm it reads the prefix from cache. After a gap longer than the cache lifetime the summarization reprocesses full history uncached (costliest when resuming an old session). Docs advise running /compact at natural breaks rather than letting auto-compaction trigger mid-task.
facts.limits: First compaction after a resumed session that kept an older system prompt switches to the current prompt and rebuilds that layer once. /rewind truncates to an already-cached prefix and keeps cache.

facts.behavior: If a long conversation is idle on the one-hour TTL, Claude Code can compact it shortly before the cache expires.
facts.limits: Turn off with idleCompaction: false; requires v2.1.290+.

facts.behavior: When the next request would pass the API's image/PDF count limits or Claude Code's total size cap, Claude Code removes a batch of the oldest images and PDFs from what it sends; Claude can no longer see them. The next request reprocesses from the earliest changed message onward.
facts.limits: One slower turn per batch; share the image again if needed.

facts.behavior: A new version typically updates system prompt or tool definitions, so the first conversation after an upgrade builds its cache from the top. Auto-update applies on next launch, never mid-session; DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 controls when upgrades apply.
facts.limits: A resumed conversation keeps its original system prompt by default; the change takes effect after compaction or a new conversation.

facts.behavior: Editing repository files (appends a system-reminder noting the file changed), editing CLAUDE.md mid-session, changing permission mode, changing output style (delivered as a message; applies from next message since v2.1.251), invoking skills and commands (injected as user messages), /recap, /rewind, and spawning a subagent all keep the cache.
facts.limits: Exceptions: opusplan plan-mode toggle and skills/commands with a different model frontmatter are model switches.

facts.behavior: Main conversation (interactive turns, -p, Agent SDK) vs everything else (subagents, workflows, in-process teammates, forks, compaction, session titles). Claude subscription within plan usage: main conversation one hour, everything else five minutes except server-controlled helper requests at one hour. Usage credits, API key or cloud provider: five minutes for both. Over plan usage on subscription drops main to five minutes.
facts.limits: One-hour TTL not available through the Claude apps gateway; Bedrock support varies by model; LLM gateways must forward the anthropic-beta header.

facts.behavior: promptCacheTtl / CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL (main), subagentPromptCacheTtl / CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL (everything else), values 5m or 1h only. Precedence: FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1, bucket env var, bucket setting, subagent experimental cacheTtl frontmatter (v2.1.248+), ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1, default. Verify with claude -p "hello" --output-format json and usage.cache_creation.
facts.limits: Requires v2.1.242+. FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M overrides managed settings.

facts.behavior: Effectively scoped to one machine and directory: the system prompt embeds auto memory paths and the conversation opens with working directory, platform, shell, OS version. Parallel sessions in the same directory read each other's cache; sequential sessions share the prefix only when the startup git status snapshot matches.
facts.limits: Different directories miss each other's cache.

facts.behavior: A subagent starts its own conversation with its own system prompt and tools; its first request doesn't read the parent's cache and it warms its own. Parent's cache unaffected. A fork inherits the parent's system prompt, tools and history, so its first request reads the parent's cache. Workflow fan-outs hold all but the first agent up to 5 seconds so they read the first agent's cached prefix.
facts.limits: Subagents get five-minute TTL even on a subscription unless configured.

facts.behavior: /usage shows a 'Prompt cache (main)' line with hit ratio, miss count, warm state (v2.1.251+), and likely cause of last miss (v2.1.260+). Status line scripts read current_usage (cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens) and the prompt_cache object. OpenTelemetry exports cache tokens.
facts.limits: Likely-cause text only when Claude Code can identify one.

facts.behavior: Env vars set to 1: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING (all), DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU/SONNET/OPUS/FABLE (default model of that alias only). Can go in managed settings env block. Docs: for normal use leave caching enabled.
facts.limits: SONNET/OPUS vars apply only to the model the alias resolves to; other pinned model IDs keep caching. HAIKU covering main conversation needs v2.1.283+.

facts.behavior: Claude Code marks a mid-conversation system-context block (e.g. file-change notices) for caching. If a gateway rejects with 400 naming cache_control, Claude Code moves the marker onto the last conversation message for the rest of the process. If a gateway strips markers while succeeding, the whole history bills uncached every turn.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS sends that block uncached.

facts.behavior: Neither the context-window nor prompt-caching page states a size cap, line limit, or warning for CLAUDE.md or rule files. Implications stated: CLAUDE.md, auto memory and unscoped rules load every session and are re-injected from disk after compaction (cost on every message); path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md load on demand and are lost to compaction summary; /clear is advised because old conversation 'costs tokens on every message'.
facts.limits: Size limits, if any, live on other pages (memory, best-practices, costs) not fetched here. No native warning on instruction-file length is documented on these three pages.
